title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子所雅言詩書執禮皆雅言也
劉大章
同考試官教諭袁　批〔雅言無非至教此作敘述赤〕
〔予垂訓事實而詞不浮泛宜錄以式〕
考試官學正王　批〔說理精切遣詞雅暢〕
考試官教授馮　批〔結說易與春秋尤完健〕
聖人之所常言無非道之切于人者也夫詩也
===
書也執禮也皆道之切于日用而不可離者聖
人常言之也有以哉記者之意蓋謂天下之道
固不待言而存而聖人之教亦必因言以顯吾
夫子欲無言矣乃其慮小子之何述而常不倦
於誨人明大道之為公而每無隱以垂訓不有
雅言者乎雅言維何溫柔敦厚詩教也諷詠之
意微而物理之情悉美刺之詞婉而勸懲之義
昭以理性情蓋取諸詩疏通知遠書教也平章
之治闡化於典謨經濟之圖宣猷於訓誥以道
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子所雅言，詩、書、執禮，皆雅言也。

劉大章

同考試官教諭袁批〔雅言無非至教，此作敘述赤〕〔予垂訓事實，而詞不浮泛，宜錄以式。〕
考試官學正王批〔說理精切，遣詞雅暢。〕
考試官教授馮批〔結說易與春秋，尤完健。〕

聖人之所常言，無非道之切于人者也。夫詩也，書也，執禮也，皆道之切于日用而不可離者，聖人常言之也，有以哉！記者之意，蓋謂天下之道，固不待言而存，而聖人之教，亦必因言以顯。吾夫子欲無言矣，乃其慮小子之何述，而常不倦於誨人；明大道之為公，而每無隱以垂訓。不有雅言者乎？雅言維何？溫柔敦厚，詩教也。諷詠之意微，而物理之情悉；美刺之詞婉，而勸懲之義昭。以理性情，蓋取諸詩。疏通知遠，書教也。平章之治，闡化於典謨；經濟之圖，宣猷於訓誥。以道
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“The subjects of which the Master regularly spoke were the Odes, the Documents, and the practice of ritual. Of all these he regularly spoke.”

Liu Dazhang

Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: “The Master's regular discourse was invariably the highest instruction. This composition recounts the actual circumstances of [the Master's?] imparting instruction [the transcription 赤予 is doubtful], and its language is neither superficial nor vague. It should be included as a model.”
Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “Its exposition of principle is precise and incisive; its language is elegant and fluent.”
Examiner Feng, Professor, comments: “The concluding discussion of the Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals is especially complete and vigorous.”

What the sage regularly spoke of was invariably that aspect of the Way which closely concerns human beings. The Odes, the Documents, and the practice of ritual all embody the Way as it bears closely upon daily life and cannot be dispensed with. Surely there was good reason for the sage to speak of them regularly!

The recorder's meaning, it would seem, is that although the Way of the world exists without depending upon words, the sage's teaching must nevertheless be made manifest through words. Our Master wished to remain silent; yet, concerned about what his disciples would then have to transmit, he remained tireless in instructing others. Understanding that the great Way belongs to all, he withheld nothing when imparting his teaching. Did he not have subjects of which he regularly spoke? What were these subjects?

Gentleness and kindness, sincerity and generosity: these are the teaching of the Odes. The meaning conveyed through recitation and chanting is subtle, yet fully encompasses the true nature of things and their principles. The language of praise and criticism is tactful, yet its purpose of encouragement and admonition is clear. To bring human nature and feelings into proper order, he drew upon the Odes.

Breadth of understanding and knowledge of the distant past: these are the teaching of the Documents. The governance that brings order and harmony unfolds its transforming influence in the Canons and Counsels; plans for ordering the world and aiding the people proclaim their guiding principles in the Instructions and Announcements. To guide…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
政事蓋取諸書恭儉莊敬禮教也中正立其防
義非徒於誦說儀文章其軌道可緣以持循以
謹節文蓋取諸執禮詩也書也切於日用均之
爲夫子之常言是故言修齊於二南正始也言
孝友於君陳論政也立言爲訓匪詩則書蓋不
但刪述之勞而庸言所及雖三復不以爲煩矣
禮之執也裨於身心敷之爲聖門之彝訓是故
言儉戚於林放崇本也言學立於伯魚敦教也
吐詞爲經匪詩則禮蓋不特損益之究而恒言
===
爲教雖再三不以爲瀆矣噫孔門循循之教切
已之學固如此雖然夫子之道在六經易陳天
道春秋紀時事而雅言不及豈不以易之精微
雖夫子猶俟於假年而春秋隱義游夏不能贊
一詞者乎學者由詩書以探其深約禮以通其
變則天人之理一以貫之易春秋在其中矣
誠則形形則著著則明
張翊
同考試官教諭黃　批〔形著明雖發外之盛而未〕
punctuated:
政事，蓋取諸書。恭儉莊敬，禮教也。中正立其防，義非徒於誦說；儀文章其軌道，可緣以持循，以謹節文，蓋取諸執禮。詩也，書也，切於日用，均之爲夫子之常言。是故言修齊於二南，正始也；言孝友於君陳，論政也。立言爲訓，匪詩則書，蓋不但刪述之勞，而庸言所及，雖三復不以爲煩矣。禮之執也，裨於身心，敷之爲聖門之彝訓。是故言儉戚於林放，崇本也；言學立於伯魚，敦教也。吐詞爲經，匪詩則禮，蓋不特損益之究，而恒言爲教，雖再三不以爲瀆矣。噫！孔門循循之教，切已之學，固如此。雖然，夫子之道在六經，易陳天道，春秋紀時事，而雅言不及，豈不以易之精微，雖夫子猶俟於假年，而春秋隱義，游夏不能贊一詞者乎？學者由詩書以探其深，約禮以通其變，則天人之理一以貫之，易春秋在其中矣。

誠則形，形則著，著則明。
張翊

同考試官教諭黃，批〔形著明，雖發外之盛，而未〕
translation_en:
…government affairs: for this, he drew upon the Book of Documents. Reverence, frugality, solemnity, and respect are the teaching of ritual. Centrality and correctness establish its safeguards; its principles are not merely a matter of recitation and exposition. Its ceremonial forms embellish the prescribed course [?], which one can follow and uphold. To observe its measured forms carefully, he drew upon the practice of ritual. The Book of Odes and the Book of Documents bear directly upon daily life, and both were among the Master's constant subjects of speech. Thus, when he spoke of cultivating oneself and ordering the family through the two “Southern” sections of the Odes, he was setting beginnings right; when he spoke of filial devotion and brotherly affection through “Jun Chen” in the Documents, he was discussing government. In establishing teachings through his words, he drew upon either the Odes or the Documents. His work was therefore not confined to editing and transmitting them: when they entered his everyday speech, he did not consider even three repetitions tiresome.

The practice of ritual benefits both body and mind; expounded, it becomes an enduring teaching of the sage's school. Thus, when he spoke to Lin Fang of frugality and grief, he was honoring fundamentals; when he spoke to Boyu of learning and establishing oneself, he was strengthening instruction. His utterances became authoritative standards, drawing upon either the Odes or ritual. His work was therefore not confined to investigating what should be removed or added: when his habitual words served as instruction, he did not consider repeated teaching an undue imposition. Ah! Such indeed were the orderly guidance of Confucius's school and its learning directed toward oneself. Nevertheless, the Master's Way resides in the Six Classics. The Book of Changes sets forth the Way of Heaven, and the Spring and Autumn Annals records the affairs of its age. Why, then, were these not among his regular subjects of speech? Was it not because the Changes is so subtle that even the Master awaited additional years to study it, while the Annals conceals meanings to which even Ziyou and Zixia could not contribute a single word? If learners explore these depths through the Odes and Documents, and discipline themselves through ritual so as to comprehend their transformations, then a single principle will run through the patterns of Heaven and humanity. The Changes and the Spring and Autumn Annals will be encompassed within this.

“Sincerity takes form; taking form, it becomes manifest; becoming manifest, it becomes luminous.”
Zhang Yi

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: 〔Although taking form, becoming manifest, and becoming luminous represent the fullness of outward expression, they have not yet…〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
涉事業作者難於措筆詞不重復而意已明淨僅
見此篇
同考試官教諭蔡　批　誠明題最難發揮此篇於
積中發外以漸致盛處體認親切詞旨渾成理學之
士也
考試官學正王　批　純雅可錄
考試官教授馮　批　簡明
中庸推實德之徵於外以漸而極其盛焉夫誠
於中而後形於外也形而至於著且明焉其數
===
之漸盛蓋有不能自已者歟中庸極言思誠之
功以見人之未始不為天也蓋曰德莫盛於至
誠功莫難於致曲曲無不致則德無不實吾見
無妄者反其初而誠通誠復之真以全湛一者
還其性而天精天粹之純不泪積諸中而形諸
外天機活潑有不容自掩之機根於心而生於
色實德呈露有不可終祕之妙誠其有不形乎
形矣則不能不著蓋視之又加顯焉流於既溢
之餘和順者著其英華發於持滿之後充實者
punctuated:
涉事業，作者難於措筆。詞不重復，而意已明淨，僅見此篇。
同考試官教諭蔡批：誠明題最難發揮，此篇於積中發外、以漸致盛處，體認親切，詞旨渾成，理學之士也。
考試官學正王批：純雅可錄。
考試官教授馮批：簡明。
中庸推實德之徵於外，以漸而極其盛焉。夫誠於中而後形於外也，形而至於著且明焉，其數之漸盛，蓋有不能自已者歟？中庸極言思誠之功，以見人之未始不為天也。蓋曰：德莫盛於至誠，功莫難於致曲。曲無不致，則德無不實。吾見無妄者反其初，而誠通誠復之真以全；湛一者還其性，而天精天粹之純不泪。積諸中而形諸外，天機活潑，有不容自掩之機；根於心而生於色，實德呈露，有不可終祕之妙。誠其有不形乎？形矣，則不能不著，蓋視之又加顯焉。流於既溢之餘，和順者著其英華；發於持滿之後，充實者
translation_en:
…extend to practical undertakings, making it difficult for a writer to set brush to paper. Only in this piece have I seen language that avoids repetition while making the meaning clear and limpid.

Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: Topics concerning sincerity and illumination are most difficult to expound. This piece shows an intimate understanding of how what accumulates within manifests itself outwardly and gradually reaches its fullest development. Its language and meaning form a seamless whole: its author is a scholar of the Learning of Principle.

Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: Pure and elegant; worthy of selection.

Examiner Feng, Professor, comments: Concise and clear.

The Doctrine of the Mean traces the outward evidence of genuine virtue as it gradually reaches its fullest development. Only after one is sincere within does sincerity take outward form. Once it takes form, it becomes evident and then luminous. In this progressive unfolding toward fullness, is there not something that cannot stop of itself? The Doctrine of the Mean fully expounds the work of seeking sincerity, showing that the human has never been incapable of becoming one with Heaven. Its meaning is this: no virtue surpasses utmost sincerity in fullness, and no work is more difficult than fully developing each particular incipient goodness. When no such particular is left undeveloped, no aspect of virtue remains unrealized. I see that one who is free of falsity returns to the original beginning, thereby preserving whole the reality of sincerity in its outgoing activity and its return; one who is limpid and undivided returns to the true nature, so that the purity of Heaven’s essence and refinement remains unclouded [?]. Accumulating within and taking form without, Heaven’s vital impulse is lively and flowing, with a dynamism that cannot conceal itself. Rooted in the heart and appearing in the countenance, genuine virtue reveals itself, with a subtle efficacy that cannot remain hidden forever. Could sincerity ever fail to take form? Once it has taken form, it cannot but become evident, becoming still more visible than before. Flowing forth after already overflowing, what is harmonious and compliant displays its finest flowering; issuing forth after fullness has been sustained, what is inwardly full and substantial …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
昭其光大是非形之外有所謂著也其顯如是
而形不足以盡之耳著矣則不能不明蓋又有
光輝發越之盛焉抑之愈揚而道德之光華暄
赫於威儀者其暉古也遏之愈光而有道之氣
象粹盎於面背者其文蔚也是非著之外復有
所謂明也其盛如是而著不足以限之耳夫誠
也形也積中之徵也形也著也明也發外之盛
也相因不已而漸進以至於極則致曲之功全
而至誠之道臻矣然而不動者未之有也易曰
===
見龍在田天下文明學者誠能由誠明之功而
馴致乎文明之化推而極於篤恭不顯而後已
焉則天人之道融而聖賢之能事畢矣上天之
載無聲無臭至矣非天下之至誠其孰能與於
此故曰聖同天賢希聖要之自致曲始
親親仁也敬長義也無他達之天下也
田稔
同考試官教諭林 批 愛敬即是仁義達言性善〔之同此作發明親切蓋留心性學者〕
punctuated:
昭其光大。是非形之外有所謂著也，其顯如是，而形不足以盡之耳。著矣，則不能不明，蓋又有光輝發越之盛焉。抑之愈揚，而道德之光華暄赫於威儀者，其暉古也；遏之愈光，而有道之氣象粹盎於面背者，其文蔚也。是非著之外復有所謂明也，其盛如是，而著不足以限之耳。夫誠也，形也，積中之徵也；形也，著也，明也，發外之盛也。相因不已，而漸進以至於極，則致曲之功全，而至誠之道臻矣。然而不動者，未之有也。《易》曰：「見龍在田，天下文明。」學者誠能由誠明之功，而馴致乎文明之化，推而極於篤恭不顯而後已焉，則天人之道融，而聖賢之能事畢矣。「上天之載，無聲無臭。」至矣！非天下之至誠，其孰能與於此？故曰：「聖同天，賢希聖。」要之，自致曲始。

親親，仁也；敬長，義也；無他，達之天下也。

田稔

同考試官教諭林批：愛敬即是仁義，達言性善〔之同。此作發明親切，蓋留心性學者。〕
translation_en:
…display their radiance and grandeur. This does not mean that beyond taking visible form there is something separate called becoming manifest. Rather, its visibility is such that taking form is insufficient to describe it fully. Once manifest, it cannot but become luminous: there is a further fullness of radiance shining forth. The more it is suppressed, the higher it rises; the splendor of moral virtue shines brilliantly in one's dignified bearing—such is its radiance [?]. The more it is restrained, the brighter it grows; the presence of one who possesses the Way, pure and abundant, appears in face and back—such is the richness of its pattern. This does not mean that beyond becoming manifest there is something separate called becoming luminous. Rather, its fullness is such that manifestation cannot encompass it. Sincerity and taking form are evidence of what has accumulated within; taking form, becoming manifest, and becoming luminous are the fullness of its outward expression. These stages follow one another without cease, advancing gradually to the utmost. Then the work of fully developing each particular incipient goodness is complete, and the Way of utmost sincerity is attained. Never has this failed to move others. The Book of Changes says: “The dragon appears in the field; all under Heaven becomes illuminated and refined.” If students can truly proceed through the work of sincerity and illumination and gradually bring about this transforming illumination, extending it to the utmost in profound reverence without display and stopping only then, the Ways of Heaven and humanity will merge, and all that sages and worthies can accomplish will be fulfilled. “The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor scent.” This is the utmost! Who but one possessing the utmost sincerity under Heaven could participate in this? Thus it is said: “The sage is one with Heaven; the worthy aspires to sagehood.” In essence, it begins with fully developing each particular incipient goodness.

“Loving one's parents is benevolence; respecting one's elders is righteousness. There is nothing else: extend these throughout all under Heaven.”

Tian Ren

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Love and respect are themselves benevolence and righteousness. ‘Extend’ speaks of the goodness of human nature 〔being shared by all. This composition explains the point aptly and directly; its author evidently devotes attention to the study of human nature.〕”

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭趙　批　〔講仁義親長多用經傳語而詞暢理明當式多士〕
考試官學正王　批　〔詞不費而說理懇到〕
考試官教授馮　批　〔詞暢旨融〕
大賢指愛敬爲性之德以其情之同也夫愛親
敬長情也而天下無不同焉謂非仁義之性乎
孟子指而言之以見知能之良也蓋曰仁義不
假於外求孝弟自根於所性且孩提之童於親
而知親焉若不知以語仁也然仁主於愛而立
===
愛惟親可以觀仁也致愛致慕心德之真切也
靡瞻靡依愛理之惻怛也在情則謂之親在性
則謂之仁仁不出於親親之外矣惡有仁而遺
其親者耶乃若於長而知敬焉若未足以語義
也然義主於敬而立敬惟長可以觀義也因心
之友其宅心之制也天顯之念其天理之宜也
在事則謂之敬在理則謂之義義不越乎敬長
之間矣惡有義而後其兄者耶夫愛敬者情也
仁義者性也於愛敬之情而直指爲仁義之性
punctuated:
同考試官教諭趙，批：〔講仁義親長，多用經傳語，而詞暢理明，當式多士。〕
考試官學正王，批：〔詞不費，而說理懇到。〕
考試官教授馮，批：〔詞暢旨融。〕
大賢指愛敬爲性之德，以其情之同也。夫愛親敬長，情也，而天下無不同焉，謂非仁義之性乎？孟子指而言之，以見知能之良也。蓋曰：仁義不假於外求，孝弟自根於所性。且孩提之童，於親而知親焉，若不知以語仁也。然仁主於愛而立，愛惟親可以觀仁也。致愛致慕，心德之真切也；靡瞻靡依，愛理之惻怛也。在情則謂之親，在性則謂之仁，仁不出於親親之外矣。惡有仁而遺其親者耶？乃若於長而知敬焉，若未足以語義也。然義主於敬而立，敬惟長可以觀義也。因心之友，其宅心之制也；天顯之念，其天理之宜也。在事則謂之敬，在理則謂之義，義不越乎敬長之間矣。惡有義而後其兄者耶？夫愛敬者，情也；仁義者，性也。於愛敬之情而直指爲仁義之性
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: 〔In discussing benevolence and righteousness, parents and elders, this essay draws extensively on the language of the Classics and their commentaries. Its expression is fluent and its reasoning clear; it should serve as a model for the candidates.〕
Examiner Wang, School Director, comments: 〔The language is economical, and the explanation of principle earnest and thorough.〕
Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: 〔The expression is fluent and the meaning fully integrated.〕
The great worthy identifies love and respect as virtues of human nature because these feelings are shared by all. Loving one’s parents and respecting one’s elders are feelings, and no one under Heaven is without them. Can we say that they are not the nature of benevolence and righteousness? Mencius points to them and explains them to reveal the innate goodness of our knowing and doing. His meaning is that benevolence and righteousness need not be sought outside oneself: filial devotion and fraternal deference are rooted in our inherent nature. Even a small child knows to love its parents. One might not recognize this as grounds for speaking of benevolence. Yet benevolence is established with love as its foundation, and in love, affection for parents is precisely where benevolence can be seen. The fullest love and longing express the genuineness and depth of the heart’s virtue; having no one to look to or rely upon expresses the poignant grief inherent in love. In terms of feeling, this is called affection; in terms of human nature, it is called benevolence. Benevolence does not lie outside loving one’s parents. How could anyone possess benevolence yet neglect their parents?
Likewise, knowing to respect one’s elders might seem insufficient for speaking of righteousness. Yet righteousness is established with respect as its foundation, and in respect, reverence for elders is precisely where righteousness can be seen. Fraternal affection arising from the heart is the ordering disposition established within that heart; mindfulness of the bonds clearly manifested by Heaven accords with the fitting order of heavenly principle. In terms of conduct, this is called respect; in terms of principle, it is called righteousness. Righteousness does not extend beyond respecting one’s elders. How could anyone possess righteousness yet put their elder brother last? Love and respect are feelings; benevolence and righteousness are human nature. To take the feelings of love and respect and identify them directly as the nature of benevolence and righteousness…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
者豈有他哉誠以獨親其親而天下有不同焉
是之謂私愛愛之私者不可以言仁自敬其長
而天下有弗同焉是之謂私敬敬之私者不可
以言義今也一本之恩原於天性者達之天下
均之不可解於其心友于之誼察於人倫者達
之天下均之無所逃於其分天下之親不同而
愛同未有不愛其親而愛他人者蓋仁爲公理
而愛則爲公心矣天下之長不同而敬同未有
不敬其兄而敬他人者蓋義爲達德而敬爲達
===
道矣此愛敬之所以爲仁義也此知能之所以
爲良也苟能充之豈直盡巳之性巳耶親吾親
以及人之親長吾長以及人之長卒之人人親
其親長其長而天下平焉則良知良能始爲不
虛而仁義之用極矣故曰堯舜之道孝弟而巳
矣此固孟子之意也
易
天行健君子以自強不息
劉大章
punctuated:
者，豈有他哉？誠以獨親其親，而天下有不同焉，是之謂私愛。愛之私者，不可以言仁；自敬其長，而天下有弗同焉，是之謂私敬。敬之私者，不可以言義。今也，一本之恩，原於天性者，達之天下，均之不可解於其心；友于之誼，察於人倫者，達之天下，均之無所逃於其分。天下之親不同而愛同，未有不愛其親而愛他人者，蓋仁爲公理，而愛則爲公心矣。天下之長不同而敬同，未有不敬其兄而敬他人者，蓋義爲達德，而敬爲達道矣。此愛敬之所以爲仁義也，此知能之所以爲良也。苟能充之，豈直盡巳之性巳耶？親吾親以及人之親，長吾長以及人之長，卒之人人親其親、長其長，而天下平焉，則良知良能始爲不虛，而仁義之用極矣。故曰：「堯舜之道，孝弟而巳矣。」此固孟子之意也。

易
天行健，君子以自強不息。
劉大章
translation_en:
…is there any other reason for this? Surely, if one loves only one’s own parents, without sharing this disposition with all under Heaven, this is called private affection. Affection that is private cannot be called benevolence. If one respects only one’s own elders, without sharing this disposition with all under Heaven, this is called private respect. Respect that is private cannot be called righteousness. Now, affection for our common familial root, originating in our Heaven-endowed nature, extends throughout the world: it is equally inseparable from everyone’s heart. The obligation of brotherly affection, manifest in human relationships, extends throughout the world: no one can escape the duties of their position. People throughout the world have different parents, but their love is the same. No one loves others without loving their own parents. Thus benevolence is a universal principle, and love is a disposition common to all. People throughout the world have different elders, but their respect is the same. No one respects others without respecting their own elder brothers. Thus righteousness is a universally applicable virtue, and respect is a universally applicable Way. This is why love and respect constitute benevolence and righteousness, and why such knowing and ability are innate. If one can fully extend them, would one merely fulfill one’s own nature? By loving our own parents and extending this love to the parents of others, and honoring our own elders and extending this honor to the elders of others, eventually everyone will love their parents and honor their elders, and all under Heaven will be at peace. Only then will innate knowledge and innate ability be fully realized, and the workings of benevolence and righteousness reach their utmost extent. Thus it is said: “The Way of Yao and Shun is simply filial piety and brotherly deference.” This is indeed what Mencius meant.

Book of Changes
“Heaven’s movement is vigorous; the noble man accordingly strengthens himself without ceasing.”
Liu Dazhang

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭袁　批
理涉天人處自難措詞是
篇能推天以發明君子體乾之意信非健筆不能到
考試官學正王　批
發明自強處有力而粹
考試官教授馮　批
詞暢理到
天運者不已之象而君子有法天之學焉夫天
人之理一而已矣天運不已而君子法之亦不
已焉其善用乾者乎夫子傳象之意以爲乾天
象也重乾天運也蓋於穆宰其機命流行而不
已貞觀彰其度道恒久而不窮日周而日新繇
===
之不見其始天不變而道亦不變也時推而時
行引之不見其終道無盡而化亦無盡也是天
之行健之至也而乾之象也君子法之以爲天
德之在人本如是其健也而有欲焉則餒矣本
如是其久也而有間焉則息矣於是果確以致
命而天德之剛不雜以一毫之私緝熙以成能
浩然之氣常伸於萬物之上陽明自勝而陰
不得以乘之至大而不可量也至剛而不可
也天精天粹何有出入存亡焉至誠無息之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭袁　批：理涉天人處，自難措詞。是篇能推天以發明君子體乾之意，信非健筆不能到。
考試官學正王　批：發明自強處，有力而粹。
考試官教授馮　批：詞暢理到。
天運者，不已之象，而君子有法天之學焉。夫天人之理，一而已矣。天運不已，而君子法之，亦不已焉，其善用乾者乎！夫子傳象之意，以爲乾，天象也；重乾，天運也。蓋於穆宰其機，命流行而不已；貞觀彰其度，道恒久而不窮。日周而日新，繇之不見其始，天不變而道亦不變也；時推而時行，引之不見其終，道無盡而化亦無盡也。是天之行，健之至也，而乾之象也。君子法之，以爲天德之在人，本如是其健也，而有欲焉則餒矣；本如是其久也，而有間焉則息矣。於是果確以致命，而天德之剛不雜以一毫之私；緝熙以成能，浩然之氣常伸於萬物之上。陽明自勝，而陰不得以乘之，至大而不可量也，至剛而不可也。天精天粹，何有出入存亡焉？至誠無息之
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: Where the principles of Heaven and humanity intersect, finding the right words is inherently difficult. This essay develops its account of Heaven to elucidate how the gentleman embodies Qian. Truly, only a vigorous writer could attain this.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: Its elucidation of self-strengthening is forceful and refined.

Comment by Examiner Feng, Professor: The language flows freely, and the principles are fully conveyed.

Heaven’s movement presents an image of ceaseless activity, and the gentleman has a discipline of learning to model himself on Heaven. The principle governing Heaven and humanity is one and the same. Heaven moves without cease, and the gentleman, modeling himself on it, likewise never ceases. Is he not one who makes good use of Qian? The Master’s intention in the Commentary on the Images was that Qian represents Heaven, while doubled Qian represents Heaven’s movement. Unfathomable majesty presides over its workings, and its mandate flows without cease; its constancy, displayed for all to behold, manifests its regular order, and its Way endures without exhaustion. Each day it completes its circuit, and each day it is renewed. Trace it back, and its beginning cannot be seen: Heaven does not change, and neither does the Way. The seasons advance and proceed in their course. Extend this onward, and its end cannot be seen: the Way is inexhaustible, and so too is transformation. Such is Heaven’s movement, the utmost vigor, and the image of Qian.

The gentleman models himself on this, considering that Heaven’s virtue within human beings is originally just as vigorous; yet when desires arise, it weakens. It is originally just as enduring; yet when interruptions arise, it ceases. Thus, through resolution and firmness he fulfills his allotted destiny, so that the strength of Heaven’s virtue is unmixed with the slightest selfishness. Through sustained cultivation of luminous virtue he perfects his capacities, and his vast, flowing vital energy constantly extends above the myriad things. The bright yang prevails within him, and yin cannot take advantage of it. It is supremely great and cannot be measured; it is supremely firm and cannot be … [?]. Such is Heaven’s pure essence: how could there be any coming and going, preservation and loss? The unceasing activity of utmost sincerity …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
用蓋與天運相爲流通矣德性常用而物欲不
得以干之有所存而自不忘也有所理而自不
亂也常明常覺何有間斷先後焉純亦不已之
妙蓋與造化相爲終始矣是則天行健者在天
之乾也自強不息者君子法天之乾也聖同天
不旣深乎雖然乾之義一也夫子於四德皆言
聖人御天弘化之事而此但以法天成德爲訓
蓋以法天自強者王道之體御天弘化者天德
之用要之四德不備不足以語自強君子能健
以立其體行四德以達其用則天德王道一以
貫之而乾道備矣
===
昔者聖人之作易也將以順性命之理是
以立天之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔
與剛立人之道曰仁與義兼三才而兩
之故易六畫而成卦分陰分陽迭用柔
剛故易六位而成章
蘇濬
同考試官教諭袁　批　畫前有易聖人特順其理
punctuated:
用，蓋與天運相爲流通矣。德性常用，而物欲不得以干之；有所存而自不忘也，有所理而自不亂也。常明常覺，何有間斷先後焉？純亦不已之妙，蓋與造化相爲終始矣。是則天行健者，在天之乾也；自強不息者，君子法天之乾也。聖同天，不旣深乎？雖然，乾之義一也。夫子於四德，皆言聖人御天弘化之事，而此但以法天成德爲訓，蓋以法天自強者，王道之體；御天弘化者，天德之用。要之，四德不備，不足以語自強。君子能健以立其體，行四德以達其用，則天德王道一以貫之，而乾道備矣。

昔者聖人之作易也，將以順性命之理，是以立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

蘇濬

同考試官教諭袁　批：畫前有易，聖人特順其理
translation_en:
…its operation indeed flows in communion with the movement of Heaven. Moral nature is constantly at work, and material desires cannot intrude upon it. What is preserved is naturally never forgotten; what is ordered is naturally never confused. Ever lucid and ever aware, how could there be interruption or a distinction between before and after? The subtle workings of purity that likewise never ceases share their beginning and end with the processes of creation and transformation. Thus, “Heaven moves vigorously” describes Qian as it exists in Heaven; “strengthening oneself without cease” describes the noble man's emulation of Heaven's Qian. Is not the sage's oneness with Heaven profound indeed? Nevertheless, the meaning of Qian is one. In discussing the four virtues, the Master speaks throughout of the sage's work of directing Heaven's course and extending its transforming influence; here, however, he teaches only emulation of Heaven and perfection of virtue. This is because emulating Heaven and strengthening oneself constitute the substance of the kingly Way, while directing Heaven's course and extending its transforming influence constitute the functioning of heavenly virtue. In sum, without all four virtues, one cannot speak of strengthening oneself. If the noble man can establish this substance through vigor and realize its functioning by practicing the four virtues, heavenly virtue and the kingly Way will be united by a single thread, and the Way of Qian will be complete.

“In ancient times, when the sages made the Book of Changes, they intended to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny. Thus they established the Way of Heaven, calling it yin and yang; established the Way of Earth, calling it yielding and firm; and established the Way of humanity, calling it benevolence and righteousness. They embraced the Three Powers and doubled them; thus, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. They distinguished yin and yang and employed yielding and firm in alternation; thus, in the Changes, the six positions form a pattern.”

Su Jun 蘇濬

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor: “The Changes existed before the lines were drawn; the sages merely followed its principles…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
以作耳此篇體認精切蓋深於易者
考試官學正王　批　説理精明
考試官教授馮　批　雅健
説卦詳聖人之作易本三極以成功也夫易之
理見于三極者也聖人本之以作易其功之成
也有由哉説卦之意蓋謂古之聖人所以立卦
而意以盡生爻而動以顯者豈徒然哉蓋將以
性命之理神於會通有以極其精而不亂妙於
體化因以合其大而無餘然亦何以見之耶蓋
===
是理也三才盡之矣斡旋之而在上則有以立
天道焉或靜專而爲陰或動直而爲陽以兩而
成象者此也凝固之而在下則有以立地道焉
或靜翕而爲柔或動闢而爲剛以兩而成質者
此也亮周于天地之間則有以立人道焉育萬
民而爲仁正萬民而爲義以兩而成德者此也
聖人之於斯理既有以會於心自有以陳於易
以小成不足以語全也因而重之兼其三以爲
六引而伸之合其二以立體將見貞悔以之而
punctuated:
以作耳。此篇體認精切，蓋深於易者。
考試官學正王批：説理精明。
考試官教授馮批：雅健。
説卦詳聖人之作易，本三極以成功也。夫易之理，見于三極者也。聖人本之以作易，其功之成也有由哉！説卦之意，蓋謂古之聖人所以立卦而意以盡，生爻而動以顯者，豈徒然哉？蓋將以性命之理，神於會通，有以極其精而不亂；妙於體化，因以合其大而無餘。然亦何以見之耶？蓋是理也，三才盡之矣。斡旋之而在上，則有以立天道焉：或靜專而爲陰，或動直而爲陽，以兩而成象者此也。凝固之而在下，則有以立地道焉：或靜翕而爲柔，或動闢而爲剛，以兩而成質者此也。亮周于天地之間，則有以立人道焉：育萬民而爲仁，正萬民而爲義，以兩而成德者此也。聖人之於斯理，既有以會於心，自有以陳於易。以小成不足以語全也，因而重之，兼其三以爲六，引而伸之，合其二以立體，將見貞悔以之而
translation_en:
…and thereby made it, that is all. This essay grasps the principles with precision and penetration; its author is surely deeply versed in the Changes.
Examiner Wang, an Instructor, comments: “The exposition of principle is precise and clear.”
Examiner Feng, a Professor, comments: “Elegant and vigorous.”
The Explanation of the Trigrams details how the sages made the Changes, basing themselves on the Three Ultimates to accomplish their work. The principles of the Changes are manifested in the Three Ultimates. The sages based themselves on these to make the Changes: surely their accomplishment had its grounds! The meaning of the Explanation of the Trigrams is, broadly, that the ancient sages established hexagrams through which their meaning could be fully expressed, and generated lines through which movement could be revealed. Could this have been done to no purpose? They sought, through the principles of human nature and Heaven’s mandate, to achieve a spiritual mastery of their convergence and interconnection, fathoming their subtlety without confusion; and to attain a wondrous embodiment of transformation, thereby encompassing their vastness with nothing left over. Yet how can this be seen? These principles are fully comprehended in the Three Powers.
Revolving above, they establish the Way of Heaven: in stillness, concentrated, they constitute yin; in movement, direct, they constitute yang. It is through this pair that images take shape. Condensing below, they establish the Way of Earth: in stillness, closed, they constitute the yielding; in movement, opening, they constitute the firm. It is through this pair that material forms take shape. Pervading with illumination [?] the space between Heaven and Earth, they establish the Way of humanity: nurturing the myriad people constitutes benevolence; setting the myriad people right constitutes righteousness. It is through this pair that virtue takes shape.
Having apprehended these principles in their hearts, the sages naturally had the means to set them forth in the Changes. Since the lesser completion—the three-line trigram—was insufficient to express the whole, they doubled it, combining its three lines to make six. Extending and developing it, they joined the two trigrams to establish the complete structure. Thus one would see the inner and outer trigrams, through this, …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
悉備也始終以之而成質也列于全體者莫非
三極之定位矣不有以成卦乎以純象不足以
盡文也分陰陽之適中而小大有定妙剛柔之
迭用而上下無常將見經緯以之而有條也錯
綜以之而可觀也雜于六爻者莫非三極之呈
露矣不有以成章乎是則統而言之性命有以
立其體析而觀之性命因以顯其用聖人之所
以順其理也蓋如此抑斯義也皇聖人作易之
實乎是故性命也三才也陰陽剛柔仁義也皆
===
理之流行而可見者也易以像此而已非有所
加也外是而卜筮之小豈足以觀其大哉不然
何以曰天地鬼神之奧乎讀易者觀其深焉可
也
書
乃聖乃神乃武乃文
田 稔
同考試官教諭趙 批 敘述四德詞不煩而廣運
之意自見當是作者
punctuated:
悉備也，始終以之而成質也。列于全體者，莫非三極之定位矣，不有以成卦乎？以純象不足以盡文也，分陰陽之適中而小大有定，妙剛柔之迭用而上下無常，將見經緯以之而有條也，錯綜以之而可觀也。雜于六爻者，莫非三極之呈露矣，不有以成章乎？是則統而言之，性命有以立其體；析而觀之，性命因以顯其用。聖人之所以順其理也，蓋如此。抑斯義也，皇聖人作易之實乎？是故性命也，三才也，陰陽剛柔仁義也，皆理之流行而可見者也。易以像此而已，非有所加也。外是而卜筮之小，豈足以觀其大哉？不然，何以曰天地鬼神之奧乎？讀易者觀其深焉可也。

書
乃聖乃神乃武乃文
田稔

同考試官教諭趙批：敘述四德，詞不煩而廣運之意自見，當是作者。
translation_en:
…are fully provided for, and beginning and end thereby acquire definite form. Everything arrayed within the whole constitutes the fixed positions of the Three Ultimates. Does this not serve to form the hexagrams? Since undifferentiated images are insufficient to express the full pattern, yin and yang are distinguished as they attain their appropriate central positions, and the small and great have their determinate places; the alternating operation of the yielding and firm is wondrously employed, and their positions above and below are not constant. Thus their warp and weft become orderly, and their interweaving and combination become discernible. Everything intermingled among the six lines manifests the Three Ultimates. Does this not serve to complete the pattern? Viewed as a whole, nature and destiny thereby establish their substance; examined separately, nature and destiny thereby reveal their functioning. Such, indeed, is how the sage follows their underlying principle. Yet is this meaning the true substance of the august sage’s making of the Changes [?]? Thus nature and destiny, the Three Powers, and yin and yang, the yielding and firm, benevolence and righteousness, are all visible manifestations of principle in its circulation. The Changes merely represents these; it adds nothing. Apart from this, how could the minor practice of divination with tortoise shells and milfoil suffice to reveal its greatness? Otherwise, why speak of the mysteries of Heaven and Earth, ghosts and spirits? Those who read the Changes should attend to its profundity.

Book of Documents
“Both sagely and spirit-like, both martial and cultured.”
Tian Ren

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: “In describing the four virtues, the wording is concise, yet the sense of their vast reach and operation emerges of itself. This surely is the work of an accomplished writer.”

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭林　批　〔不泛不拘意明詞暢者〕〔於經學者〕
考試官學正王　批　〔結並稱堯舜允當〕
考試官教授馮　批　〔簡實閒雅〕
大臣贊帝德之盛隨變化而得名焉蓋聖神文
武堯之德也變化不同而名稱亦異其斯以爲
盛乎伯益因舜稱堯而贊堯之德如此意謂有
聖人之德而後可以居天子之位帝德維何彼
大而化之之謂聖乃聖焉包含徧覆蕩蕩乎如
===
天之仁溥博淵泉安安焉光表之化不思不勉
從容中道其聖有如此者聖不可知之之謂神乃
神焉至治與天地同流道篤恭而不顯大化與
鬼神合德民順則而不知望之如雲就之如日
其神有如此者以至威之可畏武也乃武焉濯
濯厥靈神武昭不殺之威赫赫厥聲剛健發中
正之德大畏小懷無遠不服其武也何如英華
發外文也乃文焉光輝發越巍然其有成功道
德明著煥乎其有文章經天緯地灼于四方其
punctuated:
同考試官教諭林，批：〔不泛不拘，意明詞暢者〕〔於經學者〕。
考試官學正王，批：〔結並稱堯舜，允當〕。
考試官教授馮，批：〔簡實閒雅〕。
大臣贊帝德之盛，隨變化而得名焉。蓋聖神文武，堯之德也；變化不同，而名稱亦異，其斯以爲盛乎？伯益因舜稱堯，而贊堯之德如此。意謂有聖人之德，而後可以居天子之位。帝德維何？彼大而化之之謂聖，乃聖焉。包含徧覆，蕩蕩乎如天之仁；溥博淵泉，安安焉光表之化。不思不勉，從容中道，其聖有如此者。聖不可知之之謂神，乃神焉。至治與天地同流，道篤恭而不顯；大化與鬼神合德，民順則而不知。望之如雲，就之如日，其神有如此者。以至威之可畏，武也，乃武焉。濯濯厥靈，神武昭不殺之威；赫赫厥聲，剛健發中正之德。大畏小懷，無遠不服，其武也何如？英華發外，文也，乃文焉。光輝發越，巍然其有成功；道德明著，煥乎其有文章。經天緯地，灼于四方，其
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔Neither diffuse nor constrained; the meaning is clear and the language flows freely.〕〔In classical scholarship [?].〕
Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: 〔The conclusion’s joint praise of Yao and Shun is entirely appropriate.〕
Examiner Feng, Professor, comments: 〔Concise, substantial, composed, and elegant.〕
A great minister praises the abundance of the emperor’s virtue, naming it according to its changing manifestations. Sageliness, spiritual efficacy, civil refinement, and martial prowess were Yao’s virtues. Their manifestations differed, and so their names also differed: was this not what constituted their abundance? Following Shun’s praise of Yao, Bo Yi praised Yao’s virtue in these terms. His meaning was that only after possessing the virtue of a sage could one occupy the position of Son of Heaven. What was this imperial virtue? One who is great and transforms others is called a sage: thus he was sagely. Embracing all and sheltering everything, his benevolence was vast as Heaven; broad and deep as a wellspring, his transforming influence shone forth naturally and serenely. Without deliberation or exertion, he effortlessly accorded with the mean. Such was his sageliness.
A sage whose workings cannot be fathomed is called spiritually efficacious: thus he was spiritually efficacious. His consummate government flowed together with Heaven and Earth; his Way was one of earnest reverence without display. His great transforming influence accorded in virtue with the spirits; the people followed his standards without knowing it. Seen from afar, he was like a cloud; approached, he was like the sun. Such was his spiritual efficacy.
As for the awe inspired by his majesty, this was martial prowess: thus he was martial. Resplendent was his numinous power: his spiritual martial prowess displayed an authority that required no killing. Illustrious was his renown: his firmness and vigor manifested the virtue of centrality and correctness. The great feared him and the small cherished him; none, however distant, failed to submit. How great was his martial prowess!
The outward expression of inner excellence is civil refinement: thus he was refined. His radiance shone forth, lofty were his accomplishments; his moral virtue was clearly manifest, brilliant was his cultivated order. He ordered Heaven and Earth, shining throughout the four quarters. As for his…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
文也又何如是則聖也神也文也武也自其廣
而觀之則德之咸備非一善之能名自其運而
觀之則德之變化無一息之或間堯之德至矣
雖甚盛德蔑以加矣抑重華協于帝舜之德似
無愧於堯而益之舍舜稱堯不一而足者蓋舜
方以克艱爲圖而益復以責難自效君聖臣賢
故堯之德因舜而愈彰而舜之治視堯而益顯
此唐虞際會之盛而都俞揖遜之景象猶可想
見故曰泰和在唐虞宇宙間信夫
===
東漸于海西被于流沙朔南暨聲教訖于
四海
王牧
同考試官教諭趙 批〔漸被暨訖字史氏之文作者多窘於詞此作親題敷述詞〕〔達而古明可錄〕
同考試官教諭林 批〔禹貢紀禹之功而實舜之德篇中稱禹功化終後歸重舜〕〔如人安民信史也錄之〕
考試官學正王 批〔條理貫串〕
考試官教授馮 批〔豐瞻〕
punctuated:
文也又何如？是則聖也，神也，文也，武也。自其廣而觀之，則德之咸備，非一善之能名；自其運而觀之，則德之變化，無一息之或間。堯之德至矣，雖甚盛德，蔑以加矣。抑重華協于帝，舜之德似無愧於堯，而益之舍舜稱堯，不一而足者，蓋舜方以克艱爲圖，而益復以責難自效。君聖臣賢，故堯之德因舜而愈彰，而舜之治視堯而益顯。此唐虞際會之盛，而都俞揖遜之景象猶可想見。故曰：「泰和在唐虞宇宙間。」信夫！
東漸于海，西被于流沙，朔南暨，聲教訖于四海。
王牧
同考試官教諭趙批〔漸、被、暨、訖字，史氏之文，作者多窘於詞。此作親題敷述，詞〕〔達而古明，可錄。〕
同考試官教諭林批〔禹貢紀禹之功，而實舜之德。篇中稱禹功化，終後歸重舜〕〔如人安民，信史也，錄之。〕
考試官學正王批〔條理貫串。〕
考試官教授馮批〔豐瞻。〕
translation_en:
…And what, then, of his cultural refinement? Thus he was sagely, spirit-like, cultured, and martial. Viewed in its breadth, his virtue encompassed every excellence and could not be named by any single good quality; viewed in its operation, its transformations never ceased for even a moment. Yao’s virtue had reached perfection: even the most abundant virtue could add nothing to it. Yet Chonghua harmonized with the emperor, and Shun’s virtue seems to have been worthy of Yao’s. That Yi nevertheless passed over Shun and repeatedly praised Yao was because Shun was intent on mastering the difficulties of rulership, while Yi, for his part, sought to render service by demanding difficult accomplishments of his ruler. The ruler was a sage and his minister worthy. Thus Yao’s virtue became still more manifest through Shun, while Shun’s governance shone still more brightly in comparison with Yao’s. Such was the flourishing encounter of rulers and ministers in the ages of Tang and Yu; we can still picture their approving exchanges and their courteous yielding of the throne. Hence the saying: “Supreme harmony existed within the cosmos in the ages of Tang and Yu.” How true!
“Eastward it reached the sea; westward it extended to the Flowing Sands; it reached north and south, and the fame of his civilizing influence extended to the Four Seas.”
Wang Mu
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “The words ‘reached,’ ‘extended,’ ‘reached,’ and ‘extended to’ are the historian’s wording; writers often find themselves at a loss for words here. This composition develops its exposition closely around the topic. Its language is fluent, antique, and clear: it merits inclusion.”
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “The ‘Tribute of Yu’ records Yu’s achievements, but these in fact embody Shun’s virtue. The essay praises Yu’s achievements and transforming influence, and ultimately returns the emphasis to Shun—‘like a person bringing peace to the people’ [?]. This is faithful history; include it.”
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “Its organization is coherent throughout.”
Examiner Feng, Professor, comments: “Rich and comprehensive [?].”

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
史臣紀聖化之極無遠而弗屆也蓋化極四海
治之盛也非聖人功德之大其孰能與於此記
禹貢者至此蓋謂近利不可以言功偏安不足
以語化夫惟禹也平成之績攸同於九州而祗
德之化洋溢于四海是故東方之國盡於海隅
于海隅而漸焉凡深仁厚澤之沾濡者無間於
日出之濱也西方之國盡於流沙于流沙而被
焉凡大順大化之覆冒者不限於弱水之流也
以至朔方曰北於朔而曁則幽都皆化及之區
===
蠻方維南於南而曁則南交盡文敎之域振舉
於此而遠者聞焉風聲感召推之一世而皆同
軌範於此而遠者効焉德教流行施之四達而
不悖盡於東海盡於西海地有窮而文明之化
無窮合四海而漸之被之一天地之無弗覆載
也訖於北海訖於南海地可限而風動之休無
限橫四海而曁之及之一日月之無不照臨也
吁功成於當時化被於無外禹吾無間然矣抑
舜之稱禹曰迪朕德時乃功惟敘是知臣之功
punctuated: 史臣紀聖化之極，無遠而弗屆也。蓋化極四海，治之盛也。非聖人功德之大，其孰能與於此？記《禹貢》者至此，蓋謂近利不可以言功，偏安不足以語化。夫惟禹也，平成之績攸同於九州，而祗德之化洋溢于四海。是故東方之國盡於海隅，于海隅而漸焉，凡深仁厚澤之沾濡者，無間於日出之濱也。西方之國盡於流沙，于流沙而被焉，凡大順大化之覆冒者，不限於弱水之流也。以至朔方曰北，於朔而曁，則幽都皆化及之區；蠻方維南，於南而曁，則南交盡文敎之域。振舉於此而遠者聞焉，風聲感召，推之一世而皆同；軌範於此而遠者効焉，德教流行，施之四達而不悖。盡於東海，盡於西海，地有窮而文明之化無窮；合四海而漸之被之，一天地之無弗覆載也。訖於北海，訖於南海，地可限而風動之休無限；橫四海而曁之及之，一日月之無不照臨也。吁！功成於當時，化被於無外，禹吾無間然矣！抑舜之稱禹曰：「迪朕德，時乃功惟敘。」是知臣之功
translation_en:
The court historian records the utmost reach of the sage’s transforming influence: no place was too distant for it to reach. For that influence to extend throughout the Four Seas marks the fullness of good government. Without the greatness of a sage’s achievements and virtue, who could attain this? At this point, the author of the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong) presumably means that immediate benefits cannot be called true achievement, nor can security confined to one region suffice to describe transforming influence. It was Yu whose achievement in bringing the land and waters into order extended equally throughout the Nine Provinces, while the transforming influence of reverent virtue overflowed throughout the Four Seas.

Thus, the eastern lands extended to the edge of the sea, and there his influence permeated: the shores where the sun rises shared without distinction in the deep benevolence and abundant bounty that soaked into them. The western lands extended to Liusha, and there his influence spread: the encompassing reach of great harmony and transformation was not bounded by the course of the Ruoshui. Furthermore, the northern quarter is called the north; his influence reached that quarter, and all of Youdu lay within the region it transformed. The lands of the Man peoples lay to the south; his influence reached the south, and all of Nanjiao lay within the domain of civilizing instruction.

What was set in motion here was heard of in distant places: his reputation inspired and drew people to him, and, extended throughout the age, brought all into accord. What was established as a model here was emulated in distant places: moral instruction circulated freely, spreading in all directions without resistance. Extending to the eastern sea and to the western sea, the land had an end, but the transforming influence of civilized virtue had none. Permeating and overspreading the whole realm within the Four Seas, it was just like Heaven and Earth, which leave nothing uncovered or unsupported. Reaching the northern sea and the southern sea, the land could be bounded, but the blessings of his stirring influence were boundless. Reaching and extending across the Four Seas, it was just like the sun and moon, which leave nothing unilluminated.

Ah! His achievement was completed in his own time, and his transforming influence spread so far that nothing lay outside it. In Yu I can find no fault! Yet Shun, praising Yu, said: “You have put my virtue into practice; thus your achievements have been duly accomplished.” From this we know that a minister’s achievement…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
君之德也禹方以其克勤克儉之心而成之以
不矜不伐之美是以治定功成聲教四訖此禹
之功所以爲大而舜知人之哲安民之惠不可
誣也議者乃謂舜無洪水將以禹之功爲何如
噫
詩
俾爾戩穀罄無不宜
張詡
同考試官教諭黄　批〔戩穀罄宜作者頗多𡚁〕
===
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔詞氣和平引據精切盖合此篇鋪敘條暢詞理俱到取之〕
有學有識者宜録以式多士
考試官學正王　批〔善形容臣子忠愛之意〕
考試官教授馮　批〔詞雅意足〕
詩人願天佑其君使之吉無不利也蓋戩穀罄
宜人君莫大之福也臣子祝君以是忠愛何其
至哉天保之詩有周臣子感君恩而作也若曰
君恩莫報惟天眷爲可稽天道無言惟行事爲
punctuated:
君之德也。禹方以其克勤克儉之心，而成之以不矜不伐之美，是以治定功成，聲教四訖。此禹之功所以爲大，而舜知人之哲、安民之惠不可誣也。議者乃謂舜無洪水，將以禹之功爲何如？噫！

translation_en:
…are the virtue of the ruler. Yu, with his diligence and frugality of heart, brought his achievement to completion through the excellence of neither boasting nor vaunting his merits. Thus order was established and his work accomplished, and his renown and moral instruction reached all four quarters. This is why Yu’s achievement was great; nor can Shun’s wisdom in recognizing worthy men and his beneficence in bringing peace to the people be denied. Yet some commentators claim that there was no great flood in Shun’s time. What, then, would they make of Yu’s achievement? Alas!

Book of Odes
“May he grant you blessing and bounty, with nothing that is not fitting.”
Zhang Xu

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: 〔In treating ‘blessing and bounty’ and ‘nothing that is not fitting,’ the author has rather many faults [?].〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: 〔The language and tone are balanced and mild; the supporting citations are precise and apt. The exposition accords with this ode and unfolds clearly and fluently. Both expression and reasoning are fully realized. Accept it.〕
One who possesses learning and discernment merits inclusion as a model for the many candidates.
Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: 〔Skillfully conveys the loyal affection of a subject toward his ruler.〕
Comment by Examiner Feng, Professor: 〔Elegant language and fully expressed meaning.〕

The poet wishes Heaven to protect his ruler, bringing him good fortune, with nothing unfavorable. For blessing and bounty, with everything fitting, constitute the greatest possible good fortune for a ruler. How profound is the loyal affection of subjects who invoke such blessings upon their ruler! The ode ‘Heaven Protects’ (Tian bao) was composed by subjects of the Zhou in gratitude for their ruler’s kindness. It is as though they said: ‘Our ruler’s kindness cannot be repaid; only Heaven’s favor can be looked to for confirmation. Heaven’s Way does not speak; only deeds can serve as…’

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
可示天保吾君豈止單厚多益已哉誠以人君
首庶物以立極貞萬邦以作后使事而非善非
所以語福善而未盡非所以語福之全也是必
被之以純粹之懿而景福之萃於躬者協其旋
之吉綏之以大順之道而繁祉之形於事者會
衆善之全福極所徵不獨一事爲然也精義妙
道之發隨事皆天則之流行錫類所及不但一
時爲然也日新富有之盛無往非至善之昭著
事之盡善如此則自無不宜矣夫惟事之本於
===
身者有善有未善故行之及於人者有宜有不
宜今則庶事之康悉合於天理之正而動之無
有乎或悖百爲之著咸即乎人心之安而施之
不見其有拂善政善教遠有望而近不厭天下
雖有難合之勢而將措之得宜自有以孚衆心
之同矣宜民宜人彼無惡而此無斁天下雖有
不一之情而推行之盡利自有以妙四海之準
矣夫何有不宜哉是則事難於善尤難於盡善
善難於宜尤難於無不宜人君之福必如是而
punctuated:
可示。天保吾君，豈止單厚多益已哉？誠以人君首庶物以立極，貞萬邦以作后。使事而非善，非所以語福；善而未盡，非所以語福之全也。是必被之以純粹之懿，而景福之萃於躬者協其旋之吉；綏之以大順之道，而繁祉之形於事者會衆善之全。福極所徵，不獨一事爲然也；精義妙道之發，隨事皆天則之流行。錫類所及，不但一時爲然也；日新富有之盛，無往非至善之昭著。事之盡善如此，則自無不宜矣。
夫惟事之本於身者有善有未善，故行之及於人者有宜有不宜。今則庶事之康，悉合於天理之正，而動之無有乎或悖；百爲之著，咸即乎人心之安，而施之不見其有拂。善政善教，遠有望而近不厭；天下雖有難合之勢，而將措之得宜，自有以孚衆心之同矣。宜民宜人，彼無惡而此無斁；天下雖有不一之情，而推行之盡利，自有以妙四海之準矣。夫何有不宜哉？是則事難於善，尤難於盡善；善難於宜，尤難於無不宜。人君之福必如是而
translation_en:
…can be shown. When Heaven protects our lord, does it merely grant him abundance and ever greater benefits? Indeed, the ruler stands at the head of all things to establish the supreme standard, and sets the myriad states aright as their sovereign. If his undertakings are not good, one cannot speak of blessings; if they are good but not completely so, one cannot speak of blessings in their fullness. Heaven must clothe him in pure excellence, so that the great blessings gathered upon his person accord with the auspiciousness of his actions [?]; it must settle him in the Way of perfect accord, so that the abundant blessings manifested in his undertakings encompass every good in its completeness. The blessings of the supreme standard are evidenced in more than a single undertaking: wherever refined righteousness and the wondrous Way find expression, Heaven’s pattern operates in every affair. Nor do blessings bestowed upon others extend to just a single moment: the flourishing of daily renewal and abundant possession everywhere manifests the highest good. When undertakings are thus perfectly good, nothing can fail to be fitting.
Now, because undertakings originating in oneself are sometimes good and sometimes imperfect, their effects upon others are sometimes fitting and sometimes unfitting. Here, however, the harmonious ordering of all affairs accords entirely with the correctness of Heaven’s principle, and no action departs from it. Every endeavor, as it becomes manifest, accords with what brings peace to human hearts, and its implementation meets with no resistance. With good government and good instruction, those far away look forward to them, while those nearby never tire of them. Though circumstances throughout the realm may be difficult to reconcile, fitting measures will naturally win the common assent of all hearts. Benefiting the common people and all others, he is hated by none there and wearies none here. Though people throughout the realm differ in their dispositions, measures carried out for the benefit of all will naturally make him a consummate standard for all within the Four Seas. What, then, could fail to be fitting? Thus, it is difficult for undertakings to be good, and harder still for them to be perfectly good; it is difficult for goodness to be fitting, and harder still for it to be fitting in every respect. The ruler’s blessings must be like this before …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
後全臣子之願必如是而始足也抑是詩臣子
托天福君必以戩穀罄宜爲言有以也天人相
與之際間不容髮福之者盡善必其感之者盡
善嬰之天固類應之耳洪範序五福於皇極五
事三德之後而此詩直指戩穀爲福其亦言有
所本而又知天人合一者歟
自堂徂基自羊徂牛鼐鼎及鼒　　陳光輝
同考試官教諭黃　批〔三句作者每困於纏繞此篇〕
整齊明白亦不費力可嘉
===
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔以徂基之意互見於三事〕
之中而無一贅語蓋精於經文者宜錄
考試官學正王　批〔詞意精嚴〕
考試官教授馮　批〔文體莊重〕
周士之謹於助祭行禮必循其序焉夫禮莫大
於祭而行之貴有序也周士恪謹於是所以感
神而受福也歟周之王者祭而飲酒之詩也意
謂宗廟之祭固貴於合上下之誠禮節之詳尤
punctuated:
後全，臣子之願必如是而始足也。抑是詩臣子托天福君，必以戩穀罄宜爲言，有以也。天人相與之際，間不容髮；福之者盡善，必其感之者盡善。嬰之天固類應之耳。《洪範》序五福於皇極、五事、三德之後，而此詩直指戩穀爲福，其亦言有所本，而又知天人合一者歟？
自堂徂基，自羊徂牛，鼐鼎及鼒。陳光輝

周士之謹於助祭，行禮必循其序焉。夫禮莫大於祭，而行之貴有序也。周士恪謹於是，所以感神而受福也歟？周之王者祭而飲酒之詩也。意謂宗廟之祭，固貴於合上下之誠，禮節之詳尤
translation_en:
…only then is it complete; only thus can the wishes of subjects be fully satisfied. Yet there is a reason why the subjects in this ode, entrusting to Heaven the blessing of their ruler, necessarily speak of perfect goodness and complete fittingness. In the interaction between Heaven and humanity, there is not room for a hair’s breadth of separation. If the blessings bestowed are wholly good, what moves Heaven to bestow them must necessarily be wholly good. Heaven responds in kind to what engages it [?]. The “Great Plan” places the Five Blessings after the August Ultimate, the Five Activities, and the Three Virtues, while this ode directly identifies perfect goodness as blessing. Does this not suggest that its words have a foundation, and that its author understood the unity of Heaven and humanity?
“From the hall to its foundations; from sheep to oxen; the great cauldrons, the cauldrons, and the small cauldrons.” — Chen Guanghui
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Writers addressing these three lines frequently become entangled in their exposition. This essay is orderly and clear, and achieves this without strain. Commendable.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “The meaning of ‘to its foundations’ is brought out across the three matters, without a single superfluous phrase. The writer clearly has a precise understanding of the canonical text. It merits inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: “The diction and ideas are precise and rigorous.”
Comment by Examiner Feng, Professor: “The literary style is dignified and serious.”
The officers of Zhou were meticulous in assisting at sacrifices: in performing the rites, they invariably followed the proper sequence. Among rites, none is greater than sacrifice, and in performing it, orderly sequence is prized. Was it not through their reverent care in this that the officers of Zhou moved the spirits and received blessings? This is an ode about a king of Zhou offering sacrifice and drinking wine. Its meaning is that sacrifices in the ancestral temple certainly prize the union of sincerity among those above and below, while the particulars of ritual observance especially…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
皆於循先後之序吾周士之助祭也何如哉是
故祭必省器省牲省鑊者禮也由省器而省牲
省鑊者序也今此多士執事有恪則省器爲先
以器皿不備不可以祭也然器用列於堂上則
升自門堂省籩豆於西序省壺濯於房東周旋
於器數之間巨細咸致其詳也主人立於堂下
則降徃於基告籩豆以靜嘉告壺濯以夙具返
命於門塾之下徃來必盡其敬也由是次之而
省牲焉以犧牲不成不可以祭少牢之羊太牢
===
之牛不敢委諸庖人已也從羊以至牛省視之
必徧博碩肥腯之備必察之於啓毛特殺之餘
其所以徂基而告充者則亦循夫省器之告具
也豈曰敬於彼而遂怠於此乎又次之而省鑊
焉以烹飪不潔不可以祭大鼎之鼐小鼎之鼒
不敢任諸亨人已也由大以及小閱歷之必詳
潔淨精微之美必得之於舉幂展視之下其所
以又降而告潔者則亦循夫省牲之告充也豈
曰謹於始而遂忽於終乎是則可以觀禮也可
punctuated: 皆於循先後之序。吾周士之助祭也何如哉？是故祭必省器、省牲、省鑊者，禮也；由省器而省牲、省鑊者，序也。今此多士執事有恪，則省器爲先，以器皿不備，不可以祭也。然器用列於堂上，則升自門堂，省籩豆於西序，省壺濯於房東，周旋於器數之間，巨細咸致其詳也。主人立於堂下，則降徃於基，告籩豆以靜嘉，告壺濯以夙具，返命於門塾之下，徃來必盡其敬也。由是次之而省牲焉，以犧牲不成，不可以祭。少牢之羊、太牢之牛，不敢委諸庖人已也。從羊以至牛，省視之必徧，博碩肥腯之備，必察之於啓毛特殺之餘。其所以徂基而告充者，則亦循夫省器之告具也。豈曰敬於彼而遂怠於此乎？又次之而省鑊焉，以烹飪不潔，不可以祭。大鼎之鼐、小鼎之鼒，不敢任諸亨人已也。由大以及小，閱歷之必詳，潔淨精微之美，必得之於舉幂展視之下。其所以又降而告潔者，則亦循夫省牲之告充也。豈曰謹於始而遂忽於終乎？是則可以觀禮也，可
translation_en:
…all depend upon observing the proper sequence [?]. How do our officers of Zhou assist at sacrifices? That sacrificial vessels, victims, and cooking cauldrons must be inspected is a matter of ritual; that the inspection proceeds from vessels to victims and then to cauldrons is a matter of sequence. These many officers discharge their duties reverently, beginning with the inspection of the vessels, for a sacrifice cannot be performed unless the vessels are complete. Since the implements are arrayed in the hall, they ascend from the entrance hall, inspect the bamboo and wooden offering vessels by the western wall, and inspect the wine jars and washing vessels east of the chamber. Moving among the various vessels, they attend to every detail, great and small. Since the host stands below the hall, they descend to its foot and report that the bamboo and wooden vessels are clean and fine, and that the wine jars and washing vessels have been prepared in good time. They return to report beneath the gate lodge, showing the utmost reverence in every movement to and fro.

Next they inspect the sacrificial victims, for a sacrifice cannot be performed unless the victims are fully fit. They dare not simply leave the sheep of the lesser sacrifice and the ox of the greater sacrifice to the cooks. From sheep to ox, their inspection must cover every animal. After examining the hair and slaughtering the victims individually [?], they must ascertain that all are large, robust, fat, and well fleshed. In proceeding to the foot of the hall to report that the victims are fully fit, they follow the same procedure as when they inspected the vessels and reported that everything was ready. Could they possibly be reverent in the one matter yet negligent in the other?

Next they inspect the cooking cauldrons, for a sacrifice cannot be performed unless the cooking is clean. They dare not simply entrust the large nai tripods and small zi tripods to the cooks. From the large to the small, they must examine each in detail. By lifting the covers and laying the contents open to inspection, they must ascertain their cleanliness and meticulous preparation. In descending once more to report that everything is clean, they follow the same procedure as when they inspected the victims and reported their fitness. Could they possibly be careful at the beginning yet careless at the end? In this one may observe ritual, and one may…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
以觀序也可以觀敬也周室之助祭者如此主
祭者之賢可知矣聞之易觀盥而不薦有孚顒
若下觀而化商頌亦曰奏假無言時靡有爭然
清廟秉文之德其所由來者遠矣愚於周士之
敬豈但識其文哉遡觀先王之德知其垂祚之
長一唱而三嘆矣
春秋
冬公會齊侯于防〔隱公九年〕
楊正脉
===
同考試官教諭曹　批〔惟其假王命故其會爲〕
〔非王事此作說得明白宜錄〕
考試官學正王　批〔融會經傳僅見此篇〕
考試官教授馮　批〔得春秋本旨〕
春秋譏諸侯之講好以其假禮而行私也夫會
者諸侯所不得而行私則益悖矣齊魯之舉亦
何取焉且于防之會謀伐宋也齊魯曰聞命自
鄭鄭曰有命自周若然則王事矣亦復何尤曰
非然也考之周官有時會焉謂其合諸侯也會
punctuated:
以觀序也，可以觀敬也。周室之助祭者如此，主祭者之賢可知矣。聞之《易》：「觀，盥而不薦，有孚顒若，下觀而化。」《商頌》亦曰：「奏假無言，時靡有爭。」然清廟秉文之德，其所由來者遠矣。愚於周士之敬，豈但識其文哉？遡觀先王之德，知其垂祚之長，一唱而三嘆矣。

春秋
冬，公會齊侯于防。〔隱公九年〕
楊正脉

同考試官教諭曹　批〔惟其假王命，故其會爲非王事。此作說得明白，宜錄。〕
考試官學正王　批〔融會經傳，僅見此篇。〕
考試官教授馮　批〔得春秋本旨。〕

《春秋》譏諸侯之講好，以其假禮而行私也。夫會者，諸侯所不得，而行私則益悖矣。齊魯之舉，亦何取焉？且于防之會，謀伐宋也。齊魯曰：「聞命自鄭。」鄭曰：「有命自周。」若然，則王事矣，亦復何尤？曰：非然也。考之《周官》，有時會焉，謂其合諸侯也。會
translation_en:
…one may observe their orderly conduct, and one may observe their reverence. If those assisting at the Zhou court’s sacrifices were like this, the worthiness of the one presiding over them can be inferred. We hear in the Book of Changes: “Contemplation: the hands have been washed, but the offering has not yet been presented; there is sincerity and a reverent bearing. Those below observe and are transformed.” The Hymns of Shang likewise say: “They approach without words; there is no contention.” Thus the virtue of upholding King Wen’s example in the Pure Temple had deep origins. In considering the reverence of Zhou’s officers, do I merely recognize its outward forms? Looking back to the virtue of the former kings, I understand why the blessings they bequeathed endured so long: one singing calls forth three sighs of admiration.

Spring and Autumn Annals
“In winter, the duke met the Marquis of Qi at Fang.” 〔Ninth year of Duke Yin.〕
Yang Zhengmai

Comment by Associate Examiner Cao, Instructor: 〔Precisely because they invoked the king’s command as a pretext, their meeting was not royal business. This essay explains the point clearly and merits inclusion.〕
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔Only this essay achieves an integrated understanding of the classic and its commentaries.〕
Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor: 〔It grasps the fundamental purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals.〕

The Spring and Autumn Annals censures the feudal lords for cultivating friendly relations because they used ritual as a pretext to pursue private interests. Convening such meetings was not something the feudal lords were entitled to do; pursuing private interests through them was still more perverse. What, then, was commendable in the actions of Qi and Lu? Moreover, the meeting at Fang was intended to plan an attack on Song. Qi and Lu said, “We received the command from Zheng.” Zheng said, “The command came from Zhou.” If so, this was royal business; what further grounds were there for blame? I reply: this was not so. Examining the Offices of Zhou, we find provision for occasional assemblies, meaning the gathering of the feudal lords. They were convened…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
而發禁令焉將以討不庭也會防何爲者哉棄
門之怨未釋而鄭之仇宋日深祊田之利旣歸
而魯之交鄭益固齊懷兩利遂背同盟之歡魯
恐無名因假王事之聚使節交馳於道路宣言
時會之見兩君相見於壇壝藉口不王之討而
不知宋與鄭爲仇非仇周也雖其有罪得爲不
王乎鄭爲王卿士非代王也雖其有言得爲王
命乎命不出於王則其事爲私事事不由於王
則其會爲私會未幾而中丘有約爲師期也或
===
先時而往或遂盟而歸矯假不恭其情見矣又
未幾而于菅有敗以詐勝也先之以取郜繼之
以取防攘奪無厭其迹章矣夫實征有命所以
受錫履之光也信承魯約而從事不負太公之
烈與東征有命所以忘破斧之勞也隱承鄭告
而合黨不隳周公之績與聲人之罪而先罹于
禮之愆成人之私而自取不臣之咎齊魯亦何
所見而爲斯會也哉是故春秋之時凡書會皆
譏而防之會無異文焉所以罪其私者如此此
punctuated: 而發禁令焉，將以討不庭也。會防何爲者哉？棄門之怨未釋，而鄭之仇宋日深；祊田之利旣歸，而魯之交鄭益固。齊懷兩利，遂背同盟之歡；魯恐無名，因假王事之聚。使節交馳於道路，宣言時會之見；兩君相見於壇壝，藉口不王之討。而不知宋與鄭爲仇，非仇周也，雖其有罪，得爲不王乎？鄭爲王卿士，非代王也，雖其有言，得爲王命乎？命不出於王，則其事爲私事；事不由於王，則其會爲私會。未幾而中丘有約，爲師期也。或先時而往，或遂盟而歸，矯假不恭，其情見矣。又未幾而于菅有敗，以詐勝也。先之以取郜，繼之以取防，攘奪無厭，其迹章矣。夫實征有命，所以受錫履之光也。信承魯約而從事，不負太公之烈與？東征有命，所以忘破斧之勞也。隱承鄭告而合黨，不隳周公之績與？聲人之罪，而先罹于禮之愆；成人之私，而自取不臣之咎。齊魯亦何所見而爲斯會也哉？是故春秋之時，凡書會皆譏，而防之會無異文焉。所以罪其私者如此。此
translation_en:
…and issue prohibitions and commands there, intending thereby to punish those who fail to attend the royal court. What, then, was the purpose of the meeting at Fang? The resentment over the abandoned gate [?] remained unresolved, and Zheng’s enmity toward Song deepened daily. Once the benefit of the fields at Beng had been secured, Lu’s ties with Zheng grew firmer still. Qi entertained hopes of a double advantage and thus betrayed the amity of its sworn alliance; Lu feared having no legitimate grounds and therefore used a gathering on royal business as its pretext. Envoys sped back and forth along the roads, publicly proclaiming an audience at a duly convened assembly. The two rulers met at the ritual altar and its enclosure, invoking the punishment of disloyalty to the king as their excuse. Yet they failed to recognize that Song was Zheng’s enemy, not Zhou’s. Even if Song was guilty of wrongdoing, could that count as disloyalty to the king? The ruler of Zheng was a minister of the king, not the king’s substitute. Even if he issued a pronouncement, could it count as a royal command? If the command did not originate with the king, the undertaking was a private undertaking; if the undertaking did not proceed from the king, the meeting was a private meeting. Before long, an agreement was made at Zhongqiu to fix a date for military action. One went ahead of the appointed time; another concluded a covenant and returned. Their presumptuous and disrespectful appropriation of royal authority thus revealed their true intentions. Soon afterward came the defeat at Jian, where victory was won by deceit. First they took Gao, then they took Fang: the evidence of their insatiable plunder and seizure was plain.

Now, the charge to undertake punitive expeditions was a royal command; it was through this that the Great Duke received the honor of being granted dominion. If Qi indeed acted upon Lu’s agreement, did it not betray the Great Duke’s achievements? The eastern expedition was undertaken by royal command; this was what enabled its participants to disregard the toil that broke their axes. When Duke Yin followed Zheng’s notification and joined its faction, did he not undermine the Duke of Zhou’s accomplishments? Proclaiming another’s crimes, they themselves first incurred the fault of violating ritual propriety; furthering another’s private interests, they brought upon themselves the blame for failing in their duties as subjects. What could Qi and Lu have been thinking when they held this meeting? Thus, in the period of the Spring and Autumn Annals, every recorded meeting conveys censure, and the meeting at Fang receives no different wording. Such is the way their pursuit of private interests is condemned. This…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
義行可以章典可以貞度而好會之煩其黷之
禍廣幾乎熄哉雖然宋其獨免於戾乎殤公李
以子馮之出奔而惑於州吁之邪說東門之圍
長葛之取兵連禍結以至此極也是誰之咎歟
春秋惡鄭莊之奸雄而齊魯之誤入其術也故
因事而誅其心若殤之惡則隨事著矣
春公孫歸父會楚子于宋　夏五月宋人
及楚人平〔俱宣公十有五年〕
丁繼芳
===
同考試官教諭曹　批　〔春秋大旨只在尊君捷〕
〔妻此作發揮得出錄之以式多士〕
考試官學正王　批　〔嚴整可錄〕
考試官教授馮　批　〔得謹嚴體〕
春秋譏講好者以嚴大防貶結成者以謹大倫
此宋之會楚之平昔有關於君臣夷夏之大故
也春秋所以尤加意焉慨昔楚師在宋勢將及
魯獻子倡爲求免之謀歸父遂承薦賄之命於
是乎有會焉人之言曰宋可以後亡魯可以免
punctuated:
義行，可以章典，可以貞度，而好會之煩、其黷之禍廣，幾乎熄哉！雖然，宋其獨免於戾乎？殤公李以子馮之出奔而惑於州吁之邪說，東門之圍、長葛之取，兵連禍結，以至此極也，是誰之咎歟？春秋惡鄭莊之奸雄，而齊魯之誤入其術也，故因事而誅其心。若殤之惡，則隨事著矣。
春，公孫歸父會楚子于宋。夏，五月，宋人及楚人平。〔俱宣公十有五年〕
丁繼芳
同考試官教諭曹　批：〔春秋大旨只在尊君捷〕〔妻此作發揮得出錄之以式多士〕
考試官學正王　批：〔嚴整可錄〕
考試官教授馮　批：〔得謹嚴體〕

translation_en:
…If this principle were put into practice, established norms could be made manifest and standards set right; the troublesome multiplication of meetings and the widespread calamities arising from their abuse [?] might then almost cease! Nevertheless, could Song alone escape blame? Duke Shang, Li [?], was misled by Zhou Xu’s pernicious arguments because of Zifeng’s flight abroad. The siege of the Eastern Gate and the capture of Changge brought successive warfare and entangled calamities, reaching this extremity. Whose fault was this? The Spring and Autumn Annals condemns Duke Zhuang of Zheng’s unscrupulous ambition and Qi and Lu’s mistaken entanglement in his schemes; it therefore uses the events to condemn their intentions. As for Duke Shang’s wrongdoing, it is made evident in each successive event.
“In spring, Gongsun Guifu met the Viscount of Chu in Song.” “In summer, in the fifth month, the men of Song and the men of Chu made peace.” 〔Both entries are from the fifteenth year of Duke Xuan.〕
Ding Jifang
Comment by Associate Examiner Cao, Instructor: 〔The central purpose of the Spring and Autumn Annals lies simply in honoring the ruler and [text unclear: 捷〕〔妻]. This composition brings that purpose out; it is selected to serve as a model for the candidates.〕
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔Rigorous and orderly; worthy of selection.〕
Comment by Examiner Feng, Professor: 〔It achieves a careful and rigorous style.〕
The Spring and Autumn Annals censures those who negotiate friendly relations in order to uphold the great boundaries; it disparages those who conclude peace in order to safeguard the fundamental human relationships. This meeting at Song and this peace with Chu concerned the momentous distinctions between ruler and minister and between the outer peoples and the Xia. This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals gives them particular attention. Alas, when Chu’s army was in Song, its advance threatened to reach Lu. Xianzi proposed a plan to escape the danger, and Guifu accordingly received orders to present gifts of wealth. Thus the meeting took place. title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
難討之良者而不知其非也方楚之圍宋也投
袂而起已懷必取之圖車及蒲胥赴在諸侯之
策曾也苟念友邦之義豈不能嚴兵固圉以爲
聲援與乃謀其不免至於薦賄吾恐無以制楚
之驕秪以沮宋之氣而折衝之謀踈矣況中國
之伯猶存諸姬之望未泯而忍於外求也猶謂
國有人乎此義不行而歲幣金繒之奉遂紛然
無紀極矣不有以壞天下之大防哉春秋紀其
事而譏之所以寓經世之畧焉巳而宋圍既久
===
楚功未成華元乘堙而告僊子反感慨以輸情
於是乎爲平焉人之言曰宋以是無虞楚以是
免罪功之大者而不知其悖也方二國之相持
也築室返耕内有垂亡之急師疲糧竭外無決
勝之形二臣果有安國之忠豈不能獻謀請命
以成兩利與乃輕見情實取必於君假使容萌
乘約之心主爲背城之請而傾危之變生矣況
皆在二君之側本無待報之難而敢於專行也
猶得爲純臣乎此義不明而交歡邊境之習遂
punctuated:
難，討之良者，而不知其非也。方楚之圍宋也，投袂而起，已懷必取之圖；車及蒲胥，赴在諸侯之策。曾也苟念友邦之義，豈不能嚴兵固圉，以爲聲援與？乃謀其不免，至於薦賄。吾恐無以制楚之驕，秪以沮宋之氣，而折衝之謀踈矣。況中國之伯猶存，諸姬之望未泯，而忍於外求也，猶謂國有人乎？此義不行，而歲幣金繒之奉遂紛然無紀極矣。不有以壞天下之大防哉？春秋紀其事而譏之，所以寓經世之畧焉。
巳而宋圍既久，楚功未成，華元乘堙而告僊，子反感慨以輸情，於是乎爲平焉。人之言曰：「宋以是無虞，楚以是免罪，功之大者。」而不知其悖也。方二國之相持也，築室返耕，内有垂亡之急，師疲糧竭，外無決勝之形。二臣果有安國之忠，豈不能獻謀請命，以成兩利與？乃輕見情實，取必於君。假使容萌乘約之心，主爲背城之請，而傾危之變生矣。況皆在二君之側，本無待報之難，而敢於專行也，猶得爲純臣乎？此義不明，而交歡邊境之習遂
translation_en:
…disaster: people regarded this as sound planning [?], unaware that it was wrong. When Chu besieged Song, its ruler sprang up, shaking his sleeves, already intent on taking it. His chariot reached Puxu, and the notification was entered in the records of the feudal lords [?]. Had Lu given any thought to its obligations toward a friendly state, could it not have readied its troops and secured its frontiers to provide support? Instead, it calculated that it could not escape disaster and went so far as to offer bribes. I fear that this could do nothing to restrain Chu’s arrogance and would only dampen Song’s spirits: its strategy for warding off aggression was ill-conceived. Moreover, the hegemon of the central states still remained, and the hopes invested in the states of the Ji lineage had not vanished. Yet Lu could bring itself to seek help from an outside power! Could one still say that the state had capable men? When this principle was not upheld, annual offerings of money, gold, and silk proliferated without order or limit. Would this not undermine the great safeguards of the realm? The Spring and Autumn Annals records and censures this affair, thereby embodying a strategy for ordering the world.
Later, Song had long been under siege, but Chu had not achieved success. Hua Yuan climbed the siege mound and made his report [?]; Zifan, moved by strong feeling, disclosed the true situation. Thus they made peace. People said, “Through this, Song was freed from danger and Chu escaped culpability—a great achievement.” Yet they did not recognize its violation of principle. While the two states confronted each other, houses were built and men sent back to farm. Within the city there was the urgent danger of imminent destruction; outside, the troops were exhausted and their provisions depleted, with no prospect of decisive victory. If the two ministers truly possessed the loyalty needed to secure their states, could they not have offered their plans and requested their rulers’ commands, thereby benefiting both sides? Instead, they rashly revealed the actual circumstances and committed their rulers to the outcome. Suppose one side had entertained the intention of exploiting the other’s straits [?], or a ruler had called for a last battle with the city walls at his back: a crisis threatening ruin would then have arisen. Moreover, both ministers were beside their rulers; there was no difficulty requiring them to await a reply from afar. Yet they dared act on their own authority. Could they still be considered wholly loyal ministers? When this principle was not understood, the practice of cultivating friendly relations at the borders consequently…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
晏然爲善謀矣不有以紊天下之大倫哉春秋
特稱人以貶之所以正人臣之義焉吁大防立
而中國之勢盛大倫明而君上之分尊固非小
補云耳雖然宋魯之弱無以禦楚其情猶有可
原而晉主夏盟中國所賴伯宗之對解揚之使
何爲者哉楚勢日張諸侯皆貳而莊得列於五
伯也其責固有所歸矣
禮記
君天下曰天子朝諸侯分職授政任功曰
===
予一人　張白
同考試官教授梁　批〔發明理達分定而人君之尊自任之重具見詞莊而古暢〕
考試官學正王　批〔嚴整有文豐贍根理〕
考試官教授馮　批〔詞氣典雅〕
觀人君通稱自稱之辭而一統之盛見矣甚矣
王者無外也通稱而其辭尊自稱而其辭專一
統之盛何如哉記曲禮者意謂惟天爲大而王
punctuated:
晏然爲善謀矣，不有以紊天下之大倫哉？《春秋》特稱人以貶之，所以正人臣之義焉。吁！大防立而中國之勢盛，大倫明而君上之分尊，固非小補云耳。雖然，宋魯之弱，無以禦楚，其情猶有可原；而晉主夏盟，中國所賴，伯宗之對，解揚之使，何爲者哉？楚勢日張，諸侯皆貳，而莊得列於五伯也，其責固有所歸矣。

禮記

君天下曰天子，朝諸侯，分職授政，任功，曰予一人。　張白

同考試官教授梁　批〔發明理達分定，而人君之尊、自任之重具見，詞莊而古暢。〕
考試官學正王　批〔嚴整有文，豐贍根理。〕
考試官教授馮　批〔詞氣典雅。〕

觀人君通稱、自稱之辭，而一統之盛見矣。甚矣，王者無外也！通稱而其辭尊，自稱而其辭專，一統之盛何如哉！記《曲禮》者意謂惟天爲大，而王
translation_en:
…is complacently regarded as sound strategy. Does this not bring disorder to the great relationships governing all under Heaven? The Spring and Autumn Annals deliberately calls them merely “men” to condemn them, thereby rectifying the duty of ministers. Ah! When the great boundaries are established, the strength of the central states flourishes; when the great relationships are clarified, the sovereign’s standing is honored. This is certainly no small contribution. Even so, Song and Lu were weak and unable to withstand Chu, so their circumstances admit of some excuse. But Jin presided over the covenant of the states of Xia and was the mainstay of the central states: what, then, did Bo Zong’s reply and Xie Yang’s mission accomplish? Chu’s power grew daily, the feudal lords all wavered in their allegiance, and King Zhuang came to rank among the Five Hegemons. Responsibility for this certainly has its proper resting place.

Book of Rites

“He who rules all under Heaven is called the Son of Heaven. When receiving the feudal lords at court, allocating offices and assigning governmental duties, and entrusting responsibilities according to merit, he calls himself ‘I, the One Man.’” — Zhang Bai

Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: 〔The exposition makes the principles clear and fixes the distinctions of status, fully revealing both the sovereign’s exalted position and the weight of the responsibilities he assumes. The language is dignified, antique, and fluent.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Rigorous and orderly, with literary grace; rich and ample, and grounded in principle.〕
Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: 〔The language and tone are classically elegant.〕

By considering the terms by which the sovereign is generally addressed and those by which he refers to himself, we see the grandeur of unified rule. How far-reaching is the principle that nothing lies outside the king’s domain! The term by which he is generally addressed is exalted; the term by which he refers to himself is exclusive. How magnificent is unified rule! The compiler of the “Summary of the Rules of Propriety” meant that Heaven alone is great, and the king…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
者繼之惟王繼天而天下仰之觀其所稱而人
君之大分昭矣何則王者受天明命作斯民之
父毋宅中圖大爲億兆之君師遠而薄海內外
罔不率俾群黎歸心而萬邦仰德也大而庶邦
遠邇罔不臣服百辟承式而四夷來王也若此
者臣民則稱之曰天子焉盖天地以大君爲宗
子而主器是託大君以乾坤爲父毋而袛若不
違心代天意也口代天言也身代天工也猶子
之述父事而無忝所生不曰天子而何哉至若
===
群后來庭於萬國而慶賞攸舉五服肆覲於方
岳而黜陟旣明乃論官以宅之位事以器之貴
賤式序而欽乃攸司也明試以庸之考成以省
之淑慝知勸而嘉乃丕績也若此者則自稱曰
予一人焉以見勢無兩大權柄不至於下移尊
惟一統威福不敢以上僭庶尹我諧也庶事我
康也庶績我凝也任之極其專而臣民不與不
曰予一人而何哉夫尊其稱則事天益敬矣專
其稱則治民益切矣事天治民君道不其備哉
punctuated: 者繼之，惟王繼天，而天下仰之。觀其所稱，而人君之大分昭矣。何則？王者受天明命，作斯民之父毋，宅中圖大，爲億兆之君師。遠而薄海內外，罔不率俾，群黎歸心而萬邦仰德也；大而庶邦遠邇，罔不臣服，百辟承式而四夷來王也。若此者，臣民則稱之曰天子焉。盖天地以大君爲宗子，而主器是託；大君以乾坤爲父毋，而袛若不違。心代天意也，口代天言也，身代天工也，猶子之述父事而無忝所生，不曰天子而何哉？至若群后來庭於萬國，而慶賞攸舉；五服肆覲於方岳，而黜陟旣明。乃論官以宅之，位事以器之，貴賤式序而欽乃攸司也；明試以庸之，考成以省之，淑慝知勸而嘉乃丕績也。若此者，則自稱曰予一人焉。以見勢無兩大，權柄不至於下移；尊惟一統，威福不敢以上僭。庶尹我諧也，庶事我康也，庶績我凝也。任之極其專，而臣民不與，不曰予一人而何哉？夫尊其稱，則事天益敬矣；專其稱，則治民益切矣。事天治民，君道不其備哉？
translation_en:
…the king succeeds to Heaven. It is precisely because the king succeeds to Heaven that all under Heaven look up to him. By considering the appellations used for him, the sovereign’s supreme standing becomes clear. Why is this? The king receives Heaven’s illustrious mandate and becomes father and mother to the people. Dwelling at the center and planning great undertakings, he serves as ruler and teacher to the countless multitudes. As far as the seas and beyond, none fail to obey: the common people give him their allegiance, and the myriad states look up to his virtue. Throughout the vast array of states, near and far, none fail to submit as subjects: the many lords follow his example, and the peoples of the four quarters come to acknowledge his kingship. Thus his subjects call him the Son of Heaven. For Heaven and Earth regard the great ruler as their principal heir and entrust him with custody of the ancestral sacrificial vessels; the great ruler regards Heaven and Earth as his father and mother, reverently obeying them without deviation. His mind expresses Heaven’s intentions; his mouth speaks Heaven’s words; his person performs Heaven’s work. He is like a son who carries on his father’s undertakings without disgracing those who gave him birth. What, then, should he be called if not the Son of Heaven?

When the lords of the myriad states come to court, celebrations and rewards are duly bestowed; when those of the five zones of submission appear in audience at the sacred mountains of the regions, demotions and promotions are clearly determined. He then assesses men for offices and places them accordingly, assigning duties and employing them according to their capacities. Noble and lowly ranks are duly ordered, and each reverently attends to his charge. He openly tests men before employing them and examines their accomplishments to scrutinize their performance. Both the good and the wicked thus understand the incentive to exert themselves, and great achievements receive commendation. In these circumstances he calls himself ‘I, the One Man.’ This shows that there cannot be two supreme powers, and that authority must not pass into the hands of subordinates. Supreme dignity belongs to a single sovereign, and those below dare not usurp his power to punish and reward. It is I who bring the many officials into harmony; I who set the many affairs in order; I who bring the many achievements to completion. This responsibility is his alone in the fullest sense, and his subjects have no share in it. What, then, should he call himself if not ‘I, the One Man’? An exalted appellation makes him ever more reverent in serving Heaven; an appellation expressing his sole responsibility makes him ever more earnest in governing the people. In serving Heaven and governing the people, is not the Way of the ruler complete?

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
雖然此就稱謂者言之耳夫曰天子則凡有血
氣者皆當尊之如天而遠慢之心不敢生焉曰
予一人則凡在統御者皆當聽其號令而專擅
之心不敢萌焉其立教之意尤有所在矣此固
禮之微意也
樂統同禮辨異禮樂之說管乎人情矣
楚孔生
同考試官教授梁　批〔同言和異言序禮樂自　是情理此作有分別有歸頓和于遠於是者〕
===
考試官學正王　批〔文暢而核義悉而瑩〕
考試官教授馮　批〔理致〕
記者原禮樂之用而有以約乎其情焉蓋人情
以禮樂而治也統同辨異而人情有以約之禮
樂之用大矣哉且禮樂之在天下其始也固緣
情以立制其既也乃治情以爲功何則樂也者
情之不可變者也惟其不可變則子諒之心生
而慾心以平和易之情浹而躁心以釋君臣聽
之而和敬長幼聽之而和順聯之以恩其情洽
punctuated:
雖然，此就稱謂者言之耳。夫曰天子，則凡有血氣者皆當尊之如天，而遠慢之心不敢生焉；曰予一人，則凡在統御者皆當聽其號令，而專擅之心不敢萌焉。其立教之意尤有所在矣，此固禮之微意也。
「樂統同，禮辨異，禮樂之說管乎人情矣。」
楚孔生
同考試官教授梁批〔同言和，異言序。禮樂自是情理，此作有分別，有歸頓，和于遠於是者。〕
考試官學正王批〔文暢而核，義悉而瑩。〕
考試官教授馮批〔理致。〕
記者原禮樂之用，而有以約乎其情焉。蓋人情以禮樂而治也，統同辨異，而人情有以約之，禮樂之用大矣哉！且禮樂之在天下，其始也固緣情以立制，其既也乃治情以爲功。何則？樂也者，情之不可變者也。惟其不可變，則子諒之心生，而慾心以平；和易之情浹，而躁心以釋。君臣聽之而和敬，長幼聽之而和順。聯之以恩，其情洽
translation_en:
Even so, this speaks only of forms of address. When the ruler is called the Son of Heaven, all beings possessing blood and vital breath should revere him as Heaven, never daring to harbor thoughts of estrangement or disrespect. When he says “I, the One Man,” all under his governance should obey his commands, never daring to entertain thoughts of arrogating authority to themselves. The intention of establishing moral instruction through these terms has a still deeper significance. This is indeed a subtle meaning of ritual.
“Music unites what is shared; ritual distinguishes differences. The teachings concerning ritual and music encompass human feelings.”
Chu Kongsheng 楚孔生
Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, an Instructor: “‘Shared’ refers to harmony; ‘differences’ refers to order. Ritual and music are inherently matters of feeling and principle. This composition makes distinctions and brings its argument to a conclusion; the final phrase concerning harmony and distance is unclear [?].”
Comment by Examiner Wang, an School Instructor: “The prose is fluent and precise; the meaning is fully developed and lucid.”
Comment by Examiner Feng, an Instructor: “Principled and refined.”
The author of the Record examines the functions of ritual and music at their source and thereby provides a means of regulating human feelings. Human feelings are indeed governed through ritual and music. By uniting what is shared and distinguishing differences, they provide a means of regulating those feelings. How great are the functions of ritual and music! When ritual and music first arose in the world, institutions were established in accordance with human feelings; thereafter, their achievement lay in governing those feelings. Why is this? Music embodies that which cannot be altered in human feelings. Precisely because it cannot be altered, a disposition of kindness and sincerity [?] arises, and desire is calmed; feelings of harmony and ease permeate the heart, and agitation is dispelled. When ruler and ministers hear it, they become harmonious and respectful; when elders and juniors hear it, they become harmonious and compliant. Bound together by kindness, their feelings accord…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
也怡之以德其志順也所謂異文合愛是已不
有以統同乎禮也者理之不可易者也惟其不
可易則非僻不作而莊敬之容益章惰慢不設
而嚴肅之體益著用之朝廷而讓貴用之鄉黨
而讓齒禮儀卒度無少肆也威儀不忒毋相瀆
也所謂殊事合敬是已不有以辨異乎夫禮不
徒節而有樂以和其節樂不徒和而有禮以濟
其和則中和之德備而不足以管人情者否也
蓋樂勝則流人之情也今禮以飾貌和平感而
===
等威以辨易直形而貴賤以別相親也而不相
褻也則同者有所管而有以立天下之敬禮云
禮云人情於是乎檢矣禮勝則離人之情也今
樂以合情誠意聯屬於上下恩愛交孚於尊卑
至嚴也而寓至和也則異者有所管而有以同
天下之愛樂云樂云人情於是乎攝矣是則通
禮樂之用可以語器矣達禮樂之原可以語道
矣君子不徒泥諸其器而神諸其道則天地將
爲昭焉而況於人情乎易曰上天下澤履君子
punctuated:
也。怡之以德，其志順也。所謂異文合愛是已，不有以統同乎？禮也者，理之不可易者也。惟其不可易，則非僻不作，而莊敬之容益章；惰慢不設，而嚴肅之體益著。用之朝廷而讓貴，用之鄉黨而讓齒。禮儀卒度，無少肆也；威儀不忒，毋相瀆也。所謂殊事合敬是已，不有以辨異乎？夫禮不徒節，而有樂以和其節；樂不徒和，而有禮以濟其和，則中和之德備，而不足以管人情者否也。

蓋樂勝則流，人之情也。今禮以飾貌，和平感而等威以辨，易直形而貴賤以別，相親也而不相褻也，則同者有所管，而有以立天下之敬。禮云禮云，人情於是乎檢矣。禮勝則離，人之情也。今樂以合情，誠意聯屬於上下，恩愛交孚於尊卑，至嚴也而寓至和也，則異者有所管，而有以同天下之愛。樂云樂云，人情於是乎攝矣。

是則通禮樂之用，可以語器矣；達禮樂之原，可以語道矣。君子不徒泥諸其器，而神諸其道，則天地將爲昭焉，而況於人情乎？《易》曰：「上天下澤，履。君子
translation_en:
… Their feelings are thus brought into accord. Delighted through virtue, their intentions become harmonious. This is what is meant by “differing in outward forms but united in love.” Does this not provide a means of bringing people into unity? Ritual embodies principles that cannot be altered. Precisely because they cannot be altered, wrongdoing and perversity do not arise, and a bearing of dignity and reverence becomes ever more evident; indolence and arrogance find no place, and a demeanor of solemnity becomes ever more manifest. Applied at court, ritual teaches deference to rank; applied in village communities, it teaches deference to age. Every ritual observance conforms to its proper measure, without the slightest license; dignified conduct does not err, and people do not treat one another with disrespectful familiarity. This is what is meant by “differing in duties but united in reverence.” Does this not provide a means of distinguishing differences? Ritual does not merely impose restraint: music harmonizes its restraints. Music does not merely produce harmony: ritual complements its harmony. Thus the virtue of equilibrium and harmony is complete, and there is no possibility of failing to regulate human feelings.

When music predominates, people drift into excess: such is human nature. Now ritual regulates outward demeanor, so that even as peace and harmony move people, distinctions of rank and authority remain clear; even as ease and uprightness manifest themselves, the noble and the lowly remain distinct. People are affectionate toward one another without becoming overly familiar. Thus what unites them is regulated, and reverence can be established throughout the world. Ritual, ritual! Through it human feelings are restrained. When ritual predominates, people become estranged: such is human nature. Now music unites feelings: sincerity links those above and below, while kindness and affection inspire mutual trust between the exalted and the humble. Within the utmost solemnity resides the utmost harmony. Thus what differentiates them is regulated, and the love of all under Heaven can be united. Music, music! Through it human feelings are drawn together.

Thus, if one comprehends the workings of ritual and music, one may discuss their concrete forms; if one grasps their source, one may discuss the Way. The gentleman does not merely cling to their concrete forms, but brings wondrous efficacy to their Way. Then even Heaven and Earth will be illuminated through it—how much more so human feelings! The Book of Changes says: “Heaven above, the marsh below: Treading. The gentleman …”

…thereby distinguishes those above from those below and settles the people's purposes. “Thunder issues forth and stirs the earth: Enthusiasm (Yu). The former kings thereby made music to exalt virtue.” Great indeed are the functions of ritual and music! Yet people do not understand that Treading (Lü) means putting into practice the reverence of this heart, so that ritual without physical form arises [?]; Enthusiasm means rejoicing in the harmony of this heart, so that music without sound is complete. Thus, when the former kings practiced Treading, they shared the rhythms of Heaven and Earth; when they practiced Enthusiasm, they shared the harmony of Heaven and Earth; when they performed the suburban sacrifice [?], they shared the numinous efficacy of Heaven and Earth.
