title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
見者物物也以天下之至顯而統於天下之至
微此道之所以爲大而聖人之所不能自巳也
天下之物其散見而無所紀極者若是乎其甚
顯而其物物之藏於窅而非夫人之所能窺者
若是乎其甚微以至顯而統之於至微此其理
之與器若有不可同日而語者而不知物之可
見也必有所以綱維之者以爲之本而物物者
之不可見也必有所附麗以爲之用此顯微之
所以相爲無窮而道之所以爲大也道之大也
===
天地猶憾焉而況於聖人乎此其所以望道之
心無窮而不能自巳也君子之道達諸天張子
明斯道之大也夫天地一物也而天以陰陽五
行流行於天下而天下之物舉得而覆且載焉
則不物之物有以物天下之物無所遺焉者也
是故其物之麗乎上也有明而不可息者有燦
而不可隱者有奮而不可遏者有潤而不可巳
者有絪縕而不可窮者有往來而不可止者其
麗乎下也有高而揚者有下而沉者有融而流
punctuated:
見者，物物也。以天下之至顯而統於天下之至微，此道之所以爲大，而聖人之所不能自巳也。天下之物，其散見而無所紀極者，若是乎其甚顯；而其物物之藏於窅，而非夫人之所能窺者，若是乎其甚微。以至顯而統之於至微，此其理之與器，若有不可同日而語者。而不知物之可見也，必有所以綱維之者以爲之本；而物物者之不可見也，必有所附麗以爲之用。此顯微之所以相爲無窮，而道之所以爲大也。道之大也，天地猶憾焉，而況於聖人乎？此其所以望道之心無窮，而不能自巳也。「君子之道達諸天」，張子明斯道之大也。
夫天地，一物也。而天以陰陽五行流行於天下，而天下之物舉得而覆且載焉，則不物之物有以物天下之物，無所遺焉者也。是故其物之麗乎上也，有明而不可息者，有燦而不可隱者，有奮而不可遏者，有潤而不可巳者，有絪縕而不可窮者，有往來而不可止者。其麗乎下也，有高而揚者，有下而沉者，有融而流
translation_en:
…what cannot be seen is that which gives things their being. That the most manifest things in the world are governed by what is most subtle in the world is why the Way is great, and why even the sage cannot cease his striving. The things of the world, appearing everywhere in limitless variety, are thus utterly manifest; yet that which gives things their being, concealed in obscurity where not everyone can discern it, is thus utterly subtle. When the most manifest is governed by the most subtle, principle and concrete things might seem so different that they cannot be spoken of together. Yet this overlooks the fact that visible things must have something that orders and sustains them as their foundation; and that the invisible source of their being must have something in which to reside and through which to function. This is why the manifest and the subtle endlessly sustain one another, and why the Way is great. Such is the greatness of the Way that even Heaven and Earth fall short of it; how much more, then, must the sage? This is why his aspiration toward the Way is inexhaustible and he cannot cease his striving. “The Way of the gentleman reaches to Heaven”: Master Zhang here makes clear the greatness of this Way.
Now Heaven and Earth are a single entity. Heaven circulates throughout the world through yin and yang and the Five Phases, and all the things of the world thereby receive shelter above and support below. Thus that which is no thing, yet is the source of things, gives being to all things in the world, leaving none out. Hence, among the things situated above, some shine without ceasing; some sparkle and cannot be hidden; some surge forth and cannot be restrained; some moisten without stopping; some mingle in an inexhaustible interplay of vital forces; and some come and go without pause. Among those situated below, some rise high aloft; some lie low and sink; some melt and flow…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
者有結而止者有動而有知者有靜而有生者
其麗乎人也有約而為質者有散而為文者有
合而相附者有離而相疏者有尊而相事者有
卑而相使者夫物之麗乎上也此氣之流行而
不可已者也麗乎下也此質之一定而不可易
者也麗乎人也此事之錯綜變化於天下而不
可定者也夫氣也質也事也此皆所謂物之為
物而天下之至顯也而所謂不物乎物而能物
物者則逝遁而莫測其機形忘而莫窮其妙探
===
之而莫究其所極約之而莫知其所終窮是以
言天下之至顯者莫如物而言天下之至微者
莫如物物物物也者器也形而下者也物物也者
理也形而上者也舉天下之氣舉天下之質舉
天下之事而謂之曰此皆道也固非也舉天下
之氣與質與事而謂之曰此非道也亦非也是
氣也是質也是事也孰從而推行之孰從而主
張之其所以流行者孰為之機其所以一定者
孰為之權其所以錯綜變化而不容已者孰為
punctuated: 者，有結而止者，有動而有知者，有靜而有生者。其麗乎人也，有約而為質者，有散而為文者，有合而相附者，有離而相疏者，有尊而相事者，有卑而相使者。夫物之麗乎上也，此氣之流行而不可已者也；麗乎下也，此質之一定而不可易者也；麗乎人也，此事之錯綜變化於天下而不可定者也。夫氣也、質也、事也，此皆所謂物之為物而天下之至顯也。而所謂不物乎物而能物物者，則逝遁而莫測其機，形忘而莫窮其妙，探之而莫究其所極，約之而莫知其所終窮。是以言天下之至顯者莫如物，而言天下之至微者莫如物物。物物也者，器也，形而下者也；物物也者，理也，形而上者也。舉天下之氣，舉天下之質，舉天下之事，而謂之曰：「此皆道也。」固非也。舉天下之氣與質與事，而謂之曰：「此非道也。」亦非也。是氣也，是質也，是事也，孰從而推行之？孰從而主張之？其所以流行者，孰為之機？其所以一定者，孰為之權？其所以錯綜變化而不容已者，孰為
translation_en:
…those that congeal and come to rest, those that move and possess awareness, and those that remain still yet possess life. As manifested among human beings, there are those that are concentrated into substance and those that spread out into patterned expression; those that unite and attach themselves to one another and those that separate and grow distant; those of exalted station whom others serve and those of lowly station whom others employ.

Things manifested above are vital energy flowing ceaselessly. Those manifested below are material substance, fixed and unalterable. Those manifested among human beings are affairs interweaving and changing throughout the world, incapable of being fixed. Vital energy, material substance, and affairs: these all constitute what makes things things and are the most manifest elements of the world. Yet that which is not itself a thing among things, but can make things what they are, eludes us, so that its workings cannot be fathomed; its form disappears [?], so that its subtlety cannot be exhausted. Probe it, and its furthest reach cannot be investigated to the end; seek to encompass it, and its ultimate limit cannot be known. Thus, in speaking of what is most manifest in the world, nothing compares with things; in speaking of what is most subtle, nothing compares with that which makes things what they are. Things as things [?] are concrete entities, belonging to what is below form; that which makes things what they are is principle, belonging to what is above form.

To take all the vital energy in the world, all its material substance, and all its affairs, and say, “These are all the Way,” is certainly wrong. To take all the world's vital energy, material substance, and affairs, and say, “These are not the Way,” is also wrong. This vital energy, this material substance, these affairs—what impels them onward? What governs them? What is the motive force behind their flowing movement? What is the controlling power behind their fixity? As for their ceaseless interweaving and transformation, what brings about…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
之推行變化曰此非氣也非質也非事也不物
于物而能物物者之爲也發微而不可見充周
而不可窮物物之不可名也君子以其不可名
而名之曰道道不可名而名之曰天天也道也
極於天地而天地不能盡備於聖人而聖人不
能盡是故至隱也而天下之至彰寓焉至靜也
而天下之至動在焉天下無一而非物則亦無
一而非物物物物者不物於物者也是故麗乎
上也明者非自明也燦者非自燦也奮者潤者
===
非自奮而潤也絪緼往來者非自絪緼而往來
也其所以使之明使之燦使之奮而潤使之絪
緼而往來者有主也麗乎下也高者不能自高
也下者不能自下也融者結者不能自融而結
也動者靜者不能自動而靜也其所以使之高
使之下使之融而結使之動而靜者有機也麗
乎人也約者非自從而約之也散者非自從而
散之也合者離者非自從而合且離之也尊者
卑者非自從而尊且卑之也其所以使之約使
punctuated: 之推行變化？曰：此非氣也，非質也，非事也，不物于物而能物物者之爲也。發微而不可見，充周而不可窮，物物之不可名也。君子以其不可名而名之曰道，道不可名而名之曰天。天也，道也，極於天地而天地不能盡，備於聖人而聖人不能盡。是故至隱也，而天下之至彰寓焉；至靜也，而天下之至動在焉。天下無一而非物，則亦無一而非物物。物物者，不物於物者也。是故麗乎上也，明者非自明也，燦者非自燦也，奮者潤者非自奮而潤也，絪緼往來者非自絪緼而往來也。其所以使之明、使之燦、使之奮而潤、使之絪緼而往來者，有主也。麗乎下也，高者不能自高也，下者不能自下也，融者結者不能自融而結也，動者靜者不能自動而靜也。其所以使之高、使之下、使之融而結、使之動而靜者，有機也。麗乎人也，約者非自從而約之也，散者非自從而散之也，合者離者非自從而合且離之也，尊者卑者非自從而尊且卑之也。其所以使之約、使
translation_en:
…sets them in motion and brings about their transformations? The answer is: this is neither vital energy, nor material substance, nor affairs. It is the work of that which, without being made a thing by things, can make things what they are. It manifests its subtle workings yet cannot be seen; it pervades everything yet cannot be exhausted. That which makes things what they are cannot be named. Because it cannot be named, the gentleman gives it the name “the Way”; because the Way cannot be named, he gives it the name “Heaven.” Heaven and the Way reach throughout heaven and earth, yet heaven and earth cannot exhaust them; they are fully present in the sage, yet the sage cannot exhaust them. Thus, within the most hidden resides what is most manifest in the world; within the most still lies what is most active in the world. Nothing in the world is other than a thing; thus nothing is without that which makes it what it is. That which makes things what they are is itself not made a thing by things.

Thus, among things attached to the heavens above, what shines does not shine of itself; what is brilliant is not brilliant of itself; what stirs and what moistens do not stir and moisten of themselves; and those energies that intermingle, coming and going, do not intermingle, come, and go of themselves. That which makes them shine, makes them brilliant, makes them stir and moisten, and makes them intermingle, come, and go has a governing principle. Among things attached to the earth below, what is high cannot make itself high; what is low cannot make itself low; what melts and what congeals cannot melt and congeal of themselves; what moves and what rests cannot move and rest of themselves. That which makes them high, makes them low, makes them melt and congeal, and makes them move and rest has an animating impulse. Among things pertaining to human beings, what is bound together does not bind itself together; what is dispersed does not disperse itself; what is united and what is separated do not unite and separate themselves; what is exalted and what is lowly do not exalt and abase themselves. That which makes them bind together, makes…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
之散使之合而離使之尊而卑者有神也是故
合而言之則氣也質也事也其所以統體乎太
極者至微也分而言之則氣也質也事也其所
以各具乎太極者至隱也隱也微也神也機也
主也此道之所以大也此大之所以爲天也以
言其大無外也以言其小無內也以言其來無
始也去無終也以言其遠非久也近非暫也盈
天地之間皆物也皆物物也聖人者方以其所
受於天之物而以其不物於物者擬諸天之物
===
物以爲之根柢焉以爲之主張焉以爲之綱維
焉擬於其明者燦者奮者潤者絪緼而往來若
欲至於不晦焉隕焉息而止焉而氣之流行而
不已者不物于物而使之盡也擬於其高者下
者融者結者動而靜者欲至於不替焉墜焉凝
而流焉墜焉覆焉而質之一定而不易者不物
于物而使之變也擬於其約者散者合者離者
尊而卑者將至於敝焉戾焉疎而悖焉而事之
錯綜變化而無窮者不物於物而使之紊也夫
punctuated: 之散，使之合而離，使之尊而卑者，有神也。是故，合而言之，則氣也、質也、事也，其所以統體乎太極者至微也；分而言之，則氣也、質也、事也，其所以各具乎太極者至隱也。隱也，微也，神也，機也，主也，此道之所以大也，此大之所以爲天也。以言其大，無外也；以言其小，無內也；以言其來，無始也；去，無終也；以言其遠，非久也；近，非暫也。盈天地之間皆物也，皆物物也。聖人者，方以其所受於天之物，而以其不物於物者，擬諸天之物物，以爲之根柢焉，以爲之主張焉，以爲之綱維焉。擬於其明者、燦者、奮者、潤者、絪緼而往來，若欲至於不晦焉、隕焉、息而止焉，而氣之流行而不已者，不物于物而使之盡也。擬於其高者、下者、融者、結者、動而靜者，欲至於不替焉、墜焉、凝而流焉、墜焉、覆焉，而質之一定而不易者，不物于物而使之變也。擬於其約者、散者、合者、離者、尊而卑者，將至於敝焉、戾焉、疎而悖焉，而事之錯綜變化而無窮者，不物於物而使之紊也。夫
translation_en:
…them disperse, makes them unite and separate, and makes them exalted and lowly: there is a numinous power behind this. Thus, considered together, vital energy, material substance, and affairs embody the Supreme Ultimate as a whole in a manner supremely subtle. Considered separately, vital energy, material substance, and affairs each possess the Supreme Ultimate in a manner supremely hidden. This hiddenness, subtlety, numinous power, moving impulse, and governing agency are what make the Way great; this greatness is what makes it Heaven. Speaking of its greatness, nothing lies outside it; speaking of its smallness, nothing lies within it. Speaking of its coming, it has no beginning; of its going, it has no end. Speaking of its remoteness, it is not a matter of long duration; of its nearness, it is not a matter of brevity. All that fills the space between Heaven and Earth consists of things, and all bring things into being. The sage takes what he has received from Heaven and, through that in himself which is not subjected to things, models himself upon Heaven’s bringing things into being, thereby providing their root, their governing agency, and their sustaining framework.
He models himself upon what shines, glitters, surges, moistens, and mingles in generative interplay as it comes and goes, as though seeking to ensure that it does not grow dim, fall, subside, or cease. Thus vital energy, circulating without cessation, is not subjected to things so as to become exhausted. He models himself upon what is high and low, melts and congeals, moves and rests, seeking to ensure that it does not decline, fall, congeal and flow, fall, or overturn [?]. Thus material substance, once established and unchanging, is not subjected to things so as to be altered. He models himself upon what contracts and disperses, unites and separates, is exalted and lowly, and is about to reach deterioration, disorder, estrangement, and perversity [?]. Yet affairs, interweaving and transforming without limit, are not subjected to things so as to be thrown into confusion. Now, …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
氣而不盡也質而不變也事而不紊也此天地
之全體聖人之全德推而極於天地之大也人
方憾其覆載之偏寒暑災祥之不得其正而何
有於聖人聖人方惟自盡其心而勢之所值或
有所不及自盡其性而時之所值或有所不能
則聖人亦非不欲盡其心盡其性盡天下之道
之大而擬諸其天而時勢之所乘雖聖人亦無
如之何則聖人將以其無窮之心擬天之德會
道之全故堯舜之不能博施濟衆而兢兢業業
===
行道致孝之心未已也孔子之雖不得位而汲
汲皇皇不倦不厭之心未已也是何也道也天
也顯也微也不物於物而能物物物者也物於物
者氣也質也事也不物於物而能物物者主也
神也機也此道之所以為大也道也天也天地
全之而未窮聖人擬之而未盡窮天地亘古今
莫之能盡為堯舜孔子者亦盡其所以與天無
間者而擬諸其無窮焉若夫天地之所不能堯
舜孔子之所能此又道之無窮而聖人成能之
punctuated: 氣而不盡也，質而不變也，事而不紊也，此天地之全體，聖人之全德。推而極於天地之大也，人方憾其覆載之偏、寒暑災祥之不得其正，而何有於聖人？聖人方惟自盡其心，而勢之所值或有所不及；自盡其性，而時之所值或有所不能。則聖人亦非不欲盡其心、盡其性、盡天下之道之大而擬諸其天，而時勢之所乘，雖聖人亦無如之何。則聖人將以其無窮之心，擬天之德，會道之全。故堯舜之不能博施濟衆，而兢兢業業、行道致孝之心未已也；孔子之雖不得位，而汲汲皇皇、不倦不厭之心未已也。是何也？道也，天也，顯也，微也，不物於物而能物物物者也。物於物者，氣也，質也，事也；不物於物而能物物者，主也，神也，機也。此道之所以為大也。道也，天也，天地全之而未窮，聖人擬之而未盡。窮天地，亘古今，莫之能盡。為堯舜孔子者，亦盡其所以與天無間者，而擬諸其無窮焉。若夫天地之所不能，堯舜孔子之所能，此又道之無窮而聖人成能之
translation_en: …Vital energy is not exhausted, material substance is not altered, and affairs are not thrown into disorder: this is the complete constitution of Heaven and Earth and the complete virtue of the sage. Extending the inquiry to the utmost greatness of Heaven and Earth, people still deplore the partiality of their covering and supporting, and the failure of cold and heat, calamities and auspicious events to attain their proper balance. What, then, can one expect of the sage? The sage seeks only to fulfill his heart to the utmost, yet the circumstances he encounters may leave some things beyond his reach; he seeks to fulfill his nature to the utmost, yet the times he encounters may leave some things beyond his powers. It is not that the sage does not wish to fulfill his heart, fulfill his nature, and realize the full greatness of the Way throughout the world, thereby matching Heaven. Yet even the sage can do nothing about the sway of times and circumstances. Thus, with his inexhaustible heart, the sage seeks to match Heaven’s virtue and comprehend the wholeness of the Way. Hence, although Yao and Shun could not bestow benefits universally and bring relief to the multitude, their conscientious and vigilant resolve to practice the Way and fulfill filial piety never ceased. Although Confucius did not obtain a position, his urgent, anxious resolve, tireless and unwearying, never ceased. Why is this? It is the Way; it is Heaven; it is the manifest and the subtle: it is that which is not made a thing by things but can make things what they are [?]. What is subject to things consists of vital energy, material substance, and affairs; what is not subject to things but can make things what they are is the governing power, the numinous efficacy, and the incipient impulse. This is what makes the Way great. The Way, Heaven—Heaven and Earth embody it fully without exhausting it; the sage emulates it without encompassing it entirely. Throughout Heaven and Earth, across past and present, none can exhaust it. Even such men as Yao, Shun, and Confucius merely realize to the utmost that through which they are undivided from Heaven, and emulate its inexhaustibility. As for what Heaven and Earth cannot accomplish but Yao, Shun, and Confucius can, this again is the inexhaustibility of the Way and the sage’s resolve to bring its capacities to fulfillment…

…the heart never ceases its endeavor. This is the profound meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean, which Master Zhang so subtly apprehended.

Memorial
A memorial of thanks, composed in the voice of Hu Yuan upon his appointment under the Song as Instructor in the Directorate of Education. 〔Fourth year of Huangyou [1052].〕
By Zhang Xu.

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: 〔The historical facts are woven together with the immediacy of things personally seen and heard, while the parallel prose is classical and well regulated, moving freely within the manner of Song memorials. Even if Anding [Hu Yuan] had written his own account, it could scarcely have surpassed this. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: 〔He expounds the institution where exemplary goodness begins and the learning of those first to attain understanding. There is substantiation, argument, and sound organization. Admirable! Admirable!〕
Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: 〔Its language bears upon moral influence and instruction. It deserves inclusion.〕
Comment by Examiner Feng, Professor: 〔Grand and splendid, refined and fluent.〕

On a certain day of a certain month in the fourth year of Huangyou, I humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious favor appointing me Instructor in the Directorate of Education.
In this well-governed age, at a conjunction of prosperity and excellence, ritual gives weight to nurturing worthy men. Your sagely heart extends the benevolence that delights in educating others, and official service honors the charge of directing music. Literary cultivation thus flourishes, and outstanding scholars arise. Holding the imperial pronouncement, I gain new honor; gazing toward the gate of the Imperial University, I feel shame at my inadequacy. title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
米廩殷重瞽宗周人弘北面之風夏后始
東膠之制士兼俊造義取儀刑詩書禮樂
之道以明游息藏修之功咸備蓋設教匪
專於胄子而得人尤賴於眞儒上資啓沃
之功道存規益下藉陶鎔之力學貫淵源
故公孫倡議當時而董子揚言前代風聲
所係模範攸存弘三物以勤民張四維而
立教顧茲重寄謬畀庸流臣托跡海陵志
在丘園之賁潛修嶽麓學求堂奧之升理
===
悟麟經強濯纓於洙泗情懸鳳舘聊奮袂
於蘇湖業分體用之功道切身心之助虛
名久濫無緣咫尺
天光曲學徒勤敢謂振揚風教薦書偶辱
寵命俄頒斗山未仰於當時淵懼深齊韓愈
疏諫素慚於直道寧期爵並陽城六館方
開斂繁華於秋實二南借奏歌雅韻於春
林雲擁賢關星臨文藪聚青衿而至止寧
云衣鉢能傳趨玄室以來思誰謂門墻難
punctuated: 米廩，殷重瞽宗，周人弘北面之風，夏后始東膠之制。士兼俊造，義取儀刑，詩書禮樂之道以明，游息藏修之功咸備。蓋設教匪專於胄子，而得人尤賴於眞儒。上資啓沃之功，道存規益；下藉陶鎔之力，學貫淵源。故公孫倡議當時，而董子揚言前代。風聲所係，模範攸存，弘三物以勤民，張四維而立教。顧茲重寄，謬畀庸流。臣托跡海陵，志在丘園之賁；潛修嶽麓，學求堂奧之升。理悟麟經，強濯纓於洙泗；情懸鳳舘，聊奮袂於蘇湖。業分體用之功，道切身心之助。虛名久濫，無緣咫尺天光；曲學徒勤，敢謂振揚風教？薦書偶辱，寵命俄頒。斗山未仰於當時，淵懼深齊韓愈；疏諫素慚於直道，寧期爵並陽城？六館方開，斂繁華於秋實；二南借奏，歌雅韻於春林。雲擁賢關，星臨文藪，聚青衿而至止，寧云衣鉢能傳？趨玄室以來思，誰謂門墻難
translation_en:
…the Rice Granary school. The Yin honored the Guzong school; the people of Zhou promoted the practice of facing north in reverence to a teacher; and the rulers of Xia inaugurated the Eastern Jiao school. Scholars included both the outstanding and the accomplished, and the guiding principle was to provide exemplary models. Thus the Way of the Odes, Documents, rites, and music was made clear, and every provision was made for learning in recreation and repose, private study and sustained cultivation. Education was established not exclusively for the sons of the nobility; securing worthy men depended above all upon true Confucian scholars. Above, the ruler drew upon their work of enlightening and nourishing his mind, their Way offering correction and benefit; below, students relied upon their power to mold and refine, their learning reaching back to its deepest sources. Thus Gongsun advocated this policy in his day, while Master Dong proclaimed it in an earlier age. Upon them depended the moral influence of education; in them its models were preserved. They promoted the three branches of instruction to encourage the people and upheld the four cardinal bonds to establish moral teaching. Yet this weighty charge has mistakenly been entrusted to an ordinary man like me.

Your servant made his home in Hailing, aspiring to lend distinction to a life of rural retirement. Quietly pursuing study at the mountain’s foot, I sought to ascend into the inner chambers of learning. I apprehended principles in the Classic of the Unicorn, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and strove to wash my cap strings in the Zhu and Si rivers, the waters of Confucian learning. My heart was set upon the Phoenix Hall, and I bestirred myself in Suzhou and Huzhou. My teaching distinguished the work of fundamental principles from that of practical application, while the Way I taught directly aided the cultivation of body and mind. An undeserved reputation has long attached to me, though I have had no opportunity to approach the radiance of Your Majesty. I have merely labored diligently at my narrow learning: dare I claim to have revitalized moral instruction? A letter of recommendation unexpectedly honored me, and Your gracious appointment soon followed. I had not become an object of contemporary reverence like the Northern Dipper or Mount Tai; my profound trepidation equaled that of Han Yu [?]. In submitting remonstrances, I have always felt ashamed of falling short of the upright Way: how could I have expected to hold rank alongside Yang Cheng?

The six colleges now stand open, gathering luxuriant blossoms into autumn fruit. The airs of the Two Nan are performed, their elegant melodies sung through the spring woods. Clouds cluster about the gateway of the worthy; stars shine upon this gathering place of literary talent. Students in blue collars assemble and arrive: could I claim the ability to transmit the robe and bowl of the teaching? They hasten here toward the chamber of profound learning—who would say that the master’s walls are difficult to …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
望光榮不淺庸鄙奚堪茲蓋伏遇
學懋緝熙
德隆廣運灑
宸章於
内苑遠追姚姒之風戲
綵翰於
深宮近繼鍾王之迹萬邦咸正五典攸敦
鳳翥龍翔薄海共風雲之會
===
珠暉玉曜敷天仰奎璧之光治教並明人文
彌著闡六經之道
殊恩每及於儒臣崇四術之傳
聖念特隆於國學謂今時好尚無非詞賦爲先
故學者本原遂致講明無素盈篇月露徒
誇雕篆之工累篋珠璣何補經綸之用獨
以微臣之立教殆爲聖道之真傳分經義
時務之齋功先實學挈明德新民之要習
速靡文拔蔚菲於下僚濟冠裳于
punctuated: 望。光榮不淺，庸鄙奚堪？茲蓋伏遇學懋緝熙，德隆廣運，灑宸章於内苑，遠追姚姒之風；戲綵翰於深宮，近繼鍾王之迹。萬邦咸正，五典攸敦；鳳翥龍翔，薄海共風雲之會；珠暉玉曜，敷天仰奎璧之光。治教並明，人文彌著。闡六經之道，殊恩每及於儒臣；崇四術之傳，聖念特隆於國學。謂今時好尚，無非詞賦爲先，故學者本原，遂致講明無素。盈篇月露，徒誇雕篆之工；累篋珠璣，何補經綸之用？獨以微臣之立教，殆爲聖道之真傳。分經義時務之齋，功先實學；挈明德新民之要，習速靡文。拔蔚菲於下僚，濟冠裳于
translation_en:
…to aspire to. Such glory is no small thing: how could someone as commonplace and unworthy as I bear it? This is because I have humbly encountered Your Majesty, whose learning diligently advances in brightness and whose virtue is vast and far-reaching. You bestow imperial compositions in the inner gardens, distantly following the example of Yao and Si—the sage rulers Shun and Yu; you playfully wield your brilliant brush deep within the palace, more recently following in the traces of Zhong You and Wang Xizhi. The myriad states are all set right, and the five cardinal human relationships are strengthened. Phoenixes soar and dragons fly: all within the seas share this auspicious convergence of wind and cloud. Pearls gleam and jade shines: all beneath heaven look up to the radiance of the Kui and Bi constellations, emblems of literary accomplishment. Governance and instruction alike shine brightly, and cultural refinement becomes ever more manifest.
In expounding the Way of the Six Classics, your exceptional favor repeatedly reaches your Confucian ministers; in honoring the transmission of the four branches of learning, your sagely concern rests especially upon the Imperial University. You observe that contemporary tastes invariably put literary compositions and rhapsodies first, so that scholars have consequently lacked sustained elucidation of the foundations of learning. Pages filled with moonlight and dew merely vaunt skill in ornamental carving; chests piled with pearls and gems of language—what use are they in ordering the realm? Yet you regard the instruction established by your humble servant as perhaps the true transmission of the sages’ Way. By dividing students into halls for classical interpretation and current affairs, its efforts give priority to practical learning; by grasping the essentials of illuminating bright virtue and renewing the people, its practice hastens toward ornate writing [?]. You raise humble plants of little worth [?] from among subordinate officials and bring men in official caps and robes to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
上國臚堂新啓將期四海同仁虎榜弘開何
問六經異旨采藻芹於泮水咸矜
聖代之文植棫樸於黌宮共養
明時之器昔唐崇韻遴而漢賞桓榮是皆德
望之素彰以致甄收之特至自慚末學猥
廁清班臣敢不敷教惟勤作人爲務廣菁
莪之化用期俊乂咸歸仰夏楚之威敢冀
仁賢有就先德行而後文藝昔遠振於遐
方說禮義而敦詩書今近行於太學伏願
===
咸虛納善
晉接推誠
舞干羽于兩階羌夷革面
謳絃歌於萬國海宇歸心英才鼓舞於
洪恩上繼大音遺響多士涵濡於
盛化共揚聖水餘波臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切感戴之至謹奉
表稱
punctuated: 上國。臚堂新啓，將期四海同仁；虎榜弘開，何問六經異旨？采藻芹於泮水，咸矜聖代之文；植棫樸於黌宮，共養明時之器。昔唐崇韻遴，而漢賞桓榮，是皆德望之素彰，以致甄收之特至。自慚末學，猥廁清班。臣敢不敷教惟勤，作人爲務？廣菁莪之化，用期俊乂咸歸；仰夏楚之威，敢冀仁賢有就。先德行而後文藝，昔遠振於遐方；說禮義而敦詩書，今近行於太學。伏願咸虛納善，晉接推誠，舞干羽于兩階，羌夷革面；謳絃歌於萬國，海宇歸心。英才鼓舞於洪恩，上繼大音遺響；多士涵濡於盛化，共揚聖水餘波。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切感戴之至，謹奉表稱
translation_en:
…in the imperial capital. With the hall for ceremonial proclamations newly opened, we look forward to all within the Four Seas sharing in benevolence; with the examination honors list broadly opened, why distinguish among the differing purports of the Six Classics? Gathering water plants and celery beside the school’s pond, all take pride in the literary culture of this sagely age; planting oaks and brushwood in the school precincts, together we nurture men fit to serve this enlightened era. Formerly, the Tang honored Yunlin [?], and the Han rewarded Huan Rong. In both cases, their long-established virtue and reputation brought them exceptional recognition and appointment. Ashamed of my meager learning, I have undeservedly found a place among the honored ranks. How could your servant dare do otherwise than labor diligently at instruction and make nurturing men his task? By extending the nurturing influence celebrated in “Luxuriant Southernwood,” I hope that all outstanding talents will gather here; relying on the authority of the school’s disciplinary rods, I venture to hope that humane and worthy men will attain accomplishment. Giving priority to virtuous conduct over literary skill was formerly a teaching I spread in distant regions; expounding ritual and righteousness and fostering devotion to the Odes and Documents are practices I now pursue nearby at the Imperial University.

I humbly wish that Your Majesty remain open-minded and receptive to good counsel, and show sincerity in granting audiences. Let dances with shields and feather plumes be performed between the two stairways, so that the Qiang and Yi turn toward submission; let songs accompanied by strings resound throughout the myriad states, so that all within the seas give their allegiance. Stirred by Your Majesty’s immense grace, outstanding talents will carry forward the lingering resonance of the great music; steeped in Your Majesty’s flourishing civilizing influence, the many scholars will together spread the continuing waves of the sage’s waters. Gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, your servant cannot contain his profound gratitude and devotion. I respectfully present this memorial to express…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
謝以
聞
第叄場
策
第一問
劉大章
同考試官教諭袁　批　農桑重民衣食我
朝崇本敎化之治正在於此此篇緣述周禮頌敘
聖製典章規度詳悉明顯予眞有用世之具他日敷對
===
大廷以賛
文明之化舍子其誰
考試官學正王　批　能鋪張
列聖修齊之德教養之道可使家傳人誦以厚民生以敦民則以宣
國家禮化之盛
揚我
考試官教授馮　批　有原委有考據有識見
組織事實言由中出宏愽之士也宜錄以
獻
punctuated:
謝以聞。

第叄場，策，第一問。
劉大章。

同考試官教諭袁批：農桑重民衣食，我朝崇本敎化之治正在於此。此篇緣述周禮，頌敘聖製，典章規度詳悉明顯，予眞有用世之具。他日敷對大廷，以賛文明之化，舍子其誰？

考試官學正王批：能鋪張列聖修齊之德、教養之道，可使家傳人誦，以厚民生，以敦民則，以宣國家禮化之盛。揚我。

考試官教授馮批：有原委，有考據，有識見，組織事實，言由中出，宏愽之士也。宜錄以獻。
translation_en:
… to express thanks and submit this for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session: Policy Essay, First Question
Liu Dazhang 劉大章

Comment by Associate Examiner Yuan 袁, Instructor in a county Confucian school: Agriculture and sericulture give due importance to the people’s clothing and food. Precisely here lies our dynasty’s governance, which honors the fundamentals and transforms the people through instruction. This essay draws upon and recounts the Rites of Zhou and praises and expounds the imperial ordinances. Its treatment of institutions and regulations is detailed and clear. “I truly possess the means to serve the world” [?]. When the day comes to present answers at the imperial court and assist its civilizing transformation, who could do so but you?

Comment by Examiner Wang 王, Instructor in a subprefectural Confucian school: This essay amply expounds the successive sage emperors’ virtues of cultivating themselves and regulating their families, and their methods of educating and nurturing the people. It deserves to be transmitted in every household and recited by everyone, to enrich the people’s livelihood, strengthen their moral standards, and proclaim the flourishing transformation wrought by the state’s rites. “Exalt our” [?].

Comment by Examiner Feng 馮, Instructor in a prefectural Confucian school: It traces origins and developments, provides documentary evidence, and displays discernment. It marshals historical facts, and its words come from the heart. This is a scholar of broad learning. His essay should be recorded and presented to the throne.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
何以保治曰民民事者王政之所先也何
以維世曰禮典禮者聖人之所重也先民
事則所以勸農勸桑而建可久之業者自
隆重典禮則所以親耕親蠶而宏可大之
規者自裕農桑之務興而兆民樂康阜之
休耕蠶之儀秩而天下仰文明之治此我
皇祖貽燕翼之善符跡周王而
皇上禮教之盛超駕前古者也其固邦本維世
道垂景休於悠遐卜
===
寶曆於億萬蓋理數之必然矣猗歟盛哉且夫
農桑何始乎耒耜興而稼穡之功殷冠服
制而絲紵之用廣於是生民倚之以為衣
食之源矣耕蠶何昉乎天子藉田千畝以
共粢盛王后必有蠶室以備祭服於是後
世因之以為勸相之政矣昔后稷開周惟
以農事為務其歷世室家能躬織紝之勤
宋儒張栻曰此實王業根本而帝王心法
之要端在乎此則周家享國獨稱長久禮
punctuated:
何以保治？曰民。民事者，王政之所先也。何以維世？曰禮。典禮者，聖人之所重也。先民事，則所以勸農勸桑而建可久之業者自隆；重典禮，則所以親耕親蠶而宏可大之規者自裕。農桑之務興，而兆民樂康阜之休；耕蠶之儀秩，而天下仰文明之治。此我皇祖貽燕翼之善，符跡周王，而皇上禮教之盛，超駕前古者也。其固邦本、維世道、垂景休於悠遐、卜寶曆於億萬，蓋理數之必然矣。猗歟，盛哉！
且夫農桑何始乎？耒耜興，而稼穡之功殷；冠服制，而絲紵之用廣。於是生民倚之以為衣食之源矣。耕蠶何昉乎？天子藉田千畝，以共粢盛；王后必有蠶室，以備祭服。於是後世因之以為勸相之政矣。昔后稷開周，惟以農事為務，其歷世室家能躬織紝之勤。宋儒張栻曰：「此實王業根本，而帝王心法之要端在乎此。」則周家享國獨稱長久，禮
translation_en:
How is good government preserved? Through the people. The people’s livelihood is what kingly government puts first. How is the social order sustained? Through ritual. Ceremonial observances are what the sage esteems. When the people’s livelihood comes first, the means of encouraging agriculture and sericulture and establishing an enduring enterprise naturally flourish. When ceremonial observances are esteemed, the means of personally performing ploughing and sericulture and enlarging a pattern capable of great expansion naturally abound. When agriculture and sericulture flourish, the countless people enjoy the blessings of well-being and plenty; when the ceremonies of ploughing and sericulture are properly ordered, all under Heaven look up to a government of cultural refinement. Such was the excellence of our imperial ancestor’s provision for his descendants, matching the deeds of the kings of Zhou; and such is the magnificence of His Majesty’s instruction through ritual, surpassing earlier ages. That this should strengthen the foundations of the state, sustain the moral order, transmit splendid blessings into the distant future, and presage an imperial reign lasting hundreds of millions of years is surely the inevitable working of principle and destiny. Ah, how magnificent!
Now, how did agriculture and sericulture begin? With the invention of ploughing implements, the work of sowing and harvesting grew abundant; with the institution of caps and robes, the use of silk and ramie became widespread. The people thus came to depend on these as the source of their clothing and food. How did the ceremonies of ploughing and sericulture originate? The Son of Heaven maintained a ritual field of one thousand mu to supply grain for sacrificial offerings, and the queen invariably had a silkworm chamber to provide sacrificial vestments. Later generations accordingly adopted these practices as measures for encouraging and assisting the people. Long ago, Hou Ji laid the foundations of Zhou by devoting himself to agriculture alone, and through successive generations the women of his house personally undertook the toil of weaving. The Song Confucian scholar Zhang Shi said: “This is truly the foundation of kingly enterprise, and herein lies an essential element of the teachings on the mind transmitted by emperors and kings.” Thus the house of Zhou was uniquely renowned for the longevity of its rule, and its ritual …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
制獨稱大備所以垂有令聞者夫豈無因
而致然哉今攷其耕籍之制曰孟春之月
天子親載耒耜而耕矣推止于三節其勞
也撥止丁一限其地也自饗以醴爲交神
也衆勞以酒欲洽情也先種之種先熟之
穉俱藏於宮以有繁育之祥也其諸祈谷
除壇牲祝登收之儀亦罔不備而農業之
興率是矣又攷其親蠶之制曰后妃齋戒
東鄉而桑矣夫人必卜愼其朔也婦女毋
觀務盡力也歲單獻繭報成事也副褘而
受禮少牢也蠶室之築蠶種之浴蠶必於
川爲得潔淨之宜也其諸擇日饗蠶分繭
繅絲之儀亦莫不悉而女紅之兢倡是矣
故以爲醴酪粢盛以爲黼黻文章而王朝
之禮達故以有遺秉滯穗以有素絲綠絲
而阜民之功成此周家典禮之可因而政
治之可述者也自時而後耕籍之君固非
一人西漢之文景東漢之明章唐之太宗
punctuated: 制獨稱大備，所以垂有令聞者，夫豈無因而致然哉？今攷其耕籍之制，曰：孟春之月，天子親載耒耜而耕矣。推止于三，節其勞也；撥止丁一，限其地也；自饗以醴，爲交神也；衆勞以酒，欲洽情也；先種之種，先熟之穉，俱藏於宮，以有繁育之祥也。其諸祈谷、除壇、牲祝、登收之儀，亦罔不備，而農業之興率是矣。又攷其親蠶之制，曰：后妃齋戒，東鄉而桑矣。夫人必卜，愼其朔也；婦女毋觀，務盡力也；歲單獻繭，報成事也；副褘而受，禮少牢也；蠶室之築，蠶種之浴，蠶必於川，爲得潔淨之宜也。其諸擇日、饗蠶、分繭、繅絲之儀，亦莫不悉，而女紅之兢倡是矣。故以爲醴酪粢盛，以爲黼黻文章，而王朝之禮達；故以有遺秉滯穗，以有素絲綠絲，而阜民之功成。此周家典禮之可因，而政治之可述者也。自時而後，耕籍之君固非一人：西漢之文、景，東漢之明、章，唐之太宗
translation_en:
…its ritual institutions alone were praised as fully comprehensive, and it thus bequeathed an excellent reputation. Could this possibly have come about without a reason?

Now, examining its institutions for plowing the ritual field, we find: in the first month of spring, the Son of Heaven personally carried the plow implements in his carriage and performed the plowing. He stopped after three pushes, to moderate his exertion; the turning was limited to one [?], to restrict the ground covered. He himself partook of sweet ale to commune with the spirits; the assembled workers were rewarded with wine to foster harmony of feeling. Seed for early sowing and early-ripening young grain [?] were both stored in the palace as auspicious signs of abundant propagation. The ceremonies for praying for grain, clearing the altar, offering sacrificial animals and invocations, and gathering the harvest were likewise fully provided for. The flourishing of agriculture followed from these practices.

Examining further its institutions for personally tending silkworms, we find: the queen and consorts purified themselves through fasting and gathered mulberry leaves facing east. The noble ladies were required to consult divination, exercising care over the beginning [?]; the women were not to stand watching, but were to devote their full effort to the work. At the completion of the annual work, cocoons were presented to report its accomplishment. Wearing the ceremonial headdress and robe, the queen received them, and the occasion was honored with a lesser animal sacrifice, consisting of a sheep and a pig. Silkworm chambers were built and silkworm eggs bathed; the silkworms had to be tended by a stream [?], to secure the appropriate cleanliness. The ceremonies for selecting a day, making offerings for the silkworms, distributing cocoons, and reeling silk were likewise all fully prescribed. Competitive diligence in women’s textile work was encouraged by these practices.

Thus sweet ale, dairy preparations, and sacrificial grain were produced, as were patterned ritual garments with axe and paired-device embroidery, and the court’s rites were carried out. Thus there were sheaves left behind and ears of grain remaining in the fields, and there were white silk and green silk, accomplishing the work of enriching the people. These are the ritual institutions of the Zhou that may be followed, and the achievements in government that may be emulated.

From that time onward, there was certainly more than one ruler who plowed the ritual field: Emperors Wen and Jing of the Western Han, Emperors Ming and Zhang of the Eastern Han, and Emperor Taizong of the Tang…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
玄宗宋之仁宗高宗則著聲於各代者親
蠶之禮亦非一例西漢於東郊東漢以四
月唐行之貞觀開元宋行之景德宣和則
並記於諸史者然後官御車徒之儀多無
關睢麟趾之意而脩捗祀力穡之政或乏
殊事合敬之文故知農桑之旨眞德秀惟
稱漢之文帝以其能先民事也顧於禮有
未進享農桑之儀馬端臨獨取唐之開元
謂其能重典禮也乃於治未盡善茲固漢
唐宋之造業未純而小康可訾者也欽惟
我
太祖高皇帝
龍飛淮甸肇造區夏念小民所依在衣食則
詔以農桑爲先因國之大事在典禮則政以耕
藉爲重觀諸
諭廷臣曰古者天子藉田千畝自經喪亂其禮
已廢上無以教下無以勸其首舉行之
諭戶部曰什一之制湮奇巧之技作而後農桑
punctuated:
玄宗，宋之仁宗、高宗，則著聲於各代者。親蠶之禮亦非一例：西漢於東郊，東漢以四月，唐行之貞觀、開元，宋行之景德、宣和，則並記於諸史者。然後官御車徒之儀，多無《關睢》《麟趾》之意；而脩捗祀、力穡之政，或乏殊事合敬之文。故知農桑之旨，眞德秀惟稱漢之文帝，以其能先民事也，顧於禮有未進；享農桑之儀，馬端臨獨取唐之開元，謂其能重典禮也，乃於治未盡善。茲固漢、唐、宋之造業未純，而小康可訾者也。
欽惟我太祖高皇帝，龍飛淮甸，肇造區夏。念小民所依在衣食，則詔以農桑爲先；因國之大事在典禮，則政以耕藉爲重。觀諸諭廷臣曰：「古者天子藉田千畝，自經喪亂，其禮已廢，上無以教，下無以勸，其首舉行之。」諭戶部曰：「什一之制湮，奇巧之技作，而後農桑
translation_en:
…Xuanzong, and Renzong and Gaozong of the Song were those renowned in their respective dynasties. The rites of personally tending silkworms likewise followed more than one precedent: under the Western Han they took place in the eastern suburbs; under the Eastern Han, in the fourth month. The Tang performed them during the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan reign periods, and the Song during Jingde and Xuanhe. All these instances are recorded in the histories. Yet the ceremonial arrangements for palace officials, imperial carriages, and attendants [?] often lacked the spirit of “The Ospreys’ Cry” (Guanju) and “The Qilin’s Hooves” (Linzhi). Policies concerning the maintenance of sacrifices [?] and diligent cultivation sometimes lacked the ritual forms through which different activities expressed a common reverence. Thus, concerning an understanding of the purpose of farming and sericulture, Zhen Dexiu praised only Emperor Wen of the Han, because he could take the lead in the people’s work; yet his ritual practice still fell short. Concerning the rites honoring farming and sericulture [?], Ma Duanlin singled out only the Tang’s Kaiyuan period, saying that it gave due weight to ceremonial institutions; yet its government was not wholly good. These were indeed respects in which the foundations laid by the Han, Tang, and Song were imperfect, and their attainment of modest order remained open to criticism.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao rose like a dragon from the Huai region and founded his rule over the Chinese realm. Mindful that the common people depended on clothing and food, he decreed that farming and sericulture should come first. Since the great affairs of the state lay in its ceremonial institutions, he gave particular weight in government to ceremonial plowing. Consider his instruction to the court officials: “In antiquity, the Son of Heaven had a ceremonial plowing field of one thousand mu. Since the devastations of warfare, this rite has fallen into disuse. Those above have no means of teaching, and those below have no means of receiving encouragement. Let this rite be put into practice as a first priority.” He instructed the Ministry of Revenue: “The system of taking one-tenth in taxation fell into abeyance, and crafts devoted to ingenious luxuries arose; thereafter, farming and sericulture…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
之業廢一夫執耒而百家待食一女事織
而百夫待衣欲人無貧不可得也
聖言洋洋何莫而非先民事之發越乎又觀耕
藉田之儀則所謂擇日於仲春之月爲壇
於藉田之北酒齊取夫明水樂章奏乎四
和耕具有裹耕推有因者是已饗先農之
文則所謂緬惟神明造化萬世如斯仰冀
發太古之苗實初生之粟爲民立命服祀
無疆者是已
===
聖制皇皇何莫而非重典禮之軌度乎由是民
事興而根本固造基有類后稷也而論者
以爲
帝謨之宏遠過之由是典禮秩而儀文彰制度
蓋本周官也而說者以爲得天下之正過
之則
聖祖洪猷淵慮所以貽丕緒於無窮而
徽謨駿烈直欲紹華勳於古始者夫豈漢唐
宋諸君可得而擬議其萬一哉
punctuated:
之業廢，一夫執耒而百家待食，一女事織而百夫待衣，欲人無貧，不可得也。」聖言洋洋，何莫而非先民事之發越乎？又觀耕藉田之儀，則所謂擇日於仲春之月，爲壇於藉田之北，酒齊取夫明水，樂章奏乎四和，耕具有裹，耕推有因者是已。饗先農之文，則所謂「緬惟神明，造化萬世如斯。仰冀發太古之苗，實初生之粟，爲民立命，服祀無疆」者是已。
聖制皇皇，何莫而非重典禮之軌度乎？由是民事興而根本固，造基有類后稷也，而論者以爲帝謨之宏遠過之；由是典禮秩而儀文彰，制度蓋本周官也，而說者以爲得天下之正過之。則聖祖洪猷淵慮，所以貽丕緒於無窮，而徽謨駿烈，直欲紹華勳於古始者，夫豈漢唐宋諸君可得而擬議其萬一哉？
translation_en:
…the occupations of farming and sericulture fall into neglect. One man holds the plow while a hundred households await food; one woman works at weaving while a hundred men await clothing. To wish that people should be free from poverty under these circumstances is to wish for the impossible.” How abundant are these sagely words! What part of them does not express the priority accorded to the people’s livelihood?
Consider also the ceremonial procedures for plowing the imperial field: a day is selected in the second month of spring; an altar is constructed north of the imperial field; the ritual wines are prepared with “bright water”; and the music performed is the Four Harmonies. The farming implements have coverings [?], and the pushes of the plow follow an established pattern [?]. Such are its provisions. The text for offering sacrifice to the First Farmer says: “We reflect reverently upon your divine power, which has brought forth and nurtured life through countless ages. We look up in hope that you will make the seedlings of highest antiquity sprout and the earliest grain bear fruit, establishing the people’s livelihood, so that sacrificial service may continue without end.” Such is its language.
How resplendent are these sagely institutions! What part of them does not furnish a standard for honoring ritual? Through them, the people’s occupations flourished and the foundation was secured. In laying this foundation, he resembled Hou Ji, yet commentators hold that the breadth and foresight of his imperial plans surpassed even Hou Ji’s. Through them, the rites were ordered and their ceremonial forms made manifest. His institutions were surely grounded in the Offices of Zhou, yet commentators hold that he surpassed even Zhou in the legitimacy of his acquisition of All under Heaven. Thus the august founder’s vast designs and profound deliberations served to bequeath a mighty dynastic enterprise for all eternity. His admirable plans and great achievements aimed directly to carry forward those of Chonghua and Fangxun—Shun and Yao—from remotest antiquity. How could the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song possibly compare with even one ten-thousandth of his accomplishments?

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承恪遵成憲如
成祖文皇帝巡狩北郡作務本訓以授
仁宗昭皇帝具言農事勤勞以及王業之艱難
宣宗章皇帝嘗歷田野賦織婦詞以示侍臣欲
以耕蠶之狀繪圖而揭之
宮掖固皆有得於
聖祖心法之傳而能隆大重熙累洽之治者也
但親蠶之古制闕如而
聖代之全禮有待肆我
===
皇上備明聖之德
兼述作之善愛民則躕恤之
詔屢下崇禮則
郊廟之制俱隆然猶以農桑藉於勸相而耕蠶
所當並行乃於
萬幾之暇
駕幸西苑相度穀祇蠶壇之位創建
殿宇各區以名有取豳風無逸之文歲時舉
行使中外曉然知
punctuated:
列聖相承，恪遵成憲。如成祖文皇帝巡狩北郡，作《務本訓》以授仁宗昭皇帝，具言農事勤勞以及王業之艱難。宣宗章皇帝嘗歷田野，賦《織婦詞》以示侍臣，欲以耕蠶之狀繪圖而揭之宮掖。固皆有得於聖祖心法之傳，而能隆大重熙累洽之治者也。但親蠶之古制闕如，而聖代之全禮有待。
肆我皇上備明聖之德，兼述作之善。愛民則躕恤之詔屢下，崇禮則郊廟之制俱隆。然猶以農桑藉於勸相，而耕蠶所當並行，乃於萬幾之暇，駕幸西苑，相度穀祇蠶壇之位，創建殿宇，各區以名，有取《豳風》《無逸》之文。歲時舉行，使中外曉然知
translation_en:
The successive sage emperors faithfully observed the established statutes. For example, when Emperor Chengzu Wen toured the northern commanderies, he composed Instructions on Attending to the Fundamentals (Wuben xun) for Emperor Renzong Zhao, explaining fully the toil of farming and the difficulties of the imperial enterprise. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang once traveled through the countryside and composed the Song of the Weaving Woman to show his attendant officials. He wished to have scenes of plowing and silkworm raising painted and displayed within the palace. All these emperors had indeed received the sacred founding emperor’s transmitted teachings of the mind and were thus able to extend and magnify an age of flourishing government and enduring peace. Yet the ancient institution of personally tending silkworms remained unimplemented, and the full ritual order of this sagely dynasty awaited completion.
Thus Our Emperor possesses the virtues of enlightenment and sagacity, combining excellence in carrying on inherited institutions with excellence in creating new ones. In his love for the people, he has repeatedly issued edicts of compassionate concern [?]; in his reverence for ritual, he has fully enhanced the institutions of suburban and ancestral-temple sacrifice. Nevertheless, he considered that agriculture and sericulture depended upon encouragement and assistance, and that ceremonial plowing and silkworm tending ought to be practiced together. Therefore, in an interval between his myriad affairs of state, he proceeded to the Western Park (Xiyuan), surveyed the sites for the altars to the grain deity and the silkworm deity, and established halls and other buildings. Each precinct received a name drawn from the texts of the Airs of Bin and Against Idleness. The ceremonies were performed at their appointed seasons, so that those at court and throughout the realm would clearly understand …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
朝廷之所先者惟民事也其與
聖祖鍾山憫農徒步至淳化門後苑觀穫大喜
農事之畢者不已同符乎哉勤之
宸翰使臣工翕然仰
朝廷之所重者在典禮也其於
聖祖肅備常祀陳其明薦於先農功協稼穡昭
配止及於后稷者不更有烈乎哉由是而
耕者勸于野穡者勸于室可以臻豐穰之
效
===
御製賦所謂以計以遊兮于樂康年是已由是
而粢盛取於斯祭服取於斯可以達明禋
之忱
御製賦所謂至敬承于
皇天是已是故嘉禾合穗于
禁苑瑞麥呈秀于近地而天人協和休徵畢
至夫是之謂大順而愚何以爲
獻哉人亦有言天心仁愛人君聖人仁愛萬
民邇者
punctuated: 朝廷之所先者惟民事也。其與聖祖鍾山憫農，徒步至淳化門，後苑觀穫，大喜農事之畢者，不已同符乎哉？勤之宸翰，使臣工翕然仰朝廷之所重者在典禮也。其於聖祖肅備常祀，陳其明薦於先農，功協稼穡，昭配止及於后稷者，不更有烈乎哉？由是而耕者勸于野，穡者勸于室，可以臻豐穰之效。御製賦所謂「以計以遊兮，于樂康年」，是已。由是而粢盛取於斯，祭服取於斯，可以達明禋之忱。御製賦所謂「至敬承于皇天」，是已。是故嘉禾合穗于禁苑，瑞麥呈秀于近地，而天人協和，休徵畢至。夫是之謂大順，而愚何以爲獻哉？人亦有言：「天心仁愛人君，聖人仁愛萬民。」邇者
translation_en:
…that what the court puts first is the livelihood of the people. Does this not accord with the Sagely Ancestor’s concern for the farmers at Zhongshan, his walking to Chunhua Gate, and his watching the harvest in the rear park, greatly rejoicing at the completion of the farm work? His imperial calligraphy exhorts them [?], causing all his officials with one accord to look up in reverence to the court’s emphasis on ritual observances. Compared with the Sagely Ancestor’s solemn provision for the regular sacrifices, his presentation of pure offerings to the First Farmer, and his inclusion of Hou Ji alone as the associated recipient because of his contributions to agriculture, are these achievements not still more illustrious? Thus those who plow are encouraged in the fields, and those who harvest are encouraged indoors [?], bringing about abundant yields. This is what the imperially composed rhapsody means by: “Planning and roaming [?], ah, rejoicing in a year of plenty.” Thus the sacrificial grain is obtained here, and the sacrificial robes are obtained here, allowing sincere devotion to be expressed in pure sacrifice. This is what the imperially composed rhapsody means by: “With utmost reverence, serving August Heaven.”

Hence auspicious grain bears joined ears in the imperial park, and auspicious wheat puts forth ears nearby; Heaven and humanity are in harmony, and favorable portents arrive in full array. This is what is called the Great Accord. What, then, can I in my ignorance offer? There is also a saying: “Heaven’s heart benevolently cherishes the ruler; the sage benevolently cherishes the myriad people.” Recently…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
皇上因京邑遇雨水則錢米之給徧於市屢見
守臣報災傷則蠲貸之議責於計部是
仁愛萬民之心又有出於勸農桑典禮之外
者矣以是而答
天心之仁愛以是而迓滋至之休禎
皇圖鞏固蓋將與天地相為悠久彼八百之姬
曆奚足言哉區區芹曝之私所欲入告者
如此幸轉而聞之於
上
===
第二問　　　　　　　　田稔
同考試官教諭林　批　〔周禮經世大典間有疑處不害全體之可信子能根極底蘊足見素學〕
同考試官教諭趙　批　〔周禮此篇考訂明備庶得周公之心而無疑者後世類以漢儒附會疑〕
考試官學正王　批　〔禮待人而行師其意而不泥其迹此作得之〕
考試官教授馮　批　〔援據明確能釋經疑〕
punctuated:
皇上因京邑遇雨水，則錢米之給徧於市；屢見守臣報災傷，則蠲貸之議責於計部。是仁愛萬民之心，又有出於勸農桑典禮之外者矣。以是而答天心之仁愛，以是而迓滋至之休禎，皇圖鞏固，蓋將與天地相為悠久。彼八百之姬曆，奚足言哉！區區芹曝之私，所欲入告者如此，幸轉而聞之於上。

第二問　田稔

同考試官教諭林批〔周禮，經世大典，間有疑處，不害全體之可信。子能根極底蘊，足見素學。〕

同考試官教諭趙批〔周禮，此篇考訂明備，庶得周公之心而無疑者。後世類以漢儒附會疑。〕

考試官學正王批〔禮待人而行，師其意而不泥其迹，此作得之。〕

考試官教授馮批〔援據明確，能釋經疑。〕
translation_en:
…when the capital suffered from excessive rain and flooding, His Majesty had cash and rice distributed throughout the city; whenever he saw reports of disaster and damage from local officials, he charged the Ministry of Revenue with deliberating on tax remissions and relief loans. This benevolent concern for all the people thus extends beyond the established rites for encouraging agriculture and sericulture. By these means he answers Heaven’s benevolent concern and welcomes auspicious blessings arriving in increasing abundance. The imperial dominion, firmly secured, will surely endure as long as Heaven and Earth. What, then, are the eight hundred years of the Ji house of Zhou worth mentioning? Such is what I wish to submit, in my humble sincerity—like one offering celery or the warmth of the sun. I beg that you convey it to His Majesty.

Second Policy Question — Tian Ren 田稔

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, County School Instructor: 〔The Rites of Zhou is a great canon for governing the world. Occasional doubtful passages do not impair the trustworthiness of the whole. Your ability to probe its deepest meanings amply demonstrates your accumulated learning.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, County School Instructor: 〔This essay’s examination and verification of the Rites of Zhou are clear and comprehensive; it comes close to grasping the Duke of Zhou’s intentions and leaving no room for doubt. Later generations have generally doubted it as a contrived construction by Han scholars [?].〕

Comment by Examiner Wang, Subprefectural School Instructor: 〔Rites depend upon people to put them into practice. One should follow their underlying intent without clinging rigidly to their outward forms. This essay grasps that principle.〕

Comment by Examiner Feng, Prefectural School Instructor: 〔Its supporting citations are clear and precise, enabling it to resolve doubts about the classic.〕

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
古之聖人所以制禮於天下以垂範於無
窮者其理至微也是故善於釋經者要之
於理而後可以識聖人之心善於制治者
揆之於理而後可以用聖人之法釋經而
不要之於理則其所以討論之者非惟不
足以明聖人之心而適以滋天下後世之
惑制治而不揆之於理則其所以效法之
者非惟不足以善當時之治而適以來天
下後世之譏葢泥於其迹而不求其不言
===
之意拘于其法而不達其變通之宜此聖
人之經所以益晦於天下也執事以周禮
下策承學而有及於後世紛紛之論葢欲
求聖人之心於千載之上以決萬世之疑
也而愚也敢不據理以對夫周禮周公作
也周公旣以其道相成王以隆一代之治
而又懼天下後世之無以為法也於是因
禮作焉其經畫措置以維持乎天下者甚
悉錯綜斟酌以經綸乎天下者甚密葢監
punctuated:
古之聖人所以制禮於天下，以垂範於無窮者，其理至微也。是故善於釋經者，要之於理，而後可以識聖人之心；善於制治者，揆之於理，而後可以用聖人之法。釋經而不要之於理，則其所以討論之者，非惟不足以明聖人之心，而適以滋天下後世之惑；制治而不揆之於理，則其所以效法之者，非惟不足以善當時之治，而適以來天下後世之譏。葢泥於其迹而不求其不言之意，拘于其法而不達其變通之宜，此聖人之經所以益晦於天下也。
執事以《周禮》下策承學，而有及於後世紛紛之論，葢欲求聖人之心於千載之上，以決萬世之疑也。而愚也敢不據理以對？夫《周禮》，周公作也。周公旣以其道相成王，以隆一代之治，而又懼天下後世之無以為法也，於是因禮作焉。其經畫措置以維持乎天下者甚悉，錯綜斟酌以經綸乎天下者甚密。葢監
translation_en:
The principles by which the sages of antiquity established rites throughout the realm, to provide models for all time, are exceedingly subtle. Thus, those skilled in interpreting the classics must seek their essentials in principle before they can understand the sages’ intentions; those skilled in establishing government must assess it against principle before they can apply the sages’ methods. If interpreters of the classics do not seek their essentials in principle, their discussions will not merely fail to clarify the sages’ intentions: they will instead compound the perplexities of later generations throughout the realm. If those establishing government do not assess it against principle, their imitation will not merely fail to improve the government of their own time: it will instead invite the criticism of later generations throughout the realm. They cling to outward traces without seeking the unspoken meaning, and confine themselves to established methods without understanding how these should be adapted to circumstances. This is why the sages’ classics become ever more obscure in the world.
You, honored examiners, have set students a policy question on the Rites of Zhou (Zhou li), touching upon the many conflicting discussions of later ages. Your purpose, surely, is to recover the sages’ intentions from a thousand years ago and resolve the doubts of all generations to come. How could I, ignorant though I am, dare to reply without grounding myself in principle? The Rites of Zhou was composed by the Duke of Zhou. Having assisted King Cheng in accordance with his Way and brought the government of an entire age to greatness, the Duke of Zhou further feared that later generations throughout the realm would have no model to follow. He therefore composed this work on the basis of the rites. Its plans and arrangements for sustaining the realm were exceedingly comprehensive; its coordination and careful weighing of measures for ordering the realm were exceedingly meticulous. For he took as his model…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
二代之禮集百聖之成盡善盡美而可以
垂範於無窮也柰之何法度湊夷於衰周
之世而諸侯皆去其籍墳典燬棄於暴秦
之時而博士始失其官漢文除挾書之律
而求之不盡其方孝武開獻書之路而讀
之不盡其意是以河間王之所獻者深藏
于秘府劉更生之所校者僅著于錄畧而
諸儒之疑由此起矣而不知折之於理則
有不必疑者自今觀之設官分職非異於
===
周官也周書舉其槩以明一代之制而周
禮盡其詳以定萬世之規詳畧異名固不
必其盡同也列爵分土非殊於王制也王
制始于漢儒之掇拾而周禮出於周公之
裁成先後異時固不必其皆合也謂考工
記之可以補冬官非見之定者也審曲面
勢不足以煩六卿之貴飭材辯器不足以
語邦國之治强以合之而劉子駿之謬不
可得而辭矣謂冬官之亡其篇帙非識之
punctuated:
二代之禮，集百聖之成，盡善盡美，而可以垂範於無窮也。柰之何法度湊夷於衰周之世，而諸侯皆去其籍；墳典燬棄於暴秦之時，而博士始失其官。漢文除挾書之律，而求之不盡其方；孝武開獻書之路，而讀之不盡其意。是以河間王之所獻者，深藏于秘府；劉更生之所校者，僅著于錄畧，而諸儒之疑由此起矣。而不知折之於理，則有不必疑者。
自今觀之，設官分職，非異於《周官》也。《周書》舉其槩，以明一代之制，而《周禮》盡其詳，以定萬世之規。詳畧異名，固不必其盡同也。列爵分土，非殊於《王制》也。《王制》始于漢儒之掇拾，而《周禮》出於周公之裁成。先後異時，固不必其皆合也。
謂《考工記》之可以補《冬官》，非見之定者也。審曲面勢，不足以煩六卿之貴；飭材辯器，不足以語邦國之治。强以合之，而劉子駿之謬不可得而辭矣。謂《冬官》之亡其篇帙，非識之
translation_en:
…the rites of the two preceding dynasties, bringing together the accomplishments of the hundred sages, attaining perfect goodness and beauty, and providing a model for all time. Yet how was it that institutions and regulations fell into ruin [?] during the declining Zhou, and the feudal lords all discarded their records; that ancient writings were burned and abandoned under the violent Qin, and the Erudites then lost their offices? Emperor Wen of Han abolished the law against possessing books, but did not exhaust the means of seeking them out. Emperor Xiaowu opened channels for presenting books, but did not fully grasp their meaning when reading them. Thus what the Prince of Hejian presented lay buried deep in the palace repositories, while what Liu Gengsheng collated was merely listed in a bibliographical outline. From this arose the doubts of the various scholars. They did not realize that, if judged by principle, some matters need not be doubted.
Viewed from the present, its establishment of offices and division of duties do not differ from the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). The Documents of Zhou (Zhoushu) gives the broad outlines to illuminate the institutions of one dynasty, whereas the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) sets out every detail to establish standards for all ages. Differing in fullness and bearing different titles, they need not be identical in every respect. Its assignment of ranks and division of territory do not differ from the Royal Regulations (Wangzhi). The Royal Regulations originated in the compilations of Han scholars, whereas the Rites of Zhou emerged from the Duke of Zhou’s considered formulation. Produced at different times, earlier and later, they need not agree in every respect.
To claim that the Record of Artificers (Kaogong ji) can fill the place of the Offices of Winter (Dongguan) is not a sound judgment. Examining curves and assessing configurations does not warrant troubling so exalted a personage as one of the six ministers; preparing materials and distinguishing implements is insufficient for discussing the governance of the states. In forcing the two together, Liu Zijun cannot escape responsibility for his error. To claim that the Offices of Winter has been lost as a textual division is not an understanding that …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
真者也邦禁邦土見於六官之中縣師壓
人雜於地官之屬訂而正之而王次黠之
論不可得而뽐矣天官冢宰所以佐王均
邦國也而其所統者乃有及於中門之禁
若似於褻矣而不知古之大臣所以保王
之躬者皆於是乎在也五峯胡氏之所見
亦烏得爲至論乎秋官司寇所以佐王刑
邦國也而其所統者乃有及於賓客之禮
若似於濫矣而不知朝覲會同所以威不
===
庭之臣者皆於是乎在也鄭康成之所校
亦烏可得而輕議乎國服爲息此後世興
利之臣所以行其私也而不知泉人之所
貸者不過市之不售貨之不通因民之所
願以授之而已矣又寧有利上之心乎屬
民讀法此後世五教之興所以飾其詐也
而不知州長之所掌者不過以歲時祭祀
州社因民之會以聚之而已矣又安有擾
民之患乎漿人鹽人典絲典枲之官其職
punctuated: 真者也。邦禁、邦土見於六官之中，縣師、壓人雜於地官之屬，訂而正之，而王次黠之論不可得而뽐矣。天官冢宰所以佐王均邦國也，而其所統者乃有及於中門之禁，若似於褻矣，而不知古之大臣所以保王之躬者，皆於是乎在也。五峯胡氏之所見，亦烏得爲至論乎？秋官司寇所以佐王刑邦國也，而其所統者乃有及於賓客之禮，若似於濫矣，而不知朝覲會同所以威不庭之臣者，皆於是乎在也。鄭康成之所校，亦烏可得而輕議乎？國服爲息，此後世興利之臣所以行其私也，而不知泉人之所貸者，不過市之不售、貨之不通，因民之所願以授之而已矣，又寧有利上之心乎？屬民讀法，此後世五教之興所以飾其詐也，而不知州長之所掌者，不過以歲時祭祀州社，因民之會以聚之而已矣，又安有擾民之患乎？漿人、鹽人、典絲、典枲之官，其職
translation_en:
…is not a true understanding. Prohibitions throughout the realm and the administration of its lands appear among the six ministries; the County Masters and the Yaren [?] are interspersed among the officials of the Ministry of Earth. Once these are examined and corrected, Wang Cixia’s [?] argument can no longer be [the final verb is corrupt: 뽐]. The Celestial Office’s Minister of State assists the king in bringing order to the states, yet his jurisdiction extends even to restrictions at the inner gate. This might seem beneath his dignity, but such a view fails to recognize that precisely these matters embodied the means by which the great ministers of antiquity safeguarded the king’s person. How, then, can the views of Hu Wufeng be considered definitive? The Autumn Office’s Minister of Justice assists the king in administering punishments throughout the states, yet his jurisdiction extends even to ceremonial treatment of guests. This might seem an excessive reach, but such a view fails to recognize that court audiences and assemblies embodied the means of overawing ministers who failed to attend court. How, then, can Zheng Kangcheng’s textual collation be lightly criticized?

“Taking state service as the basis for interest”: this is what later ministers intent on increasing revenues used to advance their private interests. Yet this criticism fails to recognize that the loans made by the Treasury Officer [?] concerned only goods that remained unsold in the market or failed to circulate; they were granted simply in accordance with the people’s wishes. How could there have been any intention of enriching those above? “Assembling the people to read out the laws”: the later institution of the Five Teachings [?] used this to disguise its deceit. Yet this criticism fails to recognize that the District Chief’s responsibility extended only to seasonal sacrifices at the district’s altar of the soil, taking advantage of the people’s gatherings to assemble them. How could there have been any danger of harassing the people? As for the offices of the Beverage Officer, Salt Officer, Silk Officer, and Hemp Officer, their duties…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
可謂賤矣以太宰之尊而統之此其迹之
有可疑者而不知大臣愛君之心固當無
所不用其至也大祝甸祝詛祝司巫之官
其事可謂鄙矣以宗伯之要而統之此其
理之有可疑者而不知君子防患之道自
當無所不用其慮也廛人之在地官所以
掌斂市之布以入泉府也而有所謂絘布
總布質布罰布廛布蓋市廛逐末之民不
可以不抑而務本力穡之道不可以不興
===
也是可以為苛乎載師之屬司徒所以掌
任土之法以制地事也而有所謂宅田士
田及有所謂賈田蓋府史之在官不得以
受田而賈人之家人固可以自力也是可
以為泛乎夫聖人之所以慮天下者如此
其至所以防天下者如此其詳而後之儒
者拘一時之見以恣其倡狂無據之論執
一偏之說以逞其用已自私之心是以見
周禮之明於制地也則以為六國陰謀之
punctuated: 可謂賤矣。以太宰之尊而統之，此其迹之有可疑者，而不知大臣愛君之心，固當無所不用其至也。大祝、甸祝、詛祝、司巫之官，其事可謂鄙矣。以宗伯之要而統之，此其理之有可疑者，而不知君子防患之道，自當無所不用其慮也。廛人之在地官，所以掌斂市之布，以入泉府也，而有所謂絘布、總布、質布、罰布、廛布。蓋市廛逐末之民，不可以不抑，而務本力穡之道，不可以不興也。是可以為苛乎？載師之屬司徒，所以掌任土之法，以制地事也，而有所謂宅田、士田，及有所謂賈田。蓋府史之在官，不得以受田，而賈人之家人，固可以自力也。是可以為泛乎？夫聖人之所以慮天下者如此其至，所以防天下者如此其詳，而後之儒者，拘一時之見，以恣其倡狂無據之論；執一偏之說，以逞其用已自私之心。是以見《周禮》之明於制地也，則以為六國陰謀之
translation_en:
…may be called lowly. That they should be supervised by so exalted an official as the Grand Administrator may appear questionable in practice. Yet this overlooks the fact that a great minister’s devotion to his ruler must extend to the utmost in every respect. The offices of Grand Invocator, Field Invocator, Invocator of Curses, and Director of Shamans may be said to perform humble duties. That they should be supervised by so important an official as the Minister of Rites may appear questionable in principle. Yet this overlooks the fact that the gentleman, in guarding against misfortune, must consider every possible contingency.

The Market Tax Collector belongs to the Ministry of Education in order to collect monetary levies from the markets and remit them to the Treasury Office. These include the so-called stall levy, general levy, contract levy, penalty levy, and shop levy. People in the markets who pursue the secondary occupation of commerce must be restrained, while devotion to the fundamental occupation and diligent cultivation must be encouraged. Can this be considered oppressive?

The Land Supervisor is subordinate to the Minister of Education in order to administer the regulations for allocating land to its uses and thereby regulate affairs concerning land. There are the so-called residential lands and officers’ lands, as well as the so-called merchants’ lands. For storekeepers and scribes serving in government offices are not entitled to receive land, while members of merchants’ households can certainly support themselves by their own efforts. Can this be considered indiscriminate?

The sage’s consideration for the world is thus utterly thorough, and his provisions against its troubles are thus meticulous. Yet later Confucian scholars, confined by the views of their own time, give free rein to their wild and unfounded arguments; clinging to one-sided doctrines, they indulge their determination to follow their own judgment and serve their private interests. Thus, when they see how clearly the Rites of Zhou sets out the regulation of land, they take it to be a book of covert schemes of the Six States…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
書見周禮之異於他經也則以為漢儒附
會之書見周禮之詳於財賦也則以為成
周理財之書見周禮之難於舉行也則以
為瀆亂不經之書是皆識聖人之淺者也
而烏可以為周禮病乎乃若王通隋之隱
君子也則欲執此以往以庶幾周公於千
載之上唐太宗世之英主也則以為真聖
人之作而欲復興周道於千載之下愽綜
群書莫鄭康成若也則以為周公致太平
===
之迹而作論以排林氏之非折衷諸論莫
朱子若也則以為聖賢制作之書而設喻
以明治平之本蓋虛吾之心以求聖人之
經據吾之理以折群言之亂此周禮之所
以未泯也而當時之用之者或假而用之
或輕而用之或用之而自私其說或用之
而不免於疑是以周禮之行於新室也則
謂之僭行於宇文也則謂之虛行於荊舒
也則謂之謬行於有唐也則謂之惑然則
punctuated: 書；見周禮之異於他經也，則以為漢儒附會之書；見周禮之詳於財賦也，則以為成周理財之書；見周禮之難於舉行也，則以為瀆亂不經之書。是皆識聖人之淺者也，而烏可以為周禮病乎？乃若王通，隋之隱君子也，則欲執此以往，以庶幾周公於千載之上；唐太宗，世之英主也，則以為真聖人之作，而欲復興周道於千載之下；愽綜群書，莫鄭康成若也，則以為周公致太平之迹，而作論以排林氏之非；折衷諸論，莫朱子若也，則以為聖賢制作之書，而設喻以明治平之本。蓋虛吾之心以求聖人之經，據吾之理以折群言之亂，此周禮之所以未泯也。而當時之用之者，或假而用之，或輕而用之，或用之而自私其說，或用之而不免於疑。是以周禮之行於新室也，則謂之僭；行於宇文也，則謂之虛；行於荊舒也，則謂之謬；行於有唐也，則謂之惑。然則，
translation_en:
…a book; when they see that the Rites of Zhou differs from the other classics, they regard it as a book of strained constructions by Han scholars; when they see its detailed treatment of revenue and taxation, they regard it as a book on financial administration in the Zhou dynasty; when they see the difficulty of putting it into practice, they regard it as a disorderly, disruptive book contrary to canonical principles. All these judgments reflect a shallow understanding of the sage. How could they establish any fault in the Rites of Zhou?

Wang Tong, a gentleman living in retirement under the Sui, wished to proceed with this book as his guide, hoping to approach the achievement of the Duke of Zhou a thousand years before. Emperor Taizong of Tang, an outstanding ruler of his age, considered it truly the work of a sage and wished to revive the Way of Zhou a thousand years later. None surpassed Zheng Kangcheng in comprehensive learning across the books; he considered it a record of how the Duke of Zhou brought about supreme peace, and wrote a discourse to refute Master Lin’s criticisms. None surpassed Master Zhu in weighing and reconciling diverse arguments; he considered it a book of institutions established by sages and worthies, and used an analogy to illuminate the foundation of order and peace. It is by emptying our minds of preconceptions to seek the sage’s classic, and relying on our grasp of principle to resolve the confusion of competing claims, that the Rites of Zhou has survived.

Yet among those who applied it in their own times, some used it as a pretext, some applied it rashly, some applied it while turning its teachings to their private ends, and some applied it without escaping doubt. Thus, when the Rites of Zhou was implemented under the Xin dynasty, this was called usurpation; under the Yuwen regime, empty show; under the Duke of Jing and Shu [Wang Anshi], error; and under the Tang, delusion. If that is so, then…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
周禮之所以治天下者乃所以禍天下聖
人之所以範後人者乃所以誤後人而周
禮之不幸於是甚矣嗚呼識聖人之心則
雖訓詁音釋之不能以盡合亦不害其爲
明經師聖人之意則雖設官分職之不能
以皆同亦不害其爲善治否則飾之以小
智穿鑿之私而不探其大滯之以好古尚
文之見而不通其變毋惑乎紛紛之多疑
也抑又有說焉程子曰必有關雎麟趾之
===
意然後可以行周官之法度言周禮之不
可以輕用也張子曰周禮一書其間必有
增入者言周禮之不可以盡信也朱子亦
有言曰周公之爲周禮猶唐之顯慶開元
禮也僅述大略俟其臨事而損益之言周
禮之當變易以從時也夫程子之言信而
信者也張子之言信而疑者也朱子之言
疑而信者也然則疑周禮者不可以盡非
而信周禮者亦不可以盡是疑周禮者周
punctuated:
周禮之所以治天下者，乃所以禍天下；聖人之所以範後人者，乃所以誤後人，而周禮之不幸於是甚矣。嗚呼！識聖人之心，則雖訓詁音釋之不能以盡合，亦不害其爲明經；師聖人之意，則雖設官分職之不能以皆同，亦不害其爲善治。否則，飾之以小智穿鑿之私，而不探其大；滯之以好古尚文之見，而不通其變，毋惑乎紛紛之多疑也。

抑又有說焉。程子曰：「必有關雎麟趾之意，然後可以行周官之法度。」言周禮之不可以輕用也。張子曰：「周禮一書，其間必有增入者。」言周禮之不可以盡信也。朱子亦有言曰：「周公之爲周禮，猶唐之顯慶開元禮也，僅述大略，俟其臨事而損益之。」言周禮之當變易以從時也。夫程子之言，信而信者也；張子之言，信而疑者也；朱子之言，疑而信者也。然則疑周禮者，不可以盡非；而信周禮者，亦不可以盡是。疑周禮者，周
translation_en:
…the means by which the Rites of Zhou brings order to the world become the means by which it brings calamity upon the world; the means by which the sage provides a model for later generations become the means by which he misleads them. The misfortune of the Rites of Zhou is thus extreme indeed! Alas! If one understands the sage’s heart, then even without complete agreement in textual glosses and explanations of pronunciation, one may still understand the classic. If one takes the sage’s intent as one’s guide, then even without complete conformity in establishing offices and allocating duties, one may still govern well. Otherwise, one embellishes it with the private conceits of petty cleverness and strained interpretations, without probing its larger meaning; one becomes mired in a preference for antiquity and formal refinement, without comprehending its adaptability. It is no wonder that doubts arise in such profusion.

There is yet another point to make. Master Cheng said: “Only when one possesses the spirit of ‘The Ospreys’ (Guanju) and ‘The Qilin’s Hooves’ (Linzhi) can one implement the laws and institutions of the Offices of Zhou.” This means that the Rites of Zhou must not be put into practice lightly. Master Zhang said: “Within the book Rites of Zhou, there must be passages that were added later.” This means that the Rites of Zhou cannot be trusted in its entirety. Master Zhu also said: “The Duke of Zhou’s composition of the Rites of Zhou was like the Tang ritual codes of the Xianqing and Kaiyuan eras: it merely set out the broad outlines, leaving additions and subtractions to be made as actual circumstances arose.” This means that the Rites of Zhou ought to be modified to accord with the times. Master Cheng’s words express belief grounded in belief; Master Zhang’s express doubt within belief; Master Zhu’s express belief within doubt. Thus, those who doubt the Rites of Zhou cannot be judged wholly wrong, nor can those who believe in it be judged wholly right. When people doubt the Rites of Zhou, the Rites …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
禮猶存而誤用周禮則周禮亡矣愚欲舉
三子之說以曉天下後世之泥於周禮者
而未敢以爲然也惟執事進而教之幸甚
第三問
張詡
同考試官教諭黃　批
諸儒孔宋已有定論而考〔陳明實抑揚不謬蓋嘗究心若予之儒而知所〕
決擇者
同考試官教諭蔡　批
歷論漢唐宋諸儒而我〔朝道學之盛闡揚益明蓋究心理性者〕
===
考試官學正王　批
鑒別精明條荅詳盡
考試官教授馮　批
稱仰有宗徵予素志
理析於諸儒而斯道無一定之見理會於
真儒而學者有一定之守何則古今之不
同者人而其同者心也古今之不同者心
而其同者道也故不衍其緒無以昭繼往
之功不體其全何以集大成之妙此諸儒
衛道之功固不可少而真儒兼總之妙又
punctuated:
禮猶存，而誤用周禮，則周禮亡矣。愚欲舉三子之說，以曉天下後世之泥於周禮者，而未敢以爲然也。惟執事進而教之，幸甚。
第三問
張詡
同考試官教諭黃批：諸儒孔宋已有定論，而考〔陳明實，抑揚不謬，蓋嘗究心若予之儒而知所〕決擇者。
同考試官教諭蔡批：歷論漢唐宋諸儒，而我〔朝道學之盛，闡揚益明，蓋究心理性者〕。
考試官學正王批：鑒別精明，條荅詳盡。
考試官教授馮批：稱仰有宗，徵予素志。
理析於諸儒，而斯道無一定之見；理會於真儒，而學者有一定之守。何則？古今之不同者，人，而其同者，心也；古今之不同者，心，而其同者，道也。故不衍其緒，無以昭繼往之功；不體其全，何以集大成之妙？此諸儒衛道之功固不可少，而真儒兼總之妙又
translation_en:
…the Rites of Zhou still survives; but if the Rites of Zhou is misapplied, then the Rites of Zhou is lost. I would venture to present the explanations of these three masters to enlighten those throughout the world and in later generations who adhere rigidly to the Rites of Zhou, yet I dare not presume that my view is correct. I would be most fortunate if you would offer further instruction.
Third policy question
Zhang Xu
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Concerning the various Confucian scholars, ‘Confucius and the Song’ already have an established judgment [?]; his examination 〔and exposition are clear and substantial, his praise and criticism free of error. He has evidently devoted thought to scholars ‘such as myself’ [?] and knows how to〕 make discerning choices.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “He discusses in succession the Confucian scholars of the Han, Tang, and Song, and the flourishing of the Learning of the Way under our 〔dynasty is expounded with still greater clarity. He evidently devotes thought to principle and human nature〕.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “His discrimination is perceptive and clear; his answers to the individual points are detailed and exhaustive.”
Comment by Examiner Feng, Professor: “His praise and admiration have an authoritative basis and bear out my longstanding convictions.”
When principle is analyzed separately among the various Confucian scholars, there is no settled understanding of this Way; when principle is comprehended as a whole by a true Confucian, learners have a settled standard to uphold. Why is this? What differs between antiquity and the present is the people; what they share is the mind. What differs between antiquity and the present is the mind; what they share is the Way. Thus, without extending the inherited thread, there is no means to manifest the achievement of carrying forward the past; without embodying the whole, how can one attain the subtle mastery of bringing all together into a great synthesis? The contributions of the various Confucian scholars in defending the Way are certainly indispensable, while the subtle mastery with which a true Confucian embraces and integrates them also…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
不可不會其全也歟請因明問而悉陳之
儒之名何由立也粤自太極判而陰陽分
淑氣鍾而哲人出在當時則爲聖爲賢爲
士爲君子今之所謂儒者非古之所謂士
君子乎孔孟而後賢人邈矣漢初尚經術
其後尚節義然而學春秋者失之誣學尚
書者失之刻稽古而留情車馬服裘而有
意近名吾未見其得宗於孔子也幸而有
天人三策仲舒得儒者之醇出師二表孔
===
明近王者之佐雖未得師於孔子而其言
亦得宗於孔子矣唐初尚詞騷其後尚疏
奏然而善謀斷者道之未聞能書史者德
之有愧吟詠發放逸之狂上章非正學之
本吾未見其有功於孟子也幸而有宣公
奏議敷演仁義之七篇昌黎原道振起斯
文於八代雖其人不孟子而其功亦得齊
於孟子矣至於有宋眞儒輩出周子玉淵
金井默契道體者也而人乃言其不由師
punctuated:
不可不會其全也歟？請因明問而悉陳之。
儒之名何由立也？粤自太極判而陰陽分，淑氣鍾而哲人出，在當時則爲聖、爲賢、爲士、爲君子。今之所謂儒者，非古之所謂士君子乎？孔孟而後，賢人邈矣。漢初尚經術，其後尚節義。然而學春秋者失之誣，學尚書者失之刻；稽古而留情車馬，服裘而有意近名，吾未見其得宗於孔子也。幸而有天人三策，仲舒得儒者之醇；出師二表，孔明近王者之佐。雖未得師於孔子，而其言亦得宗於孔子矣。唐初尚詞騷，其後尚疏奏。然而善謀斷者道之未聞，能書史者德之有愧；吟詠發放逸之狂，上章非正學之本，吾未見其有功於孟子也。幸而有宣公奏議，敷演仁義之七篇；昌黎原道，振起斯文於八代。雖其人不孟子，而其功亦得齊於孟子矣。至於有宋，眞儒輩出。周子玉淵金井，默契道體者也，而人乃言其不由師
translation_en:
…must one not also comprehend it in its entirety? Allow me to respond to your illuminating question by setting it all forth.
How did the designation “Confucian scholar” arise? Ever since the Supreme Ultimate divided and yin and yang separated, pure vital energies have gathered and men of wisdom have emerged. In their own times they were called sages, worthies, scholars, and gentlemen. Are those now called Confucian scholars not those whom antiquity called scholars and gentlemen? After Kongzi and Mengzi, worthy men became rare indeed. In the early Han, learning in the Classics was esteemed; later, moral integrity and righteousness were esteemed. Yet those who studied the Spring and Autumn Annals erred in unfounded claims, and those who studied the Book of Documents erred in harshness. They investigated antiquity yet remained attached to carriages and horses; they wore fur robes yet sought a reputation. I have not seen that they succeeded in taking Kongzi as their guiding authority. Fortunately, there were the Three Policy Responses on Heaven and Man, in which Dong Zhongshu attained the purity of a Confucian scholar, and the two Memorials on Dispatching the Army, in which Zhuge Kongming approached the stature of an adviser to a true king. Though they could not study under Kongzi, their words nevertheless took Kongzi as their guiding authority.
In the early Tang, ornate verse was esteemed; later, memorials to the throne were esteemed. Yet those skilled in planning and decision had not heard the Way, and those capable of writing history fell short in virtue. Their verse gave vent to unrestrained wildness, and their submissions to the throne were not grounded in orthodox learning. I have not seen that they rendered service to the teachings of Mengzi. Fortunately, there were the memorials of Lu Zhi, known by his posthumous title Xuangong, which elaborated the benevolence and righteousness of the seven books of the Mengzi; and Han Yu of Changli’s Inquiry into the Way, which revived this cultural tradition after eight dynasties. Though these men were not Mengzi, their achievements could nevertheless rank alongside his.
By the Song, true Confucian scholars emerged in succession. Master Zhou was a jade pool and a golden well, one who silently apprehended the substance of the Way. Yet people actually say that he did not derive his learning from a teacher…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
傳焉不觀諸謝方叔曰濂溪傳千載之秘
上祖先天之易也卽此可以知其言矣明
道玉色金聲純粹如顏者也而伊川則績
密撿束焉不觀之朱文公曰孟子才高而
伊川未到伊川之撿束而却難及也卽此
可以驗其說矣窮理盡性一變至道則張
横渠也談兵乃其初年耳浩然之氣其亦
義理之勇乎歷覽無際探窟躡根則邵堯
夫也毘苦乃其工夫耳樓閣之量其亦養
===
盛之致乎楊應之勁挺不屈呂和叔至誠
敏德踐履不同而同得於程氏之教也淵
源有自來矣羅仲素之有德有言李愿中
之自然成法行實不一而一出於養靜之
功也學術有所本矣謝顯道居敬窮理達
於義利之關也矜字一去而頓覺長進何
玩物喪志之有乎張敬夫踐行篤實析乎
理欲之限也仁字一得而春風沂水非湖
海一世之豪乎以文學知名者游定夫也
punctuated: 傳焉。不觀諸謝方叔曰：「濂溪傳千載之秘，上祖先天之易也。」卽此可以知其言矣。明道玉色金聲，純粹如顏者也，而伊川則績密撿束焉。不觀之朱文公曰：「孟子才高，而伊川未到；伊川之撿束，而却難及也。」卽此可以驗其說矣。窮理盡性，一變至道，則張横渠也。談兵乃其初年耳，浩然之氣，其亦義理之勇乎？歷覽無際，探窟躡根，則邵堯夫也。毘苦乃其工夫耳，樓閣之量，其亦養盛之致乎？楊應之勁挺不屈，呂和叔至誠敏德，踐履不同，而同得於程氏之教也，淵源有自來矣。羅仲素之有德有言，李愿中之自然成法，行實不一，而一出於養靜之功也，學術有所本矣。謝顯道居敬窮理，達於義利之關也，矜字一去，而頓覺長進，何玩物喪志之有乎？張敬夫踐行篤實，析乎理欲之限也，仁字一得，而春風沂水，非湖海一世之豪乎？以文學知名者，游定夫也。
translation_en:
…transmission from a teacher. Have they not considered what Xie Fangshu said: “Lianxi transmitted the secrets of a thousand years, tracing his lineage back to the Changes of Prior Heaven”? From this alone one can understand that statement.

Mingdao had the complexion of jade and the resonance of metal, pure and unalloyed like Yan Hui; Yichuan, however, was meticulous [?] and disciplined. Have they not considered what Master Zhu, titled Wengong, said: “Mencius’s talents were lofty, and Yichuan did not reach his level; yet Yichuan’s self-discipline was difficult to equal”? This alone can substantiate the claim.

As for investigating principle to the utmost and fully realizing one’s nature, reaching the Way through a single transformation—that was Zhang Hengqu. His discussions of military affairs belonged only to his early years. Was not his vast, flowing vital energy also the courage born of righteousness and principle? As for surveying without limit, exploring hidden recesses, and tracing things to their roots—that was Shao Yaofu. His painstaking effort [?] was merely the work of cultivation. Was not his capacity, lofty as a storied pavilion, likewise the culmination of abundant cultivation?

Yang Yingzhi was firm and unyielding; Lü Heshu was utterly sincere and diligent in virtue. Their practices differed, but both benefited from the Cheng masters’ teaching: their intellectual lineage had a definite source. Luo Zhongsu possessed both virtue and worthy words; Li Yuanzhong naturally established a standard. Their conduct differed, but both arose from the work of cultivating stillness: their learning had a foundation.

Xie Xiandao maintained reverence and investigated principle, comprehending the crucial distinction between righteousness and profit. Once he cast off self-conceit, he immediately perceived great progress. How could he have dissipated his resolve by toying with things? Zhang Jingfu was earnest and substantial in practice, discerning the boundary between principle and desire. Once he grasped benevolence, he attained the spirit of the spring breeze by the River Yi. Was he not an outstanding man of his age, celebrated far and wide? The one renowned for literary learning was You Dingfu.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
天下豪傑雖老師宿儒咸推先之而清德
重望其皎如日星耶居諫官有聲者朱光
庭也爲學之本主於忠信至於終身由之
而博學強行其堅如金石耶呂祖謙倡道
於婺而心涵千古之秘爲一代之宗師陸
子靜隱居象山而道心人心之講致生徒
之數百胡康侯之傳春秋而明仲之詳說
仁仲之知言皆有體而有用一門之盛何
偉見乎蔡元定之律呂新書而父發之博
===
極群書淵沉之易訓洪範蓋三世而一轍
流派之源其有本乎若夫心窮造化之原
身體天地之道主盟斯文而獨任道統者
則朱元晦之功爲全焉至於曰極曰誠曰
仁曰道曰忠曰恕曰性命曰氣質曰天理
人欲曰陰陽鬼神千載百年習浮踵靡莫
知其說者乃能發無餘蘊而集諸儒之大
成豈非理學之藪而諸儒之凖耶然而學
者果何所取衷乎其在諸儒漢則醇矣而
punctuated: 天下豪傑，雖老師宿儒，咸推先之，而清德重望，其皎如日星耶？居諫官有聲者，朱光庭也。爲學之本，主於忠信，至於終身由之，而博學強行，其堅如金石耶？呂祖謙倡道於婺，而心涵千古之秘，爲一代之宗師。陸子靜隱居象山，而道心人心之講，致生徒之數百。胡康侯之傳《春秋》，而明仲之《詳說》、仁仲之《知言》，皆有體而有用，一門之盛，何偉見乎！蔡元定之《律呂新書》，而父發之博極群書，淵沉之《易訓》《洪範》，蓋三世而一轍，流派之源，其有本乎！若夫心窮造化之原，身體天地之道，主盟斯文而獨任道統者，則朱元晦之功爲全焉。至於曰極、曰誠、曰仁、曰道、曰忠、曰恕、曰性命、曰氣質、曰天理人欲、曰陰陽鬼神，千載百年，習浮踵靡，莫知其說者，乃能發無餘蘊，而集諸儒之大成，豈非理學之藪而諸儒之凖耶？然而學者果何所取衷乎？其在諸儒，漢則醇矣，而
translation_en:
…The outstanding men of the realm, even venerable teachers and seasoned scholars, all acknowledged his precedence. Were not his unsullied virtue and great prestige as radiant as the sun and stars? Zhu Guangting earned renown as a Remonstrance Official. He made loyalty and trustworthiness the foundation of learning and followed them throughout his life. Were not his extensive learning and resolute practice as firm as metal and stone? Lü Zuqian championed the Way in Wu; his mind encompassed the secrets of a thousand ages, and he became a master of his generation. Lu Zijing lived in retirement at Xiangshan, where his lectures on the mind of the Way and the human mind attracted hundreds of students. Hu Kanghou’s commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals, Mingzhong’s Detailed Explanations, and Renzhong’s Understanding Words all possessed both substance and practical application. How splendidly the flourishing of this one family was displayed! Cai Yuanding’s New Book on Pitch Pipes, his father Fa’s comprehensive mastery of the books, and Yuan and Chen’s [?] Teachings on the Changes and Great Plan followed a single course through three generations. Surely this scholarly current had a well-founded source!

As for one whose mind fathomed the source of creation and transformation, who personally embodied the Way of Heaven and Earth, and who presided over this cultural tradition and alone shouldered the transmission of the Way, Zhu Yuanhui’s achievement was complete. Whether the subject was the Ultimate, sincerity, benevolence, the Way, loyalty, reciprocity, human nature and destiny, psychophysical endowment, heavenly principle and human desires, or yin and yang and ghosts and spirits—for hundreds and thousands of years, people had fallen into superficial habits and followed decadent fashions, understanding none of these teachings. Yet he was able to expound them without leaving anything concealed and to bring the achievements of the various Confucian scholars to their fullest synthesis. Was he not a repository of the Learning of Principle and a standard for all Confucian scholars? Yet where, indeed, should students seek an authoritative judgment? Among the Confucian scholars, those of the Han were sound, but…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
未粹有弗取焉唐則直矣而未全有弗取
焉至於有宋則考周子之圖以啓其秘遡
二程之道以行其流約張子之論以一其
趨繹堯夫之言以適其趣至於窮理以致
知反躬以踐實主敬行恕以開其端誠意
正心以歸其極則文公之教實會其全者
也體道之準其有賴乎洪惟我
朝
天啓文明道德一而風俗同禮樂興而人文著
===
名世之儒碩達之才皆志存體道而不移
於流俗學本窮理而不奪於外誘其立言
則可以翼道其制行則足以淑人蘊之而
爲修己之規發之而爲致用之業蓋由氣
運之昌隆故其培之也至厚教化之浹洽
故其陶之也至深培之至厚則生於文明
之
盛世者自藹藹而多吉士陶之至深則成於
菁莪之
punctuated: 未粹，有弗取焉；唐則直矣，而未全，有弗取焉。至於有宋，則考周子之圖以啓其秘，遡二程之道以行其流，約張子之論以一其趨，繹堯夫之言以適其趣。至於窮理以致知，反躬以踐實，主敬行恕以開其端，誠意正心以歸其極，則文公之教實會其全者也。體道之準，其有賴乎！洪惟我朝，天啓文明，道德一而風俗同，禮樂興而人文著。名世之儒、碩達之才，皆志存體道而不移於流俗，學本窮理而不奪於外誘。其立言則可以翼道，其制行則足以淑人。蘊之而爲修己之規，發之而爲致用之業。蓋由氣運之昌隆，故其培之也至厚；教化之浹洽，故其陶之也至深。培之至厚，則生於文明之盛世者，自藹藹而多吉士；陶之至深，則成於菁莪之
translation_en:
…not wholly refined, and some things must be rejected. The scholars of the Tang were upright, yet not complete, and some things must be rejected. Coming to the Song, one examines Master Zhou’s diagram to disclose its mysteries, traces the Way of the two Cheng masters to its source so that its current may flow onward, draws together Master Zhang’s arguments to unify their direction, and unfolds Yaofu’s words to arrive at their purport. As for investigating principle to extend knowledge, examining oneself to put it into practice, making reverence central and practicing reciprocity as the starting point, and making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind as the ultimate goal: the teachings of Duke Wen [Zhu Xi] truly bring all these together in their entirety. Surely here is a standard on which to rely in embodying the Way!

We reverently consider our dynasty: Heaven has inaugurated its cultural brilliance; the Way and virtue are unified, and customs are shared; rites and music flourish, and human culture shines forth. Scholars renowned in their age and men of great learning and understanding all set their aspirations on embodying the Way, unmoved by prevailing vulgar customs. Their learning rests on investigating principle, undistracted by external temptations. The teachings they set forth can uphold the Way, and the conduct they establish suffices to improve others. Held within, this learning provides rules for cultivating themselves; expressed outwardly, it becomes work of practical service.

Because the fortunes of the age flourish, their nurture is exceedingly rich; because moral instruction permeates everywhere, their formation is exceedingly profound. With such rich nurture, those born into this flourishing age of cultural brilliance naturally include an abundance of worthy men. With such profound formation, those brought to maturity through the nurturing influence celebrated in “Luxuriant Mugwort” …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
德化者自濟濟而多眞才名儒之衆信有由
矣是豈偶然之故哉管見如斯惟進而教
之幸甚
第四問
楊正脉
同考試官教諭曹　批〔知行合一所以入道然未　有不先知而後行者此篇發學庸之異同而要之〕
〔至當歸一之論自是學到貫通處〕
考試官學正王　批〔考析精確有功聖門〕
===
考試官教授馮　批〔援據義理亙有發明辨哉〕
易曰乾以易知坤以簡能言天地之道易
簡而已矣又曰易則易知簡則易從言聖
人之道與天地合德者亦易簡而已矣夫
學以求至乎道也天地聖人之道舉不外
乎易簡而學道者顧以多說汨之多岐亂
之可乎哉嗚呼子思中庸之作將以維世
也今之時去子思之時又遠矣學者延不
能深究其意會通其旨膠於舊聞狃於臆
punctuated:
德化者，自濟濟而多眞才，名儒之衆信有由矣。是豈偶然之故哉？管見如斯，惟進而教之，幸甚。
第四問
楊正脉
同考試官教諭曹　批〔知行合一，所以入道；然未　有不先知而後行者。此篇發學庸之異同，而要之〕〔至當歸一之論，自是學到貫通處。〕
考試官學正王　批〔考析精確，有功聖門。〕
考試官教授馮　批〔援據義理，亙有發明，辨哉！〕
易曰：「乾以易知，坤以簡能。」言天地之道，易簡而已矣。又曰：「易則易知，簡則易從。」言聖人之道與天地合德者，亦易簡而已矣。夫學以求至乎道也，天地聖人之道舉不外乎易簡，而學道者顧以多說汨之，多岐亂之，可乎哉？嗚呼！子思中庸之作，將以維世也。今之時，去子思之時又遠矣。學者延不能深究其意，會通其旨，膠於舊聞，狃於臆
translation_en:
…those formed by moral instruction naturally include abundant men of true talent. There is indeed a reason for the multitude of eminent scholars. Could this have come about merely by chance? Such is my limited view. I would be most grateful for further instruction.
Fourth Policy Question
Yang Zhengmai
Associate Examiner Cao, Instructor, comments: 〔The unity of knowledge and action is the means of entering the Way. Yet knowledge must always precede action. This essay brings out the similarities and differences between the Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean, and draws them together〕〔in a perfectly fitting argument that reconciles them as one. This surely shows learning that has reached comprehensive understanding.〕
Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: 〔Precise examination and analysis: a contribution to the school of the Sage.〕
Examiner Feng, Professor, comments: 〔Drawing its evidence from moral principles, it offers illumination throughout [?]. How discerning!〕
The Book of Changes says: “Qian governs through ease; Kun accomplishes through simplicity.” This means that the Way of Heaven and Earth is nothing more than ease and simplicity.
