It also says: “What is easy is easy to understand; what is simple is easy to follow.” This means that the Way of the sages, whose virtue accords with Heaven and Earth, is likewise nothing more than ease and simplicity. Learning seeks to reach the Way. The Way of Heaven, Earth, and the sages nowhere goes beyond ease and simplicity. Can it be acceptable, then, for those who study the Way to obscure it with proliferating explanations and confuse it with diverging paths?
Alas! Zisi composed the Doctrine of the Mean to sustain the world. Our own age is still further removed from the age of Zisi. If scholars still [?] cannot investigate its meaning deeply and comprehend its purport as a whole, but cling to what they have previously heard and remain habituated to conjecture…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
誠而無從善服義之公心則道術將爲天
下裂此任世道之責者所宜致慮也夫學
何足以知之雖然明問所及敢不悉心以
對明問曰中庸之首章爲一篇之體要其
曰戒謹不覩恐懼不聞者所以立其本也
謂涵養用敬之旨學者習聞無容致疑也
曰必慎其獨者繫之大學特誠意之一目
耳甚哉言乎拙心學之綱而俗說之謬欲
人深思自得於引而不發之餘也夫孔子
===
承堯舜精一執中之傳作大學之正經而
授之曾子曾子作十傳以釋經文而其學
傳之子思格物致知乃經文條目之最先
者子思之作中庸顧忍背而遺之哉殆有
精義於其中而不可不熟究也夫天下無
往非道未有出於性之外天下無往非學
未有出於心之外心之所發之爲意是意
也自其人所不及知而言謂之獨自其幾
所不容昧而言謂之知自其意之有所屬
punctuated:
誠，而無從善服義之公心，則道術將爲天下裂。此任世道之責者所宜致慮也。夫學何足以知之？雖然，明問所及，敢不悉心以對？

明問曰：「中庸之首章爲一篇之體要，其曰戒謹不覩、恐懼不聞者，所以立其本也。謂涵養用敬之旨，學者習聞，無容致疑也。曰必慎其獨者，繫之大學，特誠意之一目耳。」甚哉，言乎！拙心學之綱而俗說之謬，欲人深思自得於引而不發之餘也。夫孔子承堯舜精一執中之傳，作大學之正經而授之曾子。曾子作十傳以釋經文，而其學傳之子思。格物致知，乃經文條目之最先者，子思之作中庸，顧忍背而遺之哉？殆有精義於其中，而不可不熟究也。夫天下無往非道，未有出於性之外；天下無往非學，未有出於心之外。心之所發之爲意，是意也，自其人所不及知而言，謂之獨；自其幾所不容昧而言，謂之知；自其意之有所屬
translation_en:
…[the opening character 誠 is doubtful in context] and lack the impartial disposition to follow what is good and submit to what is right, then the Way and its teachings will become fragmented throughout the world. This is something that those responsible for the moral order of the age ought to consider carefully. How could a student such as I know enough to understand it? Nevertheless, concerning the matters raised in your illuminating question, how could I dare not devote my whole mind to answering?

Your illuminating question says: “The opening chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean presents the essential framework of the entire work. Its statements about being watchful and cautious over what one does not see, and fearful and apprehensive over what one does not hear, serve to establish the foundation. Students are familiar with the teaching that these refer to nurturing oneself through reverent attentiveness; there is no room for doubt about this. As for the statement that one must be watchful over oneself when alone, when related to the Great Learning, it is merely one item under making the intentions sincere.” How profound these words are! They bring out [?] the guiding principles of the learning of the mind and the errors of commonplace explanations, seeking to have people reflect deeply and attain understanding for themselves through what is left implicit when the bow is drawn but the arrow is not released.

Confucius inherited from Yao and Shun the transmission of refinement, singleness of purpose, and holding fast to the Mean. He composed the canonical text of the Great Learning and entrusted it to Zengzi. Zengzi composed ten commentaries to explain the canonical text, and his learning was transmitted to Zisi. Investigating things and extending knowledge are the very first items in the canonical text. When Zisi composed the Doctrine of the Mean, could he really have borne to turn his back on them and leave them out? Surely there is a subtle meaning here that must be examined thoroughly.

Now, nowhere in the world is the Way absent, and nothing lies outside human nature; nowhere in the world is learning absent, and nothing lies outside the mind. What issues from the mind constitutes intention. This intention, considered in terms of what other people cannot know, is called being alone; considered in terms of its incipient stirrings, which must not be obscured, it is called knowing; considered in terms of that toward which the intention is directed…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
而言謂之物皆肇於一念之微也由一念
而達之其幾甚微其迹甚著其用甚廣其
變甚緐皆君子格物致知所實用力之地
而爲誠意之全功也非格物致知誠意截
然判而爲三段事也先列格致則誠意有
達觀之妙而不墮於虛專言愼獨則格致
有眞切之功而不涉於泛此聖門知行並
進之學先後一揆者也世之學者不能尋
其端緒泛求而逆施之記誦探索之勤揣
量模擬之工依倣假借之似祗見其過甚
而支離焉耳惡足以語聖人之道哉是故
格物致知之說一也善用之則爲誠意正
心之功不善用之則流而入於俗儒矣不
可不深思而自得之也是說也驟而聽之
若將以爲異也而不知朱子亦嘗言之矣
大學之或問釋格致之說詳矣其用功之
目曰察之念慮之微考之事爲之著求之
文字之中索之講論之際釋誠意章愼獨
punctuated:
而言，謂之物，皆肇於一念之微也。由一念而達之，其幾甚微，其迹甚著，其用甚廣，其變甚緐，皆君子格物致知所實用力之地，而爲誠意之全功也。非格物、致知、誠意截然判而爲三段事也。先列格致，則誠意有達觀之妙而不墮於虛；專言愼獨，則格致有眞切之功而不涉於泛。此聖門知行並進之學，先後一揆者也。世之學者不能尋其端緒，泛求而逆施之，記誦探索之勤，揣量模擬之工，依倣假借之似，祗見其過甚而支離焉耳，惡足以語聖人之道哉！是故格物致知之說一也，善用之則爲誠意正心之功，不善用之則流而入於俗儒矣，不可不深思而自得之也。

是說也，驟而聽之，若將以爲異也，而不知朱子亦嘗言之矣。《大學》之《或問》釋格致之說詳矣，其用功之目曰：「察之念慮之微，考之事爲之著，求之文字之中，索之講論之際。」釋誠意章愼獨
translation_en:
…viewed in this respect, it is called a “thing.” All these originate in the subtle stirring of a single thought. Extending outward from that thought, its incipient impulses are exceedingly subtle, its manifestations exceedingly apparent, its applications exceedingly broad, and its transformations exceedingly numerous. These are all places where the gentleman applies real effort in investigating things and extending knowledge; together they constitute the full work of making the intention sincere. Investigating things, extending knowledge, and making the intention sincere are not sharply divided into three separate undertakings. By listing the investigation of things and extension of knowledge first, the text gives sincerity of intention the subtle benefit of comprehensive understanding, preventing it from lapsing into emptiness. By speaking specifically of vigilance in solitude, it gives the investigation of things and extension of knowledge a genuine and immediate efficacy, preventing them from becoming diffuse. This is the learning of the sages’ school, in which knowledge and action advance together, and earlier and later stages follow a single principle. Scholars of the present age cannot discover its starting point. They seek indiscriminately and apply their efforts in reverse order. Their diligence in memorization, recitation, and searching inquiry; their labor in conjecture and imitation; and the semblance they achieve through copying and borrowing reveal only excess and fragmentation. How could these qualify them to speak of the Way of the sages? Thus, the teaching of investigating things and extending knowledge is one and the same: used well, it becomes the work of making the intention sincere and rectifying the mind; used poorly, it degenerates into the learning of vulgar scholars. One must therefore ponder it deeply and grasp it for oneself.

On first hearing this explanation, one might consider it strange, unaware that Master Zhu also once expressed it. His Questions and Answers on the Great Learning explains the investigation of things and extension of knowledge in detail. Its list of ways to apply effort reads: “Examine it in the subtleties of thoughts and reflections; investigate it in the evident manifestations of affairs and conduct; seek it in writings; search for it in discussion.” In explaining vigilance in solitude in the chapter on making the intention sincere…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
□□曰君子必謹之於此以審其幾焉察
之念慮者非愼獨之功乎審其幾者非格
致之事乎以察之念慮之微冠之於首則
其立言固有序矣學者讀朱子之書而不
能會朱子之意於是爲格致之學者曰一
物不知君子所耻窮年涉獵而靡所底止
要旨學者之獘而豈朱子之說使然哉是
故朱子之說一也善讀之則爲大學中庸
之助不善讀之則泥而反以病經矣不可
===
不深思而自得之也今夫人之所以妙衆
理而宰萬事者心也其未發也不覩不聞
之體鬼神不得而知也故惟敬以存之而
已無俟於言說也其旣發也善惡分焉萬
事出焉苟不隨其所發而遂加夫體察之
功則其見於應用也鮮不謬矣是故愼獨
之功學莫有先焉者也舍愼獨而談格致
豈所謂察之念慮之微乎且大學之傳自
誠意而下皆以好惡貫之夫人之情二之
punctuated:
□□曰：「君子必謹之於此，以審其幾焉。」察之念慮者，非愼獨之功乎？審其幾者，非格致之事乎？以「察之念慮之微」冠之於首，則其立言固有序矣。學者讀朱子之書，而不能會朱子之意。於是爲格致之學者曰：「一物不知，君子所耻。」窮年涉獵，而靡所底止。要旨學者之獘，而豈朱子之說使然哉？是故朱子之說一也，善讀之則爲《大學》《中庸》之助，不善讀之則泥而反以病經矣，不可不深思而自得之也。
今夫人之所以妙衆理而宰萬事者，心也。其未發也，不覩不聞之體，鬼神不得而知也，故惟敬以存之而已，無俟於言說也。其旣發也，善惡分焉，萬事出焉。苟不隨其所發而遂加夫體察之功，則其見於應用也，鮮不謬矣。是故愼獨之功，學莫有先焉者也。舍愼獨而談格致，豈所謂「察之念慮之微」乎？且《大學》之傳，自誠意而下，皆以好惡貫之。夫人之情，二之
translation_en:
…[two illegible characters] says: “The gentleman must exercise care here, so as to discern the incipient stirrings.” Is examining one’s thoughts not the work of vigilance in solitude? Is discerning their incipient stirrings not the task of investigating things and extending knowledge? By placing “examining the subtleties of one’s thoughts” first, he surely established a deliberate order in his exposition. Scholars read Zhu Xi’s books but fail to grasp his meaning. Thus those pursuing the investigation of things and extension of knowledge say: “To leave even one thing unknown is a gentleman’s shame.” They spend whole years ranging through their reading without reaching any resting point. This is, in essence, a failing of scholars [?]; how could Zhu Xi’s teaching have caused it? Thus Zhu Xi’s teaching is one and the same: read well, it aids understanding of the Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean; read poorly, it leads to rigid adherence and, instead, impairs understanding of the classics. One must reflect deeply upon it and attain understanding for oneself.
Now, that by which a person wondrously comprehends the many principles and governs the myriad affairs is the mind. Before it is aroused, its substance, unseen and unheard, cannot be known even by ghosts and spirits. Thus one need only preserve it through reverent attentiveness; there is no need for verbal exposition. Once it is aroused, good and evil become differentiated, and the myriad affairs emerge. If one does not follow its arousal and immediately apply the work of attentive examination, then, when it manifests in practical activity, error will seldom be avoided. Thus, in learning, nothing takes precedence over the work of vigilance in solitude. If one abandons vigilance in solitude and talks of investigating things and extending knowledge, can this be what is meant by “examining the subtleties of one’s thoughts”? Moreover, throughout the commentary on the Great Learning, from making the intentions sincere onward, liking and disliking form the connecting thread. As for human feelings, if one divides them into two…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
則爲好惡四之則爲喜怒哀樂也好惡公
而家國天下得其理喜怒哀樂中其節而
天地萬物順其宜其致一也故曰千聖一
心萬古一道也其聖學易簡之正傳乎然
而闢其說者又將以爲近於禪也夫禪之
說自謂明心見性而委事物於不爲吾之
說慎其獨知而達之於天下正相背也而
何疑哉又有謂誠意而不先之格致則眞
妄錯雜將有認欲以爲理者夫此心之靈
===
皎如日月善惡之萌毫髮莫遁但恐不能
禁止其自欺耳豈患於不知哉故曰莫見
乎隱莫顯乎微使有所不知則不得謂之
莫見莫顯矣小人陰爲不善而陽欲掩之
苟不知善惡之所在何以見君子而欲掩
之哉爲此說者亦異於曾子子思矣夫義
理之精入於毫芒疑似之間誠亦難辨然
必自吾之所知者而體驗擴充之則行著
習察精義入神之域可馴至矣今乃置其
punctuated:
則爲好惡，四之則爲喜怒哀樂也。好惡公，而家國天下得其理；喜怒哀樂中其節，而天地萬物順其宜，其致一也。故曰：「千聖一心，萬古一道也。」其聖學易簡之正傳乎？然而闢其說者，又將以爲近於禪也。夫禪之說，自謂明心見性，而委事物於不爲；吾之說，慎其獨知，而達之於天下，正相背也，而何疑哉？

又有謂誠意而不先之格致，則眞妄錯雜，將有認欲以爲理者。夫此心之靈，皎如日月，善惡之萌，毫髮莫遁，但恐不能禁止其自欺耳，豈患於不知哉？故曰：「莫見乎隱，莫顯乎微。」使有所不知，則不得謂之莫見莫顯矣。小人陰爲不善，而陽欲掩之，苟不知善惡之所在，何以見君子而欲掩之哉？爲此說者，亦異於曾子、子思矣。

夫義理之精，入於毫芒疑似之間，誠亦難辨。然必自吾之所知者而體驗擴充之，則行著習察、精義入神之域，可馴至矣。今乃置其
translation_en:
…then they are liking and disliking; divided into four, they are joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure. When liking and disliking are impartial, the family, state, and all under Heaven attain their proper order; when joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure are expressed in due measure, Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things accord with what is fitting. Their ultimate import is one. Thus it is said: “A thousand sages share one mind; through all ages there is one Way.” Is this not the orthodox transmission of the sages’ learning in its ease and simplicity? Yet those who reject this teaching will also deem it close to Chan Buddhism. Chan teaching claims to illuminate the mind and see one’s nature, yet leaves affairs and things unattended. My teaching calls for vigilance over what one alone knows and extends this throughout all under Heaven. The two are directly opposed: what grounds are there for doubt?

Others say that if making the intentions sincere is not preceded by investigating things and extending knowledge, truth and falsehood will become confused, and some will mistake desire for principle. Yet the luminous awareness of this mind shines as brightly as the sun and moon: not the slightest stirring of good or evil escapes it. The only fear is that one may fail to restrain one’s self-deception; why worry about not knowing? Thus it is said: “Nothing is more visible than what is hidden; nothing is more manifest than what is minute.” If there were something one did not know, it could not be called supremely visible and manifest. The petty man does evil in secret but wishes to conceal it in public. If he did not know where good and evil lay, why would he wish to conceal his conduct upon seeing a gentleman? Those who advance this argument also differ from Zengzi and Zisi.

The subtleties of moral principle enter into the finest distinctions between what is doubtful and what appears plausible, and are indeed difficult to discern. Yet one must begin with what one knows, testing it in personal experience and extending it. Then one may gradually reach the realm in which one understands one’s actions and examines one’s habitual practice, refines one’s grasp of moral principle, and penetrates the spirit-like. Yet now they set aside their…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
所巳知者而未之能行預憂其所難知者
而孜孜研窮之不暇吁亦過計之甚矣然
則忠恕近道達德達道明善誠身與夫致
曲之說尊德性而道問學之說又何若是
之紛紛耶吾固巳言之矣道無時而不存
事由微而至著自一念之微而達之要皆
君子格物致知用力之地也故曰博學之
審問之慎思之明辨之篤行之五者廢其
一非學也蓋以慎獨爲之主則凡所以旁
===
搜博採者皆吾所以遏人欲克天理之方
汗漫求之雖有得焉口耳之贅也朱子曰
自戒懼而約之則爲有以致其中自謹獨
而精之則爲有以致其和約之者虞廷之
所謂一也精之者虞廷之所謂精也精屬
知也曰自謹獨而精之則知行並進之學
一言以蔽之矣會而通之衆說雖殊爲嘗
有二致乎嗟夫子思至此其憂亦甚殷矣
又恐學者茫然而讀之將失其要領也故
punctuated: 所巳知者而未之能行，預憂其所難知者，而孜孜研窮之不暇，吁！亦過計之甚矣。然則忠恕近道、達德達道、明善誠身，與夫致曲之說、尊德性而道問學之說，又何若是之紛紛耶？吾固巳言之矣：道無時而不存，事由微而至著，自一念之微而達之，要皆君子格物致知用力之地也。故曰：「博學之，審問之，慎思之，明辨之，篤行之。」五者廢其一，非學也。蓋以慎獨爲之主，則凡所以旁搜博採者，皆吾所以遏人欲、克天理之方；汗漫求之，雖有得焉，口耳之贅也。朱子曰：「自戒懼而約之，則爲有以致其中；自謹獨而精之，則爲有以致其和。」約之者，虞廷之所謂一也；精之者，虞廷之所謂精也。精屬知也，曰「自謹獨而精之」，則知行並進之學，一言以蔽之矣。會而通之，衆說雖殊，爲嘗有二致乎？嗟夫！子思至此，其憂亦甚殷矣。又恐學者茫然而讀之，將失其要領也，故
translation_en:
…what one already knows, yet fails to put it into practice, worrying beforehand about what is difficult to know and tirelessly investigating it with no time to spare—alas, this is excessive calculation indeed! But why, then, are there so many teachings: that doing one’s utmost and treating others as oneself brings one near the Way; the universally applicable virtues and relationships; understanding goodness and making oneself sincere; developing goodness from particular beginnings; and honoring one’s moral nature while pursuing inquiry and study? I have already explained this: the Way is never absent, and affairs develop from the subtle to the manifest. Beginning with the slightest thought and extending it, all of this is ground on which the gentleman applies himself to investigating things and extending knowledge. Thus it is said: “Study broadly, inquire closely, reflect carefully, discriminate clearly, and practice earnestly.” To abandon any one of these five is not learning. If watchfulness over oneself when alone is made the governing principle, then all our wide-ranging searches and extensive gathering become methods by which we restrain human desires and realize heavenly principle [?]. If we seek without direction, whatever we gain is merely an encumbrance of words heard and repeated.

Master Zhu said: “By drawing things together through vigilance and apprehension, one has the means to bring equilibrium to its fullest realization; by refining one’s understanding through watchfulness over oneself when alone, one has the means to bring harmony to its fullest realization.” Drawing things together is what the court of Shun called being single-minded; refining one’s understanding is what that court called being discerning. Discernment belongs to knowing. The words “refining one’s understanding through watchfulness over oneself when alone” thus sum up in a single statement the learning in which knowledge and action advance together. When these teachings are brought together and understood as interconnected, however different their formulations, have they ever had divergent aims [?]? Alas! At this point Zisi’s concern was indeed profound. He further feared that students, reading in bewilderment, would miss the essential point, and therefore…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
於終篇復自爲巳謹獨之事而推之以至
於無聲無臭之極夫無聲無臭即不覩不
聞之眞體也人心本靜而有動故首章以
不覩不聞爲先工夫巳密而益密故終篇
以無聲無臭爲至曰君子之所不可及者
其惟人之所不見乎則其提掇愼獨之意
益丁寧而懇切矣程子曰有天德便可以
語王道其要只在謹獨周子曰守之貴行
之利廓之配天地豈不易簡豈爲難知不
===
守不行不廓耳蓋皆有得於聖門之宗旨
者彼韓子作原道語誠意而不及格物致
知朱子譏之就使語及格致未必有得於
聖道者又胡足深辨迂踈之見如此不識
執事以爲何如
第五問
張白
同考試官教授梁　批　古今論政惟人存政舉此篇
推原立法之意守法之難末復歸重行法之人眞知
punctuated:
於終篇復自爲巳謹獨之事，而推之以至於無聲無臭之極。夫無聲無臭，即不覩不聞之眞體也。人心本靜而有動，故首章以不覩不聞爲先；工夫巳密而益密，故終篇以無聲無臭爲至。曰：「君子之所不可及者，其惟人之所不見乎！」則其提掇愼獨之意，益丁寧而懇切矣。程子曰：「有天德便可以語王道，其要只在謹獨。」周子曰：「守之貴，行之利，廓之配天地，豈不易簡？豈爲難知？不守、不行、不廓耳。」蓋皆有得於聖門之宗旨者。彼韓子作《原道》，語誠意而不及格物致知，朱子譏之。就使語及格致，未必有得於聖道者，又胡足深辨？迂踈之見如此，不識執事以爲何如？
第五問
張白
同考試官教授梁，批：「古今論政，惟人存政舉。此篇推原立法之意、守法之難，末復歸重行法之人，眞知
translation_en:
…in the final chapter, he returns to the work of learning for oneself and being watchful in solitude [?], extending it to the utmost state of being without sound or smell. Being without sound or smell is precisely the true substance of what is neither seen nor heard. The human mind is originally still, yet has movement; thus the opening chapter gives priority to what is neither seen nor heard. As the work of cultivation becomes ever more exacting, the final chapter takes being without sound or smell as its culmination. It says: “What makes the gentleman beyond others’ reach—is it not precisely what others do not see?” Thus its emphasis on vigilance in solitude becomes still more insistent and earnest. Master Cheng said: “With the virtue of Heaven, one can speak of the Kingly Way. Its essential point lies solely in vigilance in solitude.” Master Zhou said: “To preserve it is noble; to practice it is beneficial; to extend it is to match Heaven and Earth. Is this not easy and simple? How could it be difficult to understand? It is merely that people do not preserve, practice, or extend it.” These masters all grasped something of the essential teaching of the sages. When Master Han composed his Inquiry into the Way, he discussed making the intentions sincere but did not address investigating things and extending knowledge, and Master Zhu criticized him for this. Even had he discussed investigating things and extending knowledge, he might not necessarily have grasped the Way of the sages. Why, then, would the matter merit lengthy argument? Such is my impractical and ill-informed view; I do not know what you, honored sir, think of it.
Fifth Question
Zhang Bai
Associate Examiner Liang, Professor, comments: “In discussions of government, ancient or modern, it is only when the right people are present that government flourishes. This essay traces the intentions behind establishing laws and the difficulties of upholding them, and finally returns to emphasize the people who implement them. It truly understands…”

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
本之論推此以濟時補敝如持左券矣
考試官學正王　批　援古證今likely學可見蓋
不出戶庭而能談當世之務者
考試官教授馮　批　願實可錄
聖王經國之猷法天之制也因地之宜也
盡人之能也是故以觀會通則在天者無
失時以相機宜則在地者無失節以責實
效則在人者無失事無失時而天道順矣
故曰法天之制也無失節而地道利矣故
===
曰因地之宜也無失事而人道官矣故曰
盡人之能也知是而利之不可興害之不
可去弊之不可釐者否也執事發策以屯
田水利鹽法馬政下詢承學蓋有望於足
國安邊之猷也顧愚何足以知之雖然竊
有聞矣請援古執今以對夫屯田之法昉
於漢充國田金城而羌戎不敢西侵孟德
田許下而吳人不敢南犯子儀田河中而
歲收羨餘之積師德田豐州而國享富饒
punctuated:
本之論，推此以濟時補敝，如持左券矣。
考試官學正王　批：援古證今，likely學可見，蓋不出戶庭而能談當世之務者。
考試官教授馮　批：願實可錄。
聖王經國之猷，法天之制也，因地之宜也，盡人之能也。是故以觀會通，則在天者無失時；以相機宜，則在地者無失節；以責實效，則在人者無失事。無失時而天道順矣，故曰法天之制也；無失節而地道利矣，故曰因地之宜也；無失事而人道官矣，故曰盡人之能也。知是而利之不可興、害之不可去、弊之不可釐者，否也。執事發策，以屯田、水利、鹽法、馬政下詢承學，蓋有望於足國安邊之猷也。顧愚何足以知之？雖然，竊有聞矣，請援古執今以對。夫屯田之法，昉於漢。充國田金城，而羌戎不敢西侵；孟德田許下，而吳人不敢南犯；子儀田河中，而歲收羨餘之積；師德田豐州，而國享富饒
translation_en:
…an argument addressing the fundamentals. Applying this to meet the needs of the times and remedy abuses would make success as certain as holding the creditor’s half of a contract.
Examiner Wang, an Instructor, comments: “He draws on antiquity to substantiate the present; his learning is evident [the transcription here contains ‘likely’, ?]. Here is someone able to discuss the affairs of the age without leaving his own courtyard.”
Examiner Feng, a Professor, comments: “Sincere and substantial [?]; worthy of selection.”
The sage kings’ plans for governing the state followed Heaven’s patterns, accommodated the advantages of the earth, and fully employed human abilities. Thus, in surveying how things converge and interconnect, they missed no proper timing in matters pertaining to Heaven; in assessing circumstances and appropriate measures, they missed no proper measure in matters pertaining to the earth; and in demanding practical results, they neglected no undertaking in matters pertaining to human beings. With no error in timing, Heaven’s way proceeds smoothly: hence, ‘following Heaven’s patterns.’ With no error in appropriate measures, the earth’s way brings benefit: hence, ‘accommodating the advantages of the earth.’ With no undertaking neglected, the human way is duly ordered through offices [?]: hence, ‘fully employing human abilities.’ Could one understand this yet remain unable to promote benefits, eliminate harms, or rectify abuses? No.
You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question on agricultural colonies, water management, the salt administration, and horse administration, condescending to consult us students. Surely you hope for plans to enrich the state and secure the frontiers. Yet how could someone as ignorant as I adequately understand these matters? Nevertheless, I have privately heard something of them. Allow me to draw on antiquity and consider the present in replying.
The system of agricultural colonies began under the Han. Chongguo established cultivation at Jincheng, and the Qiang tribes dared not invade from the west; Mengde established cultivation around Xu, and the men of Wu dared not attack from the south; Ziyi established cultivation in Hezhong, and surplus stores accumulated from the annual harvests; Shide established cultivation in Fengzhou, and the state enjoyed abundant wealth …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
之利行之古者未嘗不利也今則齊青魯
兗之地有衛屯有所屯額非不存也而版
籍寄於簿書田畝隱於豪右耕耨廢於貧
窶草萊蕪於逃亡則屯之未盡闢也爲今
之計而思以闢之則冊籍不可不稽也經
界不可不正也招徠不可不力也優恤不
可不至也而又多方以勸相之緩征以勞
來之如墾於一歲者謂之菑田吾無賦焉
墾於二歲者謂之畬田吾稍賦焉墾於九
===
歲者謂之南田吾成賦焉行之十年之久
則人皆樂於輕賦勇於力耕而地利可興
屯政可舉軍儲可實矣水利之興詳於周
叔敖引芍陂而楚受其惠文翁引腴口而
蜀享其利召信臣引南陽而紛爭以息鄭
當時引渭渠而漕運以通行之古者未嘗
不利也今則汶泗徂泰之泉有上源有下
源導非不勤也而丁夫占於私役錢穀侵
於積胥疏濬襲於彌文淤塞逸於顯罰則
punctuated:
之利。行之古者，未嘗不利也。今則齊青魯兗之地，有衛屯，有所屯，額非不存也。而版籍寄於簿書，田畝隱於豪右，耕耨廢於貧窶，草萊蕪於逃亡，則屯之未盡闢也。爲今之計，而思以闢之，則冊籍不可不稽也，經界不可不正也，招徠不可不力也，優恤不可不至也。而又多方以勸相之，緩征以勞來之。如墾於一歲者，謂之菑田，吾無賦焉；墾於二歲者，謂之畬田，吾稍賦焉；墾於九歲者，謂之南田，吾成賦焉。行之十年之久，則人皆樂於輕賦，勇於力耕，而地利可興，屯政可舉，軍儲可實矣。
水利之興，詳於周。叔敖引芍陂，而楚受其惠；文翁引腴口，而蜀享其利；召信臣引南陽，而紛爭以息；鄭當時引渭渠，而漕運以通。行之古者，未嘗不利也。今則汶泗徂泰之泉，有上源，有下源，導非不勤也。而丁夫占於私役，錢穀侵於積胥，疏濬襲於彌文，淤塞逸於顯罰，則
translation_en:
…the benefits of abundance. When implemented in antiquity, these measures invariably proved beneficial. Today, in the lands of Qi, Qing, Lu, and Yan, there are agricultural colonies belonging to guards and battalions, and their prescribed quotas remain in place. Yet their registers exist merely as entries in documents; their fields are concealed by powerful local families; cultivation falls into neglect through poverty; and land becomes overgrown with weeds when its cultivators flee. Thus the colony lands have not been fully brought under cultivation. If we wish to reclaim them under present conditions, we must audit the registers, rectify field boundaries, vigorously recruit settlers, and provide generous relief and protection. We must also encourage and assist them by every means, and grant tax deferments to reward and attract them. Land in its first year of reclamation is called zi land: I would levy no tax on it. Land in its second year is called yu land: I would levy a modest tax on it. Land in its ninth year is called nan land [?]: I would levy the full tax on it. If this were practiced for ten years, everyone would delight in light taxation and apply themselves eagerly to cultivation. The productive capacity of the land could then be developed, the administration of agricultural colonies put into effect, and military granaries filled.
The development of water management was elaborated under the Zhou. Shuao diverted water at Shaopi, and Chu received its benefits; Wen Weng diverted water at Yukou [?], and Shu enjoyed its advantages; Shao Xinchen diverted water in Nanyang, and disputes subsided; Zheng Dangshi diverted water into the Wei Canal, and grain transport was opened up. When implemented in antiquity, these measures invariably proved beneficial. Today, among the springs of Wen, Si, Cu, and Tai, there are upper sources and lower sources, and efforts to channel them have certainly been diligent. Yet laborers are appropriated for private service; money and grain are embezzled by entrenched clerks; dredging follows increasingly empty formalities [?]; and those responsible for silting escape public punishment. Thus…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
泉之未盡濬也而思以疏之則徒庸不可
不清也備慮不可不時也坎流不可不導
也山源不可不濬也而又酌時以啓閉之
�京法以懲勸之如淤於一日者加以輕典
吾無貸焉淤於一旬者加以中典吾無貸
焉淤於一月者加以重典吾無貸焉行之
三月之後則人皆懼於必罰奮於立功而
泉源可疏水勢可通運道可濟矣禹貢青
州貢鹽而鹽用始興周官鹽人掌鹽而鹽
===
用始重至管仲爲鹽筴之論而鹽榷之法
起矣是故蜀鹽産於井雍鹽産於池齊鹽
産於土淮鹽産於海隨其地之所出以責
其課之所入鹽法之良所以通商利息民
肩以實邊餉者誠無庸議矣但今中之於
窮邊也則有加增之額舉之於近地也則
有留難之弊給之於始也既有後時之虞
行之於終也又多私販之阻如之何商人
之不避且去也爲今之計而思以招之則
punctuated:
泉之未盡濬也，而思以疏之，則徒庸不可不清也，備慮不可不時也，坎流不可不導也，山源不可不濬也。而又酌時以啓閉之，�京法以懲勸之。如淤於一日者，加以輕典，吾無貸焉；淤於一旬者，加以中典，吾無貸焉；淤於一月者，加以重典，吾無貸焉。行之三月之後，則人皆懼於必罰，奮於立功，而泉源可疏，水勢可通，運道可濟矣。
《禹貢》青州貢鹽，而鹽用始興；《周官》鹽人掌鹽，而鹽用始重。至管仲爲鹽筴之論，而鹽榷之法起矣。是故蜀鹽産於井，雍鹽産於池，齊鹽産於土，淮鹽産於海，隨其地之所出，以責其課之所入。鹽法之良，所以通商利、息民肩，以實邊餉者，誠無庸議矣。但今中之於窮邊也，則有加增之額；舉之於近地也，則有留難之弊；給之於始也，既有後時之虞；行之於終也，又多私販之阻。如之何商人之不避且去也？爲今之計，而思以招之，則
translation_en:
…the springs have not been fully dredged. If we wish to clear them, the labor force must be properly ordered, preparations must be timely, flows through hollows must be channeled [?], and mountain sources must be dredged. Moreover, the waterways must be opened and closed at appropriate times, and the law applied to punish and encourage [?]. Where silting persists for one day, impose a light penalty: I shall grant no exemption. Where it persists for ten days, impose a moderate penalty: I shall grant no exemption. Where it persists for one month, impose a heavy penalty: I shall grant no exemption. After these measures have been practiced for three months, everyone will fear the certainty of punishment and strive to achieve results. The springs can then be cleared, the waters can flow freely, and the transport route can function.
In the Tribute of Yu, Qingzhou presented salt as tribute, and the use of salt began to flourish. In the Offices of Zhou, the Salt Officers administered salt, and its use began to acquire importance. When Guan Zhong expounded his proposals for salt policy, the system of the salt monopoly arose. Thus, salt in Shu comes from wells; salt in Yong, from pools; salt in Qi, from earth; and salt in Huai, from the sea. The revenue required from each region corresponds to what it produces. The merits of the salt system—as a means of facilitating commercial profits, easing the burdens on the people’s shoulders, and replenishing frontier military supplies—truly need no discussion. Yet nowadays, when merchants contract to supply grain at the distant frontier in exchange for salt rights, additional quotas are imposed; when this is undertaken nearer at hand, there are abuses involving obstruction and delay. At the initial stage of issuance, there is already the danger of tardiness; at the final stage of distribution, illicit sellers create further obstacles. How could merchants fail to avoid this trade and withdraw? In devising measures for the present, if we wish to attract them, then…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
鹺徒不可不禁也竈丁不可不釐也餘鹽
不可不通也常額不可不率也而又革宿
弊以召致之遺厚利以鼓舞之商人之不
藏市者否也周制校人掌王六馬庾人掌
十二閑馬之牧於官者也王畿千里馬萬
乘侯國百里馬千乘馬之牧於民者也至
魯僖有駉篇之頌而畜馬之盛著矣是故
戎馬養於官孳馬養於民與馬養於□□
馬養於農隨其民之所便以足其兵之所
===
需馬政之善所以順民情達治體以儲武
備者固無以加矣但令聯之於群長也則
有餽歛之巧屬之於馬吏也則有誅求之
煩躬解之於京也則有横索之費代俵之
於人也則有包攬之苦如之何馬户之不
窮且逃也爲今之計而思以綏之則雜役
不可不貸也科歛不可不革也常餽不可
不抑也攬索不可不懲也而又昇積徒以
安輯之易輕齎以寬恤之馬户之不寧土
punctuated:
鹺徒不可不禁也，竈丁不可不釐也，餘鹽不可不通也，常額不可不率也。而又革宿弊以召致之，遺厚利以鼓舞之，商人之不藏市者否也。

周制，校人掌王六馬，庾人掌十二閑，馬之牧於官者也；王畿千里，馬萬乘，侯國百里，馬千乘，馬之牧於民者也。至魯僖，有《駉》篇之頌，而畜馬之盛著矣。是故戎馬養於官，孳馬養於民，與馬養於□□，馬養於農，隨其民之所便，以足其兵之所需。馬政之善，所以順民情、達治體以儲武備者，固無以加矣。但令聯之於群長也，則有餽歛之巧；屬之於馬吏也，則有誅求之煩；躬解之於京也，則有横索之費；代俵之於人也，則有包攬之苦。如之何馬户之不窮且逃也？爲今之計，而思以綏之，則雜役不可不貸也，科歛不可不革也，常餽不可不抑也，攬索不可不懲也。而又昇積徒以安輯之，易輕齎以寬恤之，馬户之不寧土
translation_en:
…Salt smugglers must be suppressed, salt-making workers properly regulated, surplus salt allowed to circulate, and regular quotas observed. Furthermore, longstanding abuses must be eliminated to attract merchants, and generous profits left to them as an incentive. There would then be no merchants who failed to keep stocks in the markets.

Under the institutions of Zhou, the Director of the Stud managed the king’s six categories of horses, and the Stablemaster managed the twelve stables: these were horses raised by the government. The royal domain, a thousand li square, supplied horses for ten thousand chariots; a feudal state, a hundred li square, supplied horses for a thousand chariots: these were horses raised by the people. By the time of Duke Xi of Lu, the hymn “Stately Horses” celebrated them, making the flourishing of horse breeding manifest. Thus, warhorses were raised by the government, breeding horses by the people, carriage horses [?] by □□, and horses by farmers. Arrangements suited the circumstances of the people and thereby met the needs of the army. Such excellent horse administration accommodated popular needs, accorded with the principles of governance, and maintained military preparedness; indeed, nothing could surpass it. Yet when horse-rearing households are organized under herd headmen, there are crafty demands for gifts and levies; when placed under horse officials, they suffer vexatious exactions; when they personally deliver horses to the capital, they incur the expense of arbitrary demands; and when others undertake delivery and allocation on their behalf, they suffer at the hands of monopolistic intermediaries. How could horse-rearing households avoid impoverishment and flight? If we now seek a plan to give them security, miscellaneous labor services must be remitted, levies abolished, customary gifts curtailed, and extortion by intermediaries punished. Furthermore, measures described as 昇積徒 [?] should be taken to settle them peacefully, and substitution with readily transportable payments should ease their burdens. That horse-rearing households should fail to live contentedly on their land…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
者否也夫田也水也鹽也馬也皆天地自
然之利而國用以需者也而屯焉而利焉
而法焉而政焉皆人謀已然之能而國需
以裕者也屯田而田無不闢水利而利無
不盡鹽法而懲其不法馬政而去其害政
則天地無遺利人謀無遺能又今之裕
國之良圖而濟時之上務也雖然有要焉變
而通之存乎法神而明之存乎人故屯田
一也得其人如充國如子儀則理矣不得
===
其人如李悝則弊矣水利一也得人如叔
敖如信臣則興矣不得其人如白圭則僨
矣稅鹽有劉晏轉鹽有李沆則鹽法何患
於不行否則爲弘羊之專利而國不勝其
害矣群牧有萬歲閑廄有毛仲則馬政何
慮於不舉否則爲安石之保甲而民秪受
其擾矣故曰其人存則其政舉故曰有治
人無治法敢以是說終焉惟執事教之
punctuated: 者否也。夫田也，水也，鹽也，馬也，皆天地自然之利，而國用以需者也。而屯焉，而利焉，而法焉，而政焉，皆人謀已然之能，而國需以裕者也。屯田而田無不闢，水利而利無不盡，鹽法而懲其不法，馬政而去其害政，則天地無遺利，人謀無遺能，又今之裕國之良圖，而濟時之上務也。雖然，有要焉：變而通之存乎法，神而明之存乎人。故屯田一也，得其人如充國、如子儀，則理矣；不得其人如李悝，則弊矣。水利一也，得人如叔敖、如信臣，則興矣；不得其人如白圭，則僨矣。稅鹽有劉晏，轉鹽有李沆，則鹽法何患於不行？否則爲弘羊之專利，而國不勝其害矣。群牧有萬歲，閑廄有毛仲，則馬政何慮於不舉？否則爲安石之保甲，而民秪受其擾矣。故曰：「其人存，則其政舉。」故曰：「有治人，無治法。」敢以是說終焉，惟執事教之。
translation_en:
…there would be none who failed to settle contentedly on their land. Fields, water, salt, and horses are all natural benefits of Heaven and Earth upon which the state's expenditure depends. Establishing agricultural colonies, developing water resources, regulating salt, and administering horses all draw upon the proven capacities of human planning to provide abundantly for the state's needs. If agricultural colonies leave no land uncultivated, water management leaves no benefit unrealized, salt regulations punish unlawful practices, and horse administration removes whatever impairs its operation, then none of the benefits of Heaven and Earth will be neglected, and none of the capacities of human planning left unused. These, too, are sound plans for enriching the state today and the foremost tasks for meeting the needs of the times.

Nevertheless, there is an essential point: adapting and making things work depends upon regulations; discerning their subtleties and bringing them to light depends upon people. Agricultural colonies are one and the same institution: with the right men, such as Chongguo and Ziyi, they are well managed; with unsuitable men, such as Li Kui, abuses arise. Water management is one and the same undertaking: with men such as Shuao and Xinchen, it flourishes; with unsuitable men such as Bai Gui, it fails. With Liu Yan overseeing salt taxation and Li Hang overseeing salt transport, why fear that salt regulations will not be implemented? Otherwise, they become Hongyang's monopolization of profits, and the state cannot bear the resulting harm. With Wansui overseeing the herds and Maozhong overseeing the stables, why worry that horse administration will not be carried out? Otherwise, it becomes Anshi's baojia system of household organization, and the people suffer only its harassment. Thus it is said: “When the right men are present, their policies are carried out.” And thus it is said: “There are men who bring about good government, but no laws that do so of themselves.” I venture to conclude with this argument and respectfully await your instruction.

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
山東文獻之盛望於天下而
三載鄉薦
制也是秋棘闈竣事諸司遵
制錄文獻以
聞〔聘〕灑與觀成之後乃復申言
于多士大取士非文之求惟
===
君子之望孔子曰文莫吾猶
人也得見君子斯可矣爾多
士挾藝陳文漱六籍飫百家
斌斌焉稱在茲矣魯無君子
斯焉取斯孔門能言如予多
識如賜稱文學如游夏而皆
環視宮墻未能入室至於賢
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

山東文獻之盛，望於天下，而三載鄉薦，制也。是秋棘闈竣事，諸司遵制錄文獻以聞〔聘〕。灑與觀成之後，乃復申言于多士：大取士，非文之求，惟君子之望。孔子曰：「文莫吾猶人也。」「得見君子，斯可矣。」爾多士挾藝陳文，漱六籍，飫百家，斌斌焉稱在茲矣。「魯無君子，斯焉取斯？」孔門能言如予，多識如賜，稱文學如游夏，而皆環視宮墻，未能入室。至於賢
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

Shandong’s flourishing literary culture and learned worthies enjoy renown throughout the realm; recommending men from the province every three years is prescribed by imperial regulation. This autumn, when proceedings in the examination compound were completed, the various offices complied with the regulations by compiling a record of its writings and worthies for submission to the throne.〔Annotation: “engage” [?].〕After taking part in witnessing this accomplishment, Sa [?] once more addressed the assembled scholars: In selecting scholars, we seek not merely literary accomplishment, but men of exemplary character.

Confucius said, “In literary accomplishment, perhaps I am the equal of others,” and, “If I could meet an exemplary man, that would suffice.” You assembled scholars bring your skills and present your compositions, steeping yourselves in the Six Classics and feasting upon the hundred schools. Here indeed you merit praise for your cultivated accomplishments. “If there were no exemplary men in Lu, where could this man have acquired such qualities?” Among Confucius’s disciples were those as eloquent as Yu, as widely informed as Ci, and as renowned for literary learning as You and Xia; yet all merely looked about the palace walls and had not entered the inner chamber. As for the worthy …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
回與點然雍說開於數子獨
拳拳焉多士居聖誕之鄉習
孔庭之訓其於躬行君子不
知有得焉否也而山川之鍾
聖賢之緒蓋往往徵於文矣
是故執物而端屹然如泰山
之鎮涵虛而邃淵然如滄海
===
之瀾奔湃而流駛然如源
之突若其雍和古雅如齊韶
魯典追塵蹤迹如舜井堯墟
感激觸發如悽麟歌鳳三遷
而觀俎豆之章一變而覩先
王之道文斯盛焉豈所謂隱
居以求行義以達素位以自
punctuated: 回、與點、然雍、說開，於數子獨拳拳焉。多士居聖誕之鄉，習孔庭之訓，其於躬行君子，不知有得焉否也？而山川之鍾、聖賢之緒，蓋往往徵於文矣。是故執物而端，屹然如泰山之鎮；涵虛而邃，淵然如滄海之瀾；奔湃而流，駛然如源之突。若其雍和古雅，如齊韶魯典；追塵蹤迹，如舜井堯墟；感激觸發，如悽麟歌鳳。三遷而觀俎豆之章，一變而覩先王之道，文斯盛焉。豈所謂隱居以求，行義以達，素位以自
translation_en:
…Hui, approved of Dian, endorsed Yong, and delighted in Kai: toward these few disciples he showed particular solicitude. You candidates dwell in the birthplace of the Sage and study the teachings transmitted in Confucius’s courtyard. I wonder whether you have attained anything in personally practicing the conduct of a gentleman. Yet the concentrated influences of mountains and rivers, and the legacy of sages and worthies, frequently find expression in literary composition.

Thus, in grasping things with uprightness [?], your writing stands lofty, like the anchoring mass of Mount Tai; in embracing emptiness and profundity, it is deep like the billows of the vast sea; in its surging flow, it speeds like water bursting from a spring. In its harmony and antique elegance, it resembles the Shao music of Qi and the canonical traditions of Lu; in following the traces of the past, it resembles Shun’s well and Yao’s ancient dwelling site; in its stirring emotions, it resembles the lament for the qilin and the song of the phoenix. Through three moves, one comes to observe the ceremonial ordering of sacrificial vessels; through a single transformation, one beholds the Way of the former kings. Here literary cultivation flourishes! Could this be what is meant by dwelling in seclusion to pursue one’s aspirations, practicing righteousness to attain the Way, and abiding in one’s station to find …

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
得求爲君子者乎言行相顧
夫子特贊其慥慥至謂丘未
能一要之孝弟忠信修於詞
乎昆弟友篤於行夫是之謂
立言立德夫是之謂君子爾
多士稱孝稱悌行將寄民社
宜獻攄忠持君子之道以筮
===
焉裕如也昔漢興欲定禮樂
徵魯兩生不行轅固謂公孫
子曰務正學以言毋曲學以
阿世夫兩生非有尊國之文
濟世之略而正誼明道不愧
於魯之多賢公孫稱漢文儒
躋位侯相後世齊魯之士諱
punctuated:
得，求爲君子者乎？言行相顧，夫子特贊其慥慥，至謂「丘未能一」。要之，孝弟忠信，修於詞乎昆弟，友篤於行，夫是之謂立言立德，夫是之謂君子。爾多士稱孝稱悌，行將寄民社，宜獻攄忠，持君子之道以筮焉，裕如也。
昔漢興，欲定禮樂，徵魯兩生，不行。轅固謂公孫子曰：「務正學以言，毋曲學以阿世。」夫兩生非有尊國之文、濟世之略，而正誼明道，不愧於魯之多賢。公孫稱漢文儒，躋位侯相，後世齊魯之士諱
translation_en:
…to find fulfillment, seeking to become a gentleman? Words and deeds must accord with one another. The Master especially praised such earnest steadfastness, even saying, “I, Qiu, have not been able to achieve even one of these.” In essence, filial devotion, fraternal respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness are to be cultivated in words and among brothers, with friendship made steadfast in conduct [?]. This is what is meant by establishing enduring words and virtue; this is what is meant by being a gentleman. You assembled scholars, commended for filial devotion and fraternal respect, will soon be entrusted with the people and the altars of the soil. You should offer your service and give full expression to your loyalty. Upholding the gentleman’s Way as you enter official service, you will have ample capacity for your duties.
Formerly, when the Han dynasty arose and sought to establish rites and music, it summoned two scholars from Lu, but they declined to go. Yuan Gu told Master Gongsun: “Strive to speak on the basis of correct learning; do not distort learning to curry favor with the age.” Those two scholars did not possess literary accomplishments that might bring honor to the state or strategies for delivering the world from its troubles; yet they upheld righteousness and elucidated the Way, proving worthy of Lu’s many worthies. Gongsun was celebrated as a learned scholar of the Han and rose to become a marquis and Chancellor. Scholars of Qi and Lu in later generations were ashamed to…

title: 嘉靖二十八年山東鄉試錄
text:
爲文云乎哉孔門之選自三
千而七十而十哲庶幾者回
一人顏何人哉喻之則是多
上學宗孔顏進踐齊脩修君
子之業以馴聖賢之途以毋
貽山川羞則茲選也豈惟鄉
邦之光而凡乔觀文獻之錄
===
者彰且傳矣多士朂哉
湖廣武昌府興國州儒學學
正王三聘謹序
punctuated:
爲文云乎哉？孔門之選，自三千而七十，而十哲，庶幾者回一人。顏何人哉？喻之則是。多上學宗孔顏，進踐齊脩，修君子之業，以馴聖賢之途，以毋貽山川羞。則茲選也，豈惟鄉邦之光，而凡乔觀文獻之錄者，彰且傳矣。多士朂哉！
湖廣武昌府興國州儒學學正王三聘謹序。
translation_en:
…can it be merely a matter of literary composition? Among those selected from Confucius’s school, the number narrowed from three thousand to seventy, and then to the ten outstanding disciples; only Hui came close to the ideal. What sort of man was Yan Hui? Understand him, and this is the way [?]. You scholars [?] should take Confucius and Yan Hui as your exemplars in learning, advance in practice and cultivate yourselves together, pursuing the work of the gentleman so as gradually to enter the path of sages and worthies and bring no shame upon your native mountains and rivers. Then this selection will bring glory not only to our province: through all who consult this record of its cultural worthies [?], that glory will be made manifest and handed down. Scholars, exert yourselves!
Preface respectfully written by Wang Sanpin, School Instructor of the Confucian School of Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang.
